For example, if your integration copies a URL from another system into a Tape record, plan for URLs above the length limit. Log the error, alert the user who set up the integration, or take another action.
Errors handle 429 and other error responses. Pagination load collections in fewer requests. Webhook react to changes instead of polling. Personal access tokens create and limit a token.

General behavior Send only the properties you want to change. A field in fields with a field_id updates that existing field. A field without field_id creates a new field. Tape adds new fields after the existing ones, in the order of the array. To delete a field, add it to fields_to_delete with its field_id. This also deletes its values in every record. Entries copied from the app's fields property work too. Fields that are in neither array stay unchanged. To delete options of a category or status field, send options_to_delete in the config.settings of that field. See Category and Status. Want to make sure a request never deletes anything? Set reject_deletions to true. Requirements: apps:edit, and Full access to the app. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key. Errors With reject_deletions=true, a request that deletes a field (fields_to_delete) or an option (options_to_delete) returns 400 with deletions_rejected. Tape applies nothing from that request, not even the other changes in the body: { "status_code": 400, "endpoint": "/v1/app/1", "error_code": "deletions_rejected", "error_message": "This request asks for something to be deleted ('fields_to_delete' names 1 field(s)), and it was sent with 'reject_deletions=true'. Nothing was applied — not the deletions, and not the rest of the body. Remove the deletion from the request, or send it without 'reject_deletions'." } Query parameters reject_deletionsboolean Reject the request with 400 (deletions_rejected) if it deletes a field (fields_to_delete) or an option (options_to_delete). Nothing is applied then (default: false). Use this endpoint to list the runs you may see, newest first. POST/v1/automation-runapi.tapeapp.com

Each entry in automation_runs has these fields. So does the automation_run you get when you retrieve a single run. idstring ID of the run. A 64-bit integer, returned as a string so that every language can handle it safely. Example value "9001" automation_idinteger The automation this run executed. Example value 88 automation_namestring Name of the automation. Example value "Notify on new lead" automation_revision_idstring The revision of the automation this run executed. A 64-bit integer, returned as a string. Example value "3" app_idinteger The app the automation belongs to. Example value 42 app_namestring Name of that app. Example value "Leads" workspace_idinteger The workspace the app belongs to. Example value 7 statusstring See Statuses. Example value "completed" typestring Execution kind of the run. One of regular, manual, simulation. Example value "regular" created_atstring When the run was created (YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss), in your timezone. Example value "2024-01-18 08:12:04" created_at_utcstring Same instant as created_at, in UTC. Example value "2024-01-18 07:12:04" filtering_atstring | null When the filtering of the run was scheduled (enqueued), in your timezone. null before then. Example value "2024-01-18 08:12:04" filtering_at_utcstring | null Same instant as filtering_at, in UTC. Example value "2024-01-18 07:12:04" started_atstring | null When the run started executing (entered running), in your timezone. null before then. Example value "2024-01-18 08:12:05" started_at_utcstring | null Same instant as started_at, in UTC. Example value "2024-01-18 07:12:05" completed_atstring | null When the run finished (reached a final status), in your timezone. null while the run is pending or running. Example value "2024-01-18 08:12:09" completed_at_utcstring | null Same instant as completed_at, in UTC. Example value "2024-01-18 07:12:09" execution_duration_msinteger | null How long the run executed, in milliseconds. null until the run completes. Example value 4000 waiting_duration_msinteger | null How long the run waited (scheduled) before it started executing, in milliseconds. null until the run starts. Example value 1000 num_consumed_actionsinteger Number of action credits this run consumed. Example value 2 failure_reasonstring | null Why the run failed, if it did. One of filters_setup_failed, filters_failed, actions_setup_failed, actions_failed, actions_timeout, actions_resource_limit_exceeded, exit_on_purpose. null for any run that has not failed. Example value null error_messagestring | null Readable error detail for a failed run. null otherwise. Example value null triggered_on_record_idinteger | null The record this run executed on. null if no record triggered the run. Example value 5001 triggered_on_record_revision_idinteger | null The revision of that record. null if no record triggered the run. Example value 4 triggered_by_automation_idinteger | null The automation that started this run, if another automation called it. null otherwise. Example value null Timestamps use the Tape API datetime format YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss, with no T separator, no Z suffix and no milliseconds. Each plain field is in your timezone, and its _utc twin carries the same instant in UTC. Use the plain field for display and the _utc field for comparing, sorting and storing.

pending The run is scheduled and has not started executing yet. running The run is executing. completed The run finished successfully. failed The run finished with an error. cancelled The run was cancelled before it could finish.

Use created_at_from and created_at_to to list only runs whose created_at falls within a window. Both bounds are inclusive, and you can send either one on its own. Both use the format of created_at and are read in your timezone, so you can send a value from a response back as a bound. Request curl -X POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation-run \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ --data '{ "created_at_from": "2024-01-18 00:00:00", "created_at_to": "2024-01-18 23:59:59" }' Computing the bounds yourself? Use created_at_from_utc and created_at_to_utc instead. They take the same format, read as UTC, and pair with the created_at_utc of a run. A wall-clock time in your timezone is ambiguous when daylight saving time ends. If you send both versions of a bound, the _utc version wins. created_at_from never reaches back beyond the 30 days Tape keeps runs. An older value counts as the start of that window, so you can safely send an open lower bound. created_at_to has no such limit. The lower bound must be at or before the upper bound. Otherwise the request returns 400.

Results are paginated with a cursor. To get the next page, send the cursor from the previous response on its own. You can add limit: Request curl -X POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation-run \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ --data '{ "cursor": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..." }' The cursor carries the filters of the first page, so don't send them again. A request with a cursor and any of app_ids, automation_ids, workspace_ids, status, created_at_from, created_at_to, created_at_from_utc or created_at_to_utc returns 400. Runs come newest first, in descending order of run ID. When cursor is null, you have reached the end of the list. Why does the number of runs differ from total? Tape counts total once, when you request the first page, and keeps it for the rest of the walk. Automations keep running and old runs leave the 30-day window while you page through, so the runs you receive may differ slightly from total. How long are runs kept? Only runs from the last 30 days are available. Older runs can't be listed or retrieved. Tape doesn't return runs of deleted automations.

A run is a sequence of steps: the trigger that started it, the filter that decided whether to go on, and one entry per executed action. This is the same view of a run as under Automations → Runs in Tape and in its export (Export runs), not the raw internal event stream. Missing the step of an action? A completed run does not guarantee a success step for every top-level action. Control-flow containers (conditional, for_loop) log only their nested actions, and a deactivated action (deactivate: true) logs no entry, not even a skipped one. Some actions finish without a step, for example a skipped authenticated_http_call, collected_records_collect_referenced_records, or a referenced_records_update on a record without related records in its app. Match on the action_id you expect: a missing step doesn't prove that the run failed. Don't see all steps of a run yet? The trigger and filter steps are there from the start. Tape buffers the action steps, so they arrive after the run reaches its final status. When you poll, wait for the step of your action_id, not for logs.length > 0. idstring Stable ID of the step within its run. A durable handle, not a position. See below. Example value "9042-action-a1b2c3-1" typestring trigger, filter, action or exception. Example value "action" statusstring Outcome of the step: in_progress, success, failure, skipped or cancelled. Example value "success" labelstring Readable description of the step, as in the run log in Tape, for example "When a record is created triggered by Record ID 5001" or "Send an email". An action with a custom name in the editor shows that name. Example value "Send an email" messagesarray The messages the step logged. Each has a message and a level (info, warn, error, success or null). A message starts with its time in UTC, [HH:mm:ss.SSS]. Example value [{ "message": "[07:12:06.310] Action execution started.", "level": null }] action_idstring | null The automation action this step executed. null for trigger, filter and exception steps. Example value "a1b2c3" record_idinteger | null The record this step acted on, if it acted on one. null otherwise. Example value 5001 logged_atstring When the step was logged (YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss), in your timezone. Example value "2024-01-18 08:12:07" logged_at_utcstring Same instant as logged_at, in UTC. Example value "2024-01-18 07:12:07" The trigger step has the ID "{run_id}-trigger" and the filter step "{run_id}-filter". An action step also carries the execution it belongs to: "{run_id}-action-{action_id}-{execution_id}". An action inside a loop runs more than once, and each execution is its own step. An action that changes several records in one execution, such as collected_records_update, writes one step per record with the same id. Tell them apart by record_id. Tape adds an exception step when a run failed and no single step recorded the failure. When is a step skipped? When the run did not execute it on purpose. That is the trigger step of a manual or simulation run, and the filter step of a simulation run. In a simulation, the steps of actions that change records, such as record_create or current_record_update, read skipped too. Other action steps of a simulation, for example custom_variable or send_email, read success, but the simulation still has no side effects. A regular run produces no skipped steps. Why are labels and messages in English? type, status and level are stable values for machines and are never translated. label and message are prose, and this endpoint returns them in English, whatever the language of the user behind the credential.

A malformed body returns a 400 validation error. For example, a cursor sent together with a filter: Response { "status_code": 400, "endpoint": "/v1/automation-run", "error_code": "input_validation", "error_message": "Invalid input: data must match exactly one schema in oneOf ([...])" } The same applies to: a limit outside 1–500; a filter array with more than 100 IDs; an unknown status or an unknown body property; a date bound that is not a valid YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss datetime; a run ID that is not an integer. A lower date bound later than the upper bound also returns 400. The message names the fields you sent, for example created_at_from_utc if you used the UTC version: Response { "status_code": 400, "endpoint": "/v1/automation-run", "error_code": "validation", "error_message": "\"created_at_from\" must be before or equal to \"created_at_to\"." } See Errors for the full list of error codes.

Creates a record in a database app. Without field_assignments, it creates an empty record. { "type": "record_create", "group": "action", "config": { "app_id": 12345, "silent": false, "trigger_other_flows": false } } app_id: the target database app. Send it in every config. The schema doesn't mark it as required, and validation doesn't report it when it's missing. Without it, the action saves but Tape skips it when the automation runs. field_assignments: [] is accepted in every case. A filled assignment has the same shape as in Update the current record below. trigger_other_flows is the option Trigger automations in the automation editor. false keeps the new record from starting other automations. Keep it at false to avoid a loop when this automation triggers on the same database app. All three keys are plain scalars, with no dynamic-value arrays.

Updates the record the run works on, with a list of field_assignments. { "type": "current_record_update", "group": "action", "config": { "field_assignments": [], "silent": false } } field_assignments (optional): left out or [] is a valid update that changes no field value and still logs success. The record's last_modified_on and last_modified_by still change. A filled assignment is a typed object per field type, with lower-case field_type and assignment_type values (for example single_text and set) plus any nested match or search conditions in the public filter tree. meta/action describes the items only loosely. current_record_update shows filled assignments to copy. It targets the current record, with no app_id (that's referenced_records_update) and no record_collection (that's collected_records_update). It needs a trigger with a record, such as record_created. With no trigger, or with periodic or webhook_received, validate reports action_invalid. See Trigger context. silent, trigger_webhooks, trigger_other_flows and author_id are optional. trigger_webhooks and trigger_other_flows are the options Trigger webhooks and Trigger automations in the editor. Without author_id, the automation itself is the author.

Runs your own code in the automation sandbox. This is the most self-contained action: no referenced entities and no external service. { "type": "custom_code", "group": "action", "config": { "code": ["const sum = 1 + 1;"] } } code (required): a code dynamic value, an array of literal strings mixed with variable references that pull in record data. Value references aren't allowed here. See Dynamic values. Tape also accepts a plain string and turns it into an array. custom_variable_defs left out means the script declares no variables for later actions.

Computes a value and stores it in a declared variable that later actions can reference. { "type": "custom_variable", "group": "action", "config": { "custom_variable_defs": [{ "custom_type": "any", "label": "Result" }], "assignment_code": ["1 + 1"] } } custom_variable_defs: the declaration. Each entry is { "custom_type", "label" }. custom_type is one of any, single_file, multi_file, single_link, html_table_rows. Later actions reference the variable with { "kind": "variable", "source": "custom", "custom_type", "label" }. assignment_code: a code dynamic value (array) that computes the value. Tape evaluates it as one expression: write 1 + 1, not return 1 + 1;. A top-level return fails when the automation runs. See custom_variable. custom_code is different: its code is a block of statements. Don't use a top-level return there either. Tape runs the code of all actions as one script, so a return stops every later action. Why does my action save but do nothing? With an empty or missing custom_variable_defs, this action still validates and saves. When the automation runs, Tape skips it without a per-action log. The same happens to a for_loop without iterable and to an authenticated_http_call without authentication_provider_id.

Sends one email from the automation. { "type": "send_email", "group": "action", "config": { "to_address": ["juliet@acme.com"], "subject": ["Email from the automation"], "message_body": ["

Sent by the send_email automation action.

"] } } to_address and subject are required. message_body is optional. Without it, Tape sends the email with an empty body. All three are template dynamic values (arrays). The HTML body comes back unchanged. Without smtp_account_id, Tape uses the organization's default SMTP account. Set an ID only if you need a specific account. send_email shows where to find it.

Sends an HTTP request from the automation sandbox. { "type": "http_call", "group": "action", "config": { "http_call_type": "get", "http_call_url": ["https://tapeapp.com/"] } } http_call_type (required): a lower-case enum scalar, one of get, post, put, patch, delete. http_call_url (required): a template dynamic value (array), so you can put record data into the URL. Requests leave from Tape's worker IP addresses and are subject to network restrictions. See Troubleshooting › IP addresses. Tape refuses private and internal hosts.

A control-flow action. It runs its nested action_rows (the then-branch) only when condition is true. { "type": "conditional", "group": "control_flow", "config": { "condition": { "operator": "and", "rows": [ { "id": "cond-leaf", "code": ["true"] } ] }, "action_rows": [ { "id": "then-1", "type": "custom_code", "group": "action", "config": { "code": ["const a = 1;"] } } ] } } The branch structure lives inside config: condition, action_rows and the optional else_action_rows. Like every action, a conditional keeps its whole shape in config. See conditional. condition is a filter group. The row above is a script condition, with code instead of subject, operator and value. action_rows is the then-branch, with full nested action nodes. Add else_action_rows inside config for an else-branch. Leave it out to switch the else-branch off.

A control-flow action. It runs its nested action_rows (the loop body) once for each item of an iterable. { "type": "for_loop", "group": "control_flow", "config": { "iterable": { "kind": "variable", "source": "action", "action_type": "record_collection", "app_id": 12345 }, "action_rows": [ { "id": "loop-body", "type": "custom_code", "group": "action", "config": { "code": ["const x = 1;"] } } ] } } The loop lives inside config: iterable (what to loop over), action_rows (the body), and the optional break_condition and continue_condition. The iterable is a record_collection from an earlier collect_* action, a multi-value field or a custom variable. Without an iterable, the loop body doesn't run. The collection pattern shows how to create and reference a collection. On its own, the example doesn't validate (action_variable_missing): put a collect_app_records action before it.

The collection pattern: a collect action earlier in the list creates a record_collection, and a later action references it. Order matters. The action that creates the collection comes first. { "actions": [ { "id": "collect", "type": "collect_app_records", "group": "action", "config": { "app_id": 12345 } }, { "type": "collected_records_update", "group": "action", "config": { "record_collection": { "kind": "variable", "source": "action", "action_type": "record_collection", "app_id": 12345 }, "field_assignments": [], "silent": false } } ] } record_collection is an object reference, never a string. Tape resolves it by action_type and app_id to the nearest earlier action that creates such a collection. It doesn't name the id of the collect action. Every action that uses a collection takes the same reference shape: filter_record_collection, sort_record_collection, collected_records_comment_create, the iterable of a for_loop, and so on.

source Extra fields Points to field field_id, field_type, previous, collection, triggering A field's value on the record. trigger trigger_type (plus key_path and data_type for webhook_payload_property) The trigger's output. action action_type, app_id? The output of an earlier action. global global_type A value for the whole automation. meta meta_type, app_id, previous, collection, triggering Record metadata. custom custom_type, label A variable you declared, or the output of http_call, create_pdf, rollup_iterable_values or current_record_generate_automation_weblink. documents.t: property values come from the stored value. They can look different from the label in Tape. A status option is sent as completed, a checklist assignee as assign_user_formatted. Tape doesn't check referenced IDs when you write. A well-formed ID that doesn't exist or belongs to someone else passes here. It shows up when you validate or activate. Some references and plain config IDs are only checked when the automation runs. Tape checks the structure of a reference when you write. An unrecognized discriminator returns 400: an unknown source on a kind: "variable" reference, an unknown value_type on a kind: "value" reference, or a field reference without field_type. previous, collection and triggering are optional on write and default to false. A meta reference needs app_id, the app of the record it reads. For the current record, that's the automation's app. Tape saves a reference without app_id, but validate reports action_variable_missing and activation fails. meta references keep previous, collection and triggering on write, like field references. A read returns these flags only when they're true, so a plain meta reference reads back without them. Collection actions use a collection-scoped meta reference (collection: true, with app_id). A sort_record_collection sort key needs one. A meta reference without collection fails validation there. One reference loses data in v1. Custom variables of type html_table_rows don't keep their inner template when you read and write them back. Template and code members accept a plain string on write. It's short for a one-element literal array: "application/json" equals ["application/json"]. A read returns them wrapped in an array. This also applies to nested template members, for example each http_call_headers[].value and the template and code strings inside field_assignments. A written config doesn't come back byte for byte for these fields, so don't compare write and read. Three flags set which value a field reference returns: previous: true reads the value before the triggering change. triggering: true points to the record that fired the trigger. collection: true reads the value of each collected record in an earlier collection, which is what collection actions use. With false, it reads the current record.

Action examples dynamic values in real action configs. Filters use references as filter subjects and values. Triggers what each trigger hands to the run. Run & simulate validate an automation before you run it.

Manual run and simulate share one body. Send the payload that the automation's trigger expects. The automation in the path already fixes the trigger, so you don't name it again. Record-based (record_created, record_updated, record_deleted, date_field_arrived, record_comment_or_reply_created, automation_called, weblink_clicked) { "record_id": <id> } webhook_received { "webhook_payload": <object or string> } or { "use_last_received_webhook_payload": true } periodic, or no trigger {} A well-formed body that doesn't match the automation's actual trigger returns 400. Does a paused automation still run? Yes. Manual run and simulate use the automation's stored definition, whether it's paused or not, so you can test without setting it live. Only a broken definition returns 409. The call automation endpoint works differently: it creates no run for a paused target and reports no error. Why is there no run ID in the response? Both endpoints queue the work for a background worker and answer 202 with a fixed message. A manual run creates its run only after the record passes the filter. A simulation skips the filter. To see the result, poll List runs for an automation and match triggered_on_record_id to your record. type tells real and simulation runs apart (manual or simulation). When do run logs show up? A run's per-action logs arrive after the run reaches a final status (completed or failed). The trigger and filter steps are there from the start. Poll for the specific log entry you need. Don't wait for logs.length > 0, which can return before an action's entry is in. Some successful steps write no per-action success entry: the control-flow containers (conditional, for_loop), collected_records_collect_referenced_records and create_pdf. For those, a final completed without a setup failure is the success signal. An action with deactivate: true writes no entry. Tape removes it before the run starts, so it's missing from the log, not listed as skipped. See Automation run for how the two differ and when skipped appears. Run an automation​ Use this endpoint to run an automation on a record, with real side effects. POST/v1/automation/{automation_id}/manual-runapi.tapeapp.com Request curl -X POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation/4021/manual-run \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ --data '{ "record_id": 5001 }' Response { "message": "Use the automation-run API to poll the run. Based on queueing and limitations, this may be delayed." } To find automation_id, see List automations. In the automation editor, it's the number after /edit-workflow/ in the address. To check the run, follow step 3 of Run an existing automation. General behavior This is the API version of Manual run in the automation editor, for one record. See Execution types. Tape queues the run with at-least-once delivery. One request can run the automation more than once. Tape applies the filter. A record that doesn't match creates no run. Each request costs 1x base credits. A real run also uses automation action credits, reported as num_consumed_actions. record_id must point to a live record in the automation's app. A deleted record, a record in another database app or an unknown ID returns 404 before Tape schedules the run. To test current_record_restore, delete the record within the run: put a current_record_delete step before it. Why does my comment automation create no run? For a record_comment_or_reply_created automation, a manual run uses the record's most recent comment or reply as the current comment. A record without comments or replies creates no run. The endpoint still answers 202. Requirements: automations:run, and the Admin role in the app's workspace. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key. Errors An automation ID that isn't an integer, or a body that doesn't match the trigger, returns 400. A credential that doesn't act on behalf of a user returns 401. A token without automations:run returns 403. An automation or record that isn't available to you returns 404. A broken automation returns 409. Simulate an automation​ Use this endpoint to run the automation's stored definition as a dry run, with no side effects. POST/v1/automation/{automation_id}/simulateapi.tapeapp.com Request curl -X POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation/4021/simulate \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ --data '{ "record_id": 5001 }' The response is the same 202 with { "message": … } as for Run, with no run ID. General behavior A simulation creates a simulation run every time. Most run lists leave it out. List runs for an automation shows it, and you can retrieve it by ID. The body is the same as for Run. Each request costs 1x base credits. You also need view access to the target record. Requirements: automations:run, and the Admin role in the app's workspace. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key. Errors The same causes as for Run return 400, 401, 403, 404 and 409. Validate an automation​ Use this endpoint to check whether the current definition can run. GET/v1/automation/{automation_id}/validateapi.tapeapp.com Request curl https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation/4021/validate \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" Response { "valid": false, "errors": [ { "code": "action_app_missing", "message": "An action references an app that no longer exists.", "action_id": "a1b2c3", "app_id": 42, "deactivated": false } ] } Key fields valid: true when no error sits in an active part of the automation. An entry with deactivated: true doesn't count. errors: one entry per fault. Each entry has the same shape and the same broken-reason codes as broken_reason on the automation object. General behavior No request body. Tape computes a fresh verdict. It can differ from the stored broken flag, because create and update don't store a new verdict. What does validate check? validate checks meaning, not syntax: whether a stored definition still points to things that exist and can be reached. Typical faults are a deleted field or app, a removed connection, or an action that uses a collection no earlier action creates. These faults can appear after a successful save, without any change to the definition. Payload format is checked earlier. Create and update reject a malformed body with 400, for example an unknown enum value, a broken dynamic-value reference or a tree nested too deep. Does valid: true mean the run succeeds? Not necessarily. validate checks the listed faults, and some references only for presence. For example, Tape only checks that the app_view_id of a collect_app_view_records action isn't empty, so a wrong view ID fails only when the automation runs. Requirements: automations:read, and the Admin role in the app's workspace. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key. Errors An automation ID that isn't an integer returns 400. A credential that doesn't act on behalf of a user returns 401. A token without automations:read returns 403. An automation that isn't available to you returns 404.
