Start an automation that someone already built in Tape. You need the Admin role in the app's workspace and a personal access token with the capabilities Read automations (automations:read) and Run automations (automations:run). 1. Find the automation ID. List the automations you administer. query keeps those whose name contains the text, ignoring case. Request curl "https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation/org?query=lead" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" Response { "total": 1, "automations": [ { "id": 4021, "app_id": 87, "name": "Email the owner on a new high-priority lead", "paused": false, "broken": false } ], "cursor": null } Each entry is a full automation object. The example is shortened. Keep the id. Have the automation open in Tape? Its ID is the number after /edit-workflow/ in the address. 2. Run it on a record. The record must be in the automation's app. Request curl -X POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation/4021/manual-run \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ --data '{ "record_id": 5001 }' Response { "message": "Use the automation-run API to poll the run. Based on queueing and limitations, this may be delayed." } The response is 202 with no run ID. The run has real side effects. The run body depends on the trigger. 3. Check the run. List the runs of the automation and find the one with your triggered_on_record_id. Request curl -X POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation-run/automation/4021 \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ --data '{ "limit": 5 }' Response { "total": 1, "automation_runs": [ { "id": "9001", "automation_id": 4021, "status": "completed", "type": "manual", "triggered_on_record_id": 5001 } ], "cursor": null } The example is shortened. status is pending or running while the run works, then completed, failed or cancelled. Retrieve the run by its id to read the step logs. Does the automation have to be live? No, a manual run also starts a paused automation. Only a broken one returns 409. To test without side effects, simulate it. Want another system to start the automation without a token? Give the automation a Webhook received trigger and send a POST to its webhook URL. Retrieve the automation to read it from trigger.config.webhook_url. See Connect Google Forms to Tape.

Part Cardinality What it is Trigger 0 or 1 The event that starts the automation: a record is created, a date arrives, a schedule fires, a webhook comes in, and so on. See Triggers. Filter 0 or 1 A recursive and/or tree of conditions the triggering record must match. Omitted or null means the automation runs every time. See Filters. Actions 0 or more An ordered list of steps: send an email, create a record, branch, loop, and so on. See The action object. The discovery endpoints serve the live catalog of trigger types, action types and filter operators, with the exact config each one accepts. Build against it instead of hard-coding the list: new types show up there without an API change. Coming from Podio? A Podio flow or a Globiflow flow becomes an automation. Field references use the field_id, not the external_id. See Move your flows for the trigger and action of each flow step.

Which credential and capability do I need? Every endpoint on this resource needs a credential that acts on behalf of a user: a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key. A token also needs the matching capability from the table below. See Capabilities. Capability Endpoints automations:read Discovery, retrieve, list, revisions, validate automations:edit Create, update, replace the trigger, activate, pause, delete automations:run Run, simulate, and the two Advanced / sandbox endpoints For the endpoints on Manage, Revisions and Run & simulate, you need the Admin role in the app's workspace. That workspace must be in your own organization. A personal access token also needs the app in its content access. Can I use an automation API key? Only on the discovery endpoints and the two Advanced / sandbox endpoints (call automation and generate weblink). Everywhere else it returns 401, because an automation API key authenticates an automation, not a person. The error message names only the user API key (Automations can only be retrieved with a user API key.), but a personal access token or an OAuth access token works too. Discovery is the exception​ The three discovery endpoints (meta/trigger, meta/action, meta/filter) return a static catalog that is the same for everyone. They have no workspace scope. A token still needs automations:read. Unavailable automations return 404​ Tape IDs are unique across all organizations. Every automation you can't use returns the same 404, so the API never reveals which IDs exist. That covers an automation that doesn't exist, was deleted, is an unsaved draft, is in a workspace you don't administer, or is outside your personal access token's content access.

The automation object lists every property with an example. Triggers, Filters and Actions describe each part. Config values can pull in live record data through dynamic values. The object page also explains the broken flag. Errors & broken reasons lists every code in broken_reason.

An automation has no single status field. Its state is the pair of booleans paused and broken: paused broken Meaning false false Live. The automation runs when its trigger fires. true false Paused. A valid automation that its trigger doesn't fire. You can still run or simulate it manually. any true Broken. The definition can't run, so it doesn't. A new automation starts paused and not broken: a valid draft that you set up and then activate. Activate checks the definition again and refuses a broken one with 409. Pause succeeds every time. Every change creates a new, unchangeable revision.

Most IDs on this resource are plain JSON integers: id, app_id, workspace_id, and the automation_id in a path. Two are strings: A revision ID is a 64-bit value, returned as a string so any language can handle it safely. Action ids are opaque. Treat them as handles, not numbers. All timestamps use the Tape API datetime format YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss, with no T separator, no Z suffix and no milliseconds. A plain timestamp such as created_at is in your timezone, and its _utc twin holds the same instant in UTC. See Date & timezone.

Endpoints Cost The list endpoints (app, workspace, organization) 2x base credits Everything else: discovery, retrieve, create, update, lifecycle, revisions, validate, run, simulate 1x base credits These request credits are separate from the automation action credits that a real run uses and reports as num_consumed_actions. Runtime limits, such as the cap on actions per run, the cap of 1000 records per collection and the shared email quota, are on Limits and throttling.

Errors use the standard envelope: status_code, endpoint, error_code and error_message. On this resource: A malformed body, a path ID that isn't an integer, or a run body that doesn't match the trigger returns 400. A credential that doesn't act on behalf of a user, where the endpoint needs one, returns 401. A token without the capability the endpoint needs returns 403. See Capabilities. An automation, app, workspace, revision or record that isn't available to you returns 404. See Unavailable automations return 404. Activating, running or simulating a broken automation returns 409. See Errors & broken reasons for the Automation API and Errors for all error codes.

Run an existing automation find the ID, run it and check the run. Quickstart build and run your first automation end to end. Discovery read the catalog before you build. Manage create, update and activate automations. Run & simulate validate, run and simulate. Automation run read the runs your automations create.

Read which triggers, actions and filter operators exist. Don't hard-code them. Request curl https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation/meta/trigger \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" Do the same for /meta/action and /meta/filter?field_type=number. Trigger and action entries have a config_schema to build against. A /meta/filter entry is an operator, { operator, label, description?, value_arity }, without one.

Create the automation in an app. A new automation starts paused and not broken: a draft that you finish and then activate. Request curl -X POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation/app/87 \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ --data '{ "name": "Email the owner on a new high-priority lead", "trigger": { "type": "record_created", "config": {} } }' Replace 87 with the ID of your app. Retrieve all available apps lists the app IDs. The response is the automation object, wrapped as { "automation": … }. Keep its id for the next steps.

Add a filter and actions with a partial update. Fields you leave out stay unchanged. Request curl -X PUT https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation/4021 \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ --data '{ "filter": { "operator": "and", "rows": [ { "subject": { "kind": "variable", "source": "field", "field_id": 512, "field_type": "single_category", "previous": false, "collection": false, "triggering": false }, "operator": "is_any_of", "value": { "type": "ids", "ids": [9001] } } ] }, "actions": [ { "type": "send_email", "config": { "to_address": ["juliet@acme.com"], "subject": ["A new high-priority lead was created"] } } ] }' Replace 4021 with the id from step 2, 512 with a category field of your app and 9001 with the ID of one of its options. Retrieve a single app returns the field_id and, in config.settings.options, the option IDs. To send the email for every new record, leave out filter. Node IDs are optional: Tape creates them when you leave them out. The field reference in subject is a dynamic value that pulls in live record data.
documents.s: Step 3: Configure the filter and actions

documents.t: Check the definition before it goes live. Create and update don't store a new verdict, so broken can lag behind your edit. Request curl https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation/4021/validate \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" { "valid": true, "errors": [] } means it's ready. Otherwise each entry names the fault. See Errors & broken reasons.

Set the automation live. Tape checks the definition again and refuses a broken one with 409. Request curl -X POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation/4021/activate \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" From now on, every new record that matches the filter fires the automation. Pause it when you finish testing.

Run the automation manually on a record, then poll for the result. A manual run has real side effects. It runs asynchronously: the response is 202 with a message and no run ID. Request curl -X POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation/4021/manual-run \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ --data '{ "record_id": 5001 }' Replace 5001 with the ID of a record in the automation's app that matches the filter. A record that doesn't match creates no run. Retrieve records for an app lists the record IDs. Then list the automation's runs and find the one with your triggered_on_record_id: Request curl -X POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation-run/automation/4021 \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ --data '{ "limit": 5 }' Its status ends as completed, failed or cancelled. See List runs for an automation for the response, and Run & simulate for the run body per trigger and the polling model. A failed run names the cause in failure_reason and error_message. Retrieve the run by its id to read the step logs. Want to test without sending the email? Send the same request to /v1/automation/4021/simulate instead of /manual-run. Tape creates a run with type: "simulation" and no side effects. Its filter step reads skipped. The email step reads success, and its log message says that Tape skipped the email because of the simulation. See Simulate an automation.

Automation API the concepts, capabilities and the automation object. Discovery the full catalog with config schemas. Dynamic values reference fields and outputs of earlier steps. Action examples ready-made action configs to copy. Run & simulate simulate before you run for real. Revisions roll the automation back to an earlier version.

Property Type Description id string Opaque node ID. Optional on input, Tape creates one when you leave it out. Present on every read. type string The action type. See Action types. group string action or control_flow. Follows from type and is read-only. You can leave it out on input. custom_name string Optional label. Absent when not set. deactivate boolean Whether the step is skipped. Absent when not set. continue_on_error boolean Whether the run goes on when this step fails. Absent when not set. config object The step's settings, keyed as the action's config_schema describes. Required on every action you write through the API. An empty {} is valid for a step you haven't set up yet, unless the type's config_schema requires members, for example code for custom_code or exit_type for exit. Such a config and a missing config key return 400. Dynamic values inside use the reference model. (control-flow config) For conditional and for_loop, config holds the branch and loop structure. See Control-flow actions.

config keys come from the action's config_schema on meta/action, but a written config doesn't read back byte for byte. Tape fills in defaults for missing members on read. A missing match_condition or attach_files_match_condition reads back as an empty filter group or null, missing required arrays (ref_collection_defs, field_assignments, call_arguments, http_call_headers, sorts) as []. The exception is field_assignments of record_create: left out, it stays out on read. An unchanged GET → PUT still works, but don't compare write and read. field_assignments is a typed union per field type. It's the payload of every action that changes records (record_create, current_record_update, referenced_records_update, collected_records_update) and is told apart by field_type. The meta/action schema describes its array items only loosely, so copy the filled assignments from record_create or current_record_update. An empty [] is accepted in every case and changes no field value. A paired _enabled flag controls limit. In collect_app_records and collect_app_view_records, limit only takes effect when limit_enabled is true, so send both. Either way, a collect stops at the server maximum of 1000 records and cuts off the rest without an error when the automation runs. See Limits and throttling. The _enabled flags for triggering_app_ids and custom_variable_defs belong to the trigger config, not the action config. A condition inside config, for example the match_condition of a collect or filter action, uses the same public filter tree as the condition of a conditional: lower-case operator: "and" | "or" with rows. Passing config_schema checks only the structure. A config that passes the schema is saved. Rules that depend on meaning show up later as broken-reason codes when you validate or activate. Examples: the app_id of referenced_records_update must be an app that the trigger app relates to, and a sort key must be scoped to the collection. All config enum values are lower-case. Send them exactly as meta/action lists them, for example http_call_type: "post", exit_type: "success", ref_collection_defs[].direction: "incoming", match_type: "all". Stricter config shapes per type may follow. Read the keys from meta/action, and don't hard-code internal encodings.

There are 35 action types: 33 leaf actions (group: "action") and 2 control-flow actions (group: "control_flow"). Each type's config keys come from its config_schema on GET /v1/automation/meta/action. The labels and descriptions below follow that endpoint. The automation editor can name an action differently. Each action page gives its editor name. The families only help you read the list. An action's real grouping is its group field.
Action What it does custom_code Run code: runs custom code in the automation sandbox. custom_variable Set variable: computes and stores a custom variable for later actions.

Action What it does record_create Create record: creates a record in a database app. current_record_update Update record: updates the current record. current_record_delete Delete record: deletes the current record. current_record_restore Restore record: restores the current (soft-deleted) record. current_record_get_previous_revision Get previous revision: loads the previous revision of the current record. current_record_comment_create Add comment: adds a comment to the current record. current_record_comment_or_reply_reply_create Add reply: adds a reply to the current comment or reply. current_record_comment_or_reply_delete Delete comment or reply: deletes the current comment or reply.

Action What it does collect_app_records Collect app records: collects records from a database app, optionally filtered. collect_app_view_records Collect app view records: collects records from a view of a database app. collect_referenced_records Collect referenced records: collects records referenced by the current record. collected_records_collect_referenced_records Collect referenced records (from collection): collects records referenced by a starting record collection. filter_record_collection Filter collection: filters a record collection. sort_record_collection Sort collection: sorts a record collection. clear_record_collection Clear collection: empties a record collection. collected_records_update Update collected records: updates every record in a collection. referenced_records_update Update referenced records: updates records referenced by the current record. collected_records_comment_create Comment on collected records: adds a comment to every record in a collection. rollup_iterable_values Roll up values: aggregates the values of an iterable (count, sum, average, …). Most of these actions work in pairs: one creates a collection, a later one uses it. A collect_* action creates a record_collection. A later action uses it: filter_record_collection, sort_record_collection, clear_record_collection, the collected_records_* family, or the iterable of a for_loop. The action that creates the collection must come first in the automation. The later action references the collection with an object, { "kind": "variable", "source": "action", "action_type": "record_collection", "app_id": … }. Tape resolves it to the nearest earlier action that creates such a collection. It never names that action's id. An action that uses a collection without a matching earlier action fails validation.

Action What it does current_record_call_automation Call automation: calls another automation with the current record. collected_records_call_automation Call automation for collected records: calls another automation for every record in a collection. current_record_generate_automation_weblink Generate weblink: generates a weblink that calls an automation with the current record. display_webpage Display webpage: displays a webpage in a weblink flow. redirect_user Redirect user: redirects the user to a URL in a weblink flow. The call and weblink actions reference a target automation by ID. The target must exist, be in the right database app and have the matching trigger. Otherwise the definition fails validation. current_record_call_automation needs a target with automation_called in the same database app as the trigger. collected_records_call_automation needs a target with automation_called in the database app of its record_collection. Without record_collection, validation reports action_invalid and action_automation_invalid. current_record_generate_automation_weblink needs a target with weblink_clicked in the same database app as the trigger. The action itself runs with any trigger that has a record. See Trigger context. A paused target is a valid reference, but a call to it creates no run. See Call an automation.

Action What it does send_email Send email: sends an email. collected_records_send_email Send email for collected records: sends an email for every record in a collection. create_pdf Create PDF: renders an HTML template to a PDF file.

Action What it does http_call HTTP request: makes an outbound HTTP request. authenticated_http_call Authenticated HTTP request: makes an outbound HTTP request signed by an authentication provider. Outbound requests have SSRF protection. Tape refuses hosts that resolve to private or internal addresses. authenticated_http_call also needs an authentication_provider_id. The public API has no endpoint to create or list connections. An organization admin sets them up in Tape. You can define the action through the API, but without a valid provider ID, Tape skips it when the automation runs.

Action What it does delay Delay: pauses the automation for a fixed duration. exit Exit: ends the automation run with success or failure. for_loop For loop: runs nested actions for each item of an iterable. group: "control_flow". conditional Condition: runs nested actions only when a condition holds. group: "control_flow".

Some actions are only valid with a matching trigger. A wrong pairing fails validation with action_invalid, unless the row says otherwise. Action(s) Requires trigger display_webpage weblink_clicked redirect_user weblink_clicked. Validation doesn't check this pairing. The editor offers the action only there. current_record_comment_or_reply_reply_create, current_record_comment_or_reply_delete record_comment_or_reply_created current_record_* (update, delete, restore, get_previous_revision, comment_create, call_automation, generate_automation_weblink), collect_referenced_records Any trigger with a record (not periodic or webhook_received without a record) referenced_records_update Any trigger with a record. Validation doesn't check the trigger, only app_id: without it action_app_missing, without a relation to the trigger's database app action_app_invalid. Without a current record, Tape skips the action when the automation runs. Triggers with a record are record_created, record_updated, record_deleted, record_comment_or_reply_created, date_field_arrived, automation_called and weblink_clicked.

conditional and for_loop keep their whole structure inside config, like every other action. There are no top-level control-flow fields. Each branch or condition is switched on by presence. A member you leave out is off. A nested body is an array of actions in action_rows. conditional: config keys Key Type Description condition filter group | null The branch condition. null or left out means true in every case. action_rows array of actions The if/then branch. else_action_rows array of actions The else branch. Leave it out to switch it off. for_loop: config keys Key Type Description iterable reference The collection to loop over. The public name is iterable; the internal name is iterable_variable_def. action_rows array of actions The loop body. break_condition filter group | null Stops the loop when it matches. Leave it out to switch it off. continue_condition filter group | null Skips to the next item when it matches. Leave it out to switch it off. See conditional and for_loop for full config examples.

Find the Tape action for each step of a Podio flow or a Globiflow flow. Podio flow or Globiflow step Tape action Create item record_create item.update, update item current_record_update, referenced_records_update, collected_records_update comment.create, comment current_record_comment_create Send email send_email Wait delay, 15, 30, 45 or 60 seconds Call flow current_record_call_automation Webhook call, octoblu.trigger http_call Generate PDF create_pdf Search items, loop collect_app_records, for_loop task.create, status.create No action. Use a checklist field instead of tasks.

Action examples configs to copy for the common actions. Dynamic values reference fields and outputs of earlier steps. Filters conditions for conditional, for_loop and collect actions. Triggers which trigger an action needs. Errors & broken reasons what validation reports.

When a deal is won, this action sends the deal to a sales system through a connection and saves the response: { "type": "authenticated_http_call", "config": { "http_call_type": "post", "http_call_url": ["https://crm.acme.com/api/v2/deals"], "http_call_headers": [ { "key": "Content-Type", "value": ["application/json"] } ], "http_call_body": ["{\"deal\": \"", { "kind": "variable", "source": "meta", "meta_type": "app_record_id", "app_id": 87 }, "\", \"stage\": \"won\"}"], "http_call_follow_redirects": false, "authentication_provider_id": 44, "custom_variable_defs": [ { "custom_type": "any", "label": "API response" } ] } }

Property Type Description Example value http_call_type enum Required. HTTP method: get, post, put, patch or delete. "post" http_call_url template value Required. Request URL. ["https://crm.acme.com/api/v2/deals"] authentication_provider_id integer ID of the connection that signs the request. Optional in the schema, but without it Tape skips the action when the automation runs. 44 http_call_body template value Request body. Empty when left out. ["{\"stage\": \"won\"}"] http_call_headers array of headers Request headers. Each entry is { "key", "value" }, both required, with an optional id. Empty when left out. [] http_call_follow_redirects boolean Follows 3xx redirects. Default false. false custom_variable_defs array of variable declarations Variables this action declares. Empty when left out. [{ "custom_type": "any", "label": "API response" }] The headers and custom_variable_defs work the same way as in http_call.

In the editor, the connection is the Connection field of the action. It's an OAuth 2.0 connection that an organization admin sets up in Tape. The public API has no endpoint to create or list connections. To find authentication_provider_id, select the connection in this action in the automation editor, then retrieve the automation. You can define the action through the API without a valid ID. Tape saves it, and validation doesn't report it. When the automation runs, Tape skips the action without a per-action log.

Tape stores the response body in the first variable of custom_variable_defs. A later action reads it with a custom reference that has the same custom_type and label: { "kind": "variable", "source": "custom", "custom_type": "any", "label": "API response" } Without a declared variable, Tape sends the request and keeps no response. The editor declares one variable called API response.
documents.s: Use the response in a later action

documents.t: http_call_type and http_call_url are required. Neither has a default. Every other key except authentication_provider_id has a default: an empty body, no headers, no redirects and no declared variables. With an empty http_call_url, Tape skips the action when the automation runs. Outbound requests have SSRF protection. Tape refuses hosts that resolve to private or internal addresses. Each header needs key and value. Send "" or [] for a blank value.

To add or change this action through the API, your token needs the automations:edit capability. See Capabilities. You must administer the workspace that the automation's database app belongs to. An organization admin has set up the connection in Tape.

http_call send a request without a connection. IP addresses where requests come from and which hosts Tape refuses. Dynamic values template values and custom references. Action examples why an action can save but do nothing. Actions all 35 action types.

An earlier action collected job candidates from database app 100. This action empties that collection: { "type": "clear_record_collection", "config": { "record_collection": { "kind": "variable", "source": "action", "action_type": "record_collection", "app_id": 100 } } }

Property Type Description Example value record_collection reference Required. The collection to empty, created by an earlier action. The schema lets you save without it, but validation then reports action_invalid. { "kind": "variable", "source": "action", "action_type": "record_collection", "app_id": 100 }

record_collection is the only key. It has no default. Without record_collection, Tape saves the action, and validation reports action_invalid. A record_collection without a matching earlier action fails validation with action_variable_missing. Reference a collection from a collect action, not a single field value. Later actions that reference the same collection get an empty list.

To add or change this action through the API, your token needs the automations:edit capability. See Capabilities. You must administer the workspace that the automation's database app belongs to. An earlier action in the automation must create the collection in record_collection, for example collect_app_records.

filter_record_collection keep only some records instead of none. Dynamic values build the record_collection reference. Action examples configs to copy for the common actions. Actions all 35 action types.

This action collects up to 100 listings whose Address field isn't empty: { "type": "collect_app_records", "config": { "app_id": 4821, "match_condition": { "operator": "and", "rows": [ { "subject": { "kind": "variable", "source": "field", "field_id": 55012, "field_type": "single_text", "previous": false, "collection": false, "triggering": false }, "operator": "is_not_empty" } ] }, "limit": 100, "limit_enabled": true } }

Property Type Description Example value app_id integer ID of the database app to collect records from. Without it, Tape skips the action when the automation runs. 4821 match_condition filter group | null Filters the records to collect. Left out, Tape collects every record of the database app. A filter that matches everything reads back as null. null limit integer Maximum number of records to collect. Takes effect only when limit_enabled is true. Default 1. 100 limit_enabled boolean Whether Tape applies limit. Default false. true To find app_id and the field IDs for match_condition, see App and field IDs.

This action creates a record_collection for the database app in app_id. A later action references it with this object: { "kind": "variable", "source": "action", "action_type": "record_collection", "app_id": 4821 } Tape resolves the reference to the nearest earlier action that creates a collection for the same app_id. Use it in filter_record_collection, sort_record_collection, clear_record_collection, the collected_records_* actions and the iterable of a for_loop. See Record collections for the pattern.
documents.s: Use the collection in later actions

documents.t: Every key is optional when you save. Tape fills in the defaults. Every collect stops at 1000 records when the automation runs, with or without limit_enabled. Tape stores a limit above 1000 and reads it back unchanged. Neither the write nor validate warns. See Limits and throttling. Without app_id, the action saves and passes validation. When the automation runs, Tape skips it. An app_id of a deleted app fails validation with action_app_missing. An app_id that never existed makes validate and activate return 404. See Errors & broken reasons.
To add or change this action through the API, your token needs the automations:edit capability. See Capabilities. You must administer the workspace that the automation's database app belongs to.

collect_app_view_records collect the records of a view instead. Filters the filter group used by match_condition. Dynamic values build references to fields and collections. Action examples a collect action followed by an update of the collection. Actions all 35 action types.
This action collects up to 100 records from an Open deals view: { "type": "collect_app_view_records", "config": { "app_id": 4201, "app_view_id": 9317, "limit": 100, "limit_enabled": true } }

Property Type Description Example value app_id integer ID of the database app the view belongs to. Without it, Tape skips the action when the automation runs. 4201 app_view_id integer Required. ID of the view to collect records from. The schema lets you save without it, but validation then reports action_view_missing. 9317 limit integer Maximum number of records to collect. Takes effect only when limit_enabled is true. Default 1, like a new action in the editor. 100 limit_enabled boolean Whether Tape applies limit. Default false. true To find app_id, see App and field IDs. To find app_view_id, see Retrieve views for an app. It returns the ID of each public view as view_id.

This action creates a record_collection for the database app in app_id. A later action references it with this object: { "kind": "variable", "source": "action", "action_type": "record_collection", "app_id": 4201 } Tape resolves the reference to the nearest earlier action that creates a collection for the same app_id. Use it in filter_record_collection, sort_record_collection, clear_record_collection, the collected_records_* actions and the iterable of a for_loop. See Record collections for the pattern.
documents.s: Use the collection in later actions

documents.t: Tape collects the records that the view returns, with the view's own filters. Validation checks app_view_id for presence only. A view ID that doesn't exist passes validation and fails when the automation runs. Without app_id, the action saves and passes validation. When the automation runs, Tape skips it. An app_id of a deleted app fails validation with action_app_missing. An app_id that never existed makes validate and activate return 404. Without limit and limit_enabled, Tape fills in the defaults. Every collect stops at 1000 records when the automation runs, with or without limit_enabled. Tape stores a limit above 1000, or one with limit_enabled: false, and reads it back unchanged. Neither the write nor validate warns. See Limits and throttling.

To add or change this action through the API, your token needs the automations:edit capability. See Capabilities. You must administer the workspace that the automation's database app belongs to. The view in app_view_id must exist in the database app in app_id.

collect_app_records collect records with your own filter instead of a view. Dynamic values build references to fields and collections. Errors & broken reasons what action_view_missing and action_app_missing mean. Action examples a collect action followed by an update of the collection. Actions all 35 action types.

Starting from a project, this action collects the open tasks that the project's Tasks relation field points to: { "type": "collect_referenced_records", "config": { "ref_collection_defs": [ { "direction": "outgoing", "match_type": "filtered", "app_id": 1204, "via_field_ids": [88123], "match_condition": { "operator": "and", "rows": [ { "subject": { "kind": "variable", "source": "field", "field_id": 88140, "field_type": "single_category", "previous": false, "collection": false, "triggering": false }, "operator": "is_any_of", "value": { "type": "ids", "ids": [3] } } ] } } ] } }

Property Type Description Example value ref_collection_defs array of reference steps The steps that Tape follows from the current record. Empty when left out, and then the action collects nothing. [{ "direction": "outgoing", "match_type": "all", "app_id": 1204 }] To find app_id and the relation field IDs for via_field_ids, see App and field IDs. To find the option IDs for ids, see Retrieve a single app. It returns them in config.settings.options of the field.

Each entry in ref_collection_defs is one step along the relations: Property Type Description Example value direction enum Required. Which relations to follow. See Directions. "outgoing" match_type enum Required. all keeps every related record. filtered keeps only the records that match match_condition. "filtered" app_id integer Required. ID of the related database app to collect from. The schema lets you save without it, but validation then reports action_app_missing. 1204 via_field_ids array of integers The relation fields to follow. Left out, Tape follows every relation field to that database app. [88123] match_condition filter group | null Filters the related records in the filtered mode. Ignored with match_type: "all". An empty AND group when left out, read back as null. null id string Stable ID of the step. Tape creates one when you leave it out and returns it on read. "step-1"

direction takes one of these lower-case tokens: outgoing: records that this record points to through its own relation fields. In the editor, Outgoing via. incoming: records that point to this record through their relation fields. In the editor, Incoming via. both: records in either direction. In the editor, Both directions.

With more than one step, Tape follows them as a chain. The first step starts from the current record. Each later step starts from the records that the step before it found. Each step fills a record collection for its own app_id. A step's app_id must be a database app that the previous database app relates to. Otherwise validation reports action_app_invalid.

Each step creates a record_collection for its app_id. A later action references the tasks from the example with this object: { "kind": "variable", "source": "action", "action_type": "record_collection", "app_id": 1204 } Tape resolves the reference to the nearest earlier action that creates a collection for the same app_id. Use it in filter_record_collection, sort_record_collection, clear_record_collection, the collected_records_* actions and the iterable of a for_loop. See Record collections for the pattern.
documents.s: Use the collection in later actions

documents.t: ref_collection_defs is optional when you save. direction and match_type have no default. Send both on every step, as lower-case tokens. Neither the save nor validate reports a step without direction or match_type. The step then reads back without both keys. Without a trigger that has a record, validation reports the broken reason action_invalid. periodic and webhook_received have no record.

To add or change this action through the API, your token needs the automations:edit capability. See Capabilities. You must administer the workspace that the automation's database app belongs to. The automation needs a trigger with a record. The database app of each step must relate to the database app before it.

collected_records_collect_referenced_records start from a collection instead of the current record. Filters the filter group used by match_condition. Triggers which triggers carry a record. Dynamic values reference the collection in later actions. Actions all 35 action types.

An earlier action collects the contracts that renew next quarter. This action calls the renewal reminder automation for each of them: { "type": "collected_records_call_automation", "config": { "automation_id": 4022, "record_collection": { "kind": "variable", "source": "action", "action_type": "record_collection", "app_id": 2087 }, "call_arguments": [ { "variable_def": { "custom_type": "any", "label": "Renewal quarter" }, "assignment_type": "set", "value": ["Q1 2027"] } ] } }

Property Type Description Example value automation_id integer Required. ID of the automation to call for each record. The schema lets you save without it, but validation then reports action_automation_missing. 4022 record_collection reference Required. The collection whose records Tape calls the automation for, created by an earlier action. The schema lets you save without it, but validation then reports action_invalid and action_automation_invalid. { "kind": "variable", "source": "action", "action_type": "record_collection", "app_id": 2087 } call_arguments array of call arguments Values for the inputs that the called automation declares. Empty when left out. [] To find automation_id, see List automations. It returns the ID of each automation as id. Each call_arguments entry has the same shape as in current_record_call_automation: variable_def (required): the input to fill, as { "custom_type", "label" }. assignment_type: set uses value (a template value), set_code uses code (a code value). Default set. id: stable ID of the entry. Tape creates one when you leave it out and returns it on read.

No key is required by the schema. Tape saves the action without automation_id, record_collection or call_arguments. Tape calls the target automation once per record in the collection. Without record_collection, validation reports action_invalid. It also reports action_automation_invalid, because Tape then has no database app to check the target against. A record_collection without a matching earlier action fails validation with action_variable_missing. Tape resolves the reference to the nearest earlier action that creates a collection for the same app_id. The target automation must exist. Otherwise validation reports action_automation_missing. The target must live in the database app of the collected records and use the automation_called trigger. Otherwise validation reports action_automation_invalid. A paused target is a valid reference. Each call_arguments label must match a custom variable of the target's trigger, with custom_variable_defs_enabled set to true. Otherwise validation reports action_call_argument_invalid.

To add or change this action through the API, your token needs the automations:edit capability. See Capabilities. You must administer the workspace that the automation's database app belongs to. An earlier action in the automation must create the collection in record_collection, for example collect_app_records. The target automation uses the automation_called trigger and lives in the database app of the collected records.

current_record_call_automation call the target for the current record only. Triggers set up automation_called and its custom variables on the target. Dynamic values references for record_collection and call_arguments. Errors & broken reasons what the validation codes mean. Action examples a complete payload that collects records and uses the collection. Actions all 35 action types.

An earlier action collected solar installations from database app 87. This action collects the customers that those installations point to: { "type": "collected_records_collect_referenced_records", "config": { "record_collection": { "kind": "variable", "source": "action", "action_type": "record_collection", "app_id": 87 }, "ref_collection_defs": [ { "direction": "outgoing", "match_type": "all", "app_id": 91, "via_field_ids": [55012] } ] } }

Property Type Description Example value record_collection reference Required. The collection to start from, created by an earlier action. The schema lets you save without it, but validation then reports action_invalid. { "kind": "variable", "source": "action", "action_type": "record_collection", "app_id": 87 } ref_collection_defs array of reference steps The steps that Tape follows from the records in the collection. Empty when left out, and then the action collects nothing. [{ "direction": "outgoing", "match_type": "all", "app_id": 91 }] Each step has the same keys as in collect_referenced_records: direction (required): outgoing, incoming or both. match_type (required): all keeps every related record, filtered keeps only the records that match match_condition. app_id: the related database app. Validation reports action_app_missing without it. via_field_ids: the relation fields to follow. match_condition: a filter group for the filtered mode. An empty AND group when left out, read back as null. id: stable ID of the step. Tape creates one when you leave it out and returns it on read. With more than one step, Tape follows them as a chain. Each step starts from the records that the step before it found. To find app_id and the relation field IDs for via_field_ids, see App and field IDs.

Each step creates a record_collection for its app_id. A later action references the customers from the example with this object: { "kind": "variable", "source": "action", "action_type": "record_collection", "app_id": 91 } Tape resolves the reference to the nearest earlier action that creates a collection for the same app_id. Use it in filter_record_collection, sort_record_collection, clear_record_collection, the collected_records_* actions and the iterable of a for_loop. See Record collections for the pattern.
documents.s: Use the collection in later actions

documents.t: This action uses one collection and creates another. It starts from record_collection and fills a record collection for the app_id of each step. record_collection has no default. Without it, Tape saves the action, and validation reports action_invalid. A record_collection without a matching earlier action fails validation with action_variable_missing. direction and match_type have no default. Send both on every step, as lower-case tokens. Neither the save nor validate reports a step without direction or match_type. The step then reads back without both keys. Each step's app_id must relate to the database app before it. Otherwise validation reports action_app_invalid. For each step, the run log shows how many records Tape collected.

To add or change this action through the API, your token needs the automations:edit capability. See Capabilities. You must administer the workspace that the automation's database app belongs to. An earlier action in the automation must create the collection in record_collection, for example collect_app_records.

collect_referenced_records start from the current record instead. Filters the filter group used by each step's match_condition. Dynamic values build the record_collection reference. Actions all 35 action types.

This action asks every collected applicant to pick an interview slot: { "type": "collected_records_comment_create", "config": { "record_collection": { "kind": "variable", "source": "action", "action_type": "record_collection", "app_id": 123 }, "comment_content": ["Interview slots for next week are open. Pick one by Friday."], "silent": true } }

Property Type Description Example value comment_content template value Required. The comment text. ["Contract signed."] record_collection reference Required. The collection to comment on, created by an earlier action. The schema lets you save without it, but validation then reports action_invalid. { "kind": "variable", "source": "action", "action_type": "record_collection", "app_id": 123 } author_id integer | reference User Tape attributes the comment to: a user ID, or a reference to the creator, the last modifier or a user field. Left out, the automation itself is the author. 812 trigger_webhooks boolean Whether the comment fires outbound webhooks. Default false. false trigger_other_flows boolean Whether the comment starts other automations. Default false. false silent boolean Whether Tape sends no notifications for the comment. Default false. true author_id, trigger_webhooks, trigger_other_flows and silent are shared by every action that changes records. In the action menu of the automation editor, they are Author, Trigger webhooks, Trigger automations and Silent. To find a user ID for author_id, see Retrieve organization users.

comment_content is the only key the schema requires. Without record_collection, Tape saves the action, and validation reports action_invalid. A record_collection without a matching earlier action fails validation with action_variable_missing. Tape resolves the reference to the nearest earlier action that creates a collection for the same app_id. Tape adds the comment to each record in the collection. A field or meta reference with collection: true in comment_content reads that record's value. With an empty comment_content, Tape skips the action when the automation runs. If the references in comment_content resolve to empty text when the automation runs, the action fails, and so does the run. Mentions in comment_content can only point to members of the workspace that the collection's database app belongs to. Without author_id, the automation itself is the author. A user ID that Tape can't find gives the broken reason action_user_missing. Tape returns silent on every read. It's false when you left it out.

To add or change this action through the API, your token needs the automations:edit capability. See Capabilities. You must administer the workspace that the automation's database app belongs to. An earlier action in the automation must create the collection in record_collection, for example collect_app_records.

current_record_comment_create comment on the current record only. Dynamic values build template values and references. Action examples configs to copy for the common actions. Actions all 35 action types.

This action reminds the buyer of every collected viewing, using the email field of each record: { "type": "collected_records_send_email", "config": { "record_collection": { "kind": "variable", "source": "action", "action_type": "record_collection", "app_id": 640 }, "to_address": [{ "kind": "variable", "source": "field", "field_id": 6120, "field_type": "multi_email", "previous": false, "collection": true, "triggering": false }], "subject": ["Your viewing tomorrow"], "message_body": ["

See you at the property tomorrow. Reply to this email to reschedule.

"], "reply_address": ["juliet@acme.com"], "smtp_account_id": 812 } }

The config matches send_email, plus record_collection and fields_expanded. Property Type Description Example value record_collection reference Required. The collection whose records get one email each, created by an earlier action. The schema lets you save without it, but validation then reports action_invalid. { "kind": "variable", "source": "action", "action_type": "record_collection", "app_id": 640 } to_address template value Recipient address or addresses. Empty when left out. Without it, Tape skips the action when the automation runs. ["romeo@acme.com"] subject template value Subject line. Empty when left out. ["Your viewing tomorrow"] reply_address template value Reply-to address. Empty when left out. ["juliet@acme.com"] cc_address template value CC address or addresses. Empty when left out. ["romeo@acme.com"] bcc_address template value BCC address or addresses. Empty when left out. ["archive@acme.com"] from_address template value Sender address. Empty when left out. ["sales@acme.com"] from_name template value Sender display name. Empty when left out. ["Acme Realty"] message_body template value HTML body. Empty when left out. ["

Hello

"] smtp_account_id integer ID of the SMTP account to send from. Left out, Tape uses the organization's default SMTP account. See Sender address. Same ID as smtp_settings_id of the email endpoint. 812 attach_files_variable_defs array of references File variables Tape can attach: attachment or image fields, file custom variables such as the PDF from create_pdf, or the files of the trigger. Empty when left out. [] attach_files_match_type enum Which of those files Tape attaches. Default all. See Attachment modes. "all" attach_files_match_condition filter group | null Limits the attached files in the filtered and most_recent_filtered modes. An empty AND group when left out or null. null fields_expanded boolean Editor only: whether the address fields show expanded in the automation editor. Tape keeps it on read and write. Left out when not set. false To find smtp_account_id, select the account in this action in the automation editor, then retrieve the automation. The API has no endpoint that lists SMTP accounts.

attach_files_match_type takes one of these lower-case tokens: all: attaches every candidate file. Ignores the condition. most_recent: attaches the most recent file. Ignores the condition. filtered: attaches the files that match attach_files_match_condition. most_recent_filtered: attaches the most recent file that matches attach_files_match_condition.

Tape sends one email for each record in the collection. A field or meta reference with collection: true reads that record's value, like the email field in the example. Unlike send_email, the schema marks no key as required. Without record_collection, Tape saves the action, and validation reports action_invalid. A record_collection without a matching earlier action fails validation with action_variable_missing. Without to_address, Tape skips the action when the automation runs. Set to_address and subject for a useful email. Every other address, name and body defaults to empty. Every email an automation sends counts against the organization's shared 24-hour send quota.

To add or change this action through the API, your token needs the automations:edit capability. See Capabilities. You must administer the workspace that the automation's database app belongs to. An earlier action in the automation must create the collection in record_collection, for example collect_app_records.
send_email send a single email. Dynamic values build template values and references. Filters the filter group used by attach_files_match_condition. Actions all 35 action types.

This action marks every collected task as ready for review: { "type": "collected_records_update", "config": { "record_collection": { "kind": "variable", "source": "action", "action_type": "record_collection", "app_id": 5 }, "field_assignments": [ { "field_type": "single_text", "variable_def": { "kind": "variable", "source": "field", "field_id": 4021, "field_type": "single_text", "previous": false, "collection": false, "triggering": false }, "assignment_type": "set", "field_value": ["Ready for review"] } ], "silent": true } }

Property Type Description Example value record_collection reference Required. The collection to update, created by an earlier action. The schema lets you save without it, but validation then reports action_invalid. { "kind": "variable", "source": "action", "action_type": "record_collection", "app_id": 5 } field_assignments array of field assignments The values to set on each collected record, one entry per field. Empty when left out. See Field assignments. [] author_id integer | reference User Tape attributes the change to: a user ID, or a reference to the creator, the last modifier or a user field. Left out, the automation itself is the author. 812 trigger_webhooks boolean Whether the change fires outbound webhooks. Default false. false trigger_other_flows boolean Whether the change starts other automations. Default false. false silent boolean Whether Tape sends no notifications for the change. Default false. true To find the field IDs, see App and field IDs. author_id, trigger_webhooks, trigger_other_flows and silent are shared by every action that changes records. In the action menu of the automation editor, they are Author, Trigger webhooks, Trigger automations and Silent. To find a user ID for author_id, see Retrieve organization users.

Each entry in field_assignments sets one field on every collected record. field_type tells the 20 field-type shapes apart, for example single_text or number. variable_def is a reference to the target field. assignment_type picks how Tape produces the value. set uses field_value, set_code uses code. meta/action describes the populated shape only loosely. Copy the shapes from current_record_update and check the live config_schema before you send filled assignments.

No key is required by the schema. Without record_collection, Tape saves the action, and validation reports action_invalid. A record_collection without a matching earlier action fails validation with action_variable_missing. Tape resolves the reference to the nearest earlier action that creates a collection for the same app_id. Left out or [], field_assignments changes no field value. The action still logs a success step for each collected record. On an empty collection, the action changes nothing and logs one success step with the message No records were found in the collection. Without author_id, the automation itself is the author. A user ID that Tape can't find gives the broken reason action_user_missing. Tape returns silent on every read. It's false when you left it out.

To add or change this action through the API, your token needs the automations:edit capability. See Capabilities. You must administer the workspace that the automation's database app belongs to. An earlier action in the automation must create the collection in record_collection, for example collect_app_records.

referenced_records_update update the records related to the current record. current_record_update update only the record the run works on. Dynamic values build references and template values. Action examples a full collect-and-update payload. Actions all 35 action types.

When a deal is worth more than 50,000, this action asks the sales director for approval. Otherwise, it tells the account owner that the deal is ready to close: { "type": "conditional", "config": { "condition": { "operator": "and", "rows": [ { "subject": { "kind": "variable", "source": "field", "field_id": 601, "field_type": "number", "previous": false, "collection": false, "triggering": false }, "operator": "greater_than", "value": { "type": "number", "number": ["50000"] } } ] }, "action_rows": [ { "type": "send_email", "config": { "to_address": ["romeo@acme.com"], "subject": ["Approval needed: deal over 50,000"] } } ], "else_action_rows": [ { "type": "send_email", "config": { "to_address": ["juliet@acme.com"], "subject": ["Deal ready to close"] } } ] } }

Property Type Description Example value condition filter group | null The if condition. null or left out counts as true. { "operator": "and", "rows": [ … ] } action_rows array of nested actions The then branch. Runs when the condition holds. Empty when left out. [{ "type": "send_email", "config": { … } }] else_action_rows array of nested actions The else branch. Runs when the condition fails. Leave it out to switch the else branch off. [{ "type": "exit", "config": { "exit_type": "success" } }] To find the field IDs, see App and field IDs.

No key is required. The condition and both branches live in config, like every other action. Each branch is a nested list of actions. A missing, null or empty condition counts as true. The then branch runs on every run. It reads back as condition: null. Leave else_action_rows out to switch the else branch off. Send it, even as [], to switch it on. There are no *_enabled flags. action_rows and else_action_rows hold full action objects. GET /v1/automation/meta/action lists the types you can nest. When the API rejects the input of a nested action, the error names its path, for example config/else_action_rows/0. condition uses the same filter tree as the collect actions. GET /v1/automation/meta/filter lists the operators for each field type.
To add or change this action through the API, your token needs the automations:edit capability. See Capabilities. You must administer the workspace that the automation's database app belongs to.

exit end the run inside a branch. for_loop check the condition once per collected record. Filters the filter group used by condition. Dynamic values field references for the condition's subject. Action examples configs to copy for the common actions. Actions all 35 action types.

This action renders an invoice for the current record: { "type": "create_pdf", "config": { "filename": ["invoice-", { "kind": "variable", "source": "meta", "meta_type": "app_record_id", "app_id": 87 }, ".pdf"], "page_size": "a4", "page_orientation": "portrait", "page_margins": "normal", "pdf_body": ["

Invoice

Thank you for your order.

"], "custom_variable_def": { "custom_type": "single_file", "label": "Invoice PDF" } } }

Every key is optional. Tape fills in the same defaults as the editor, so a short config still gives a complete action. Property Type Description Example value filename template value Name of the generated file. Empty when left out. ["invoice.pdf"] custom_variable_def object The output variable that holds the generated PDF file. Default { "custom_type": "single_file", "label": "PDF" }. { "custom_type": "single_file", "label": "Invoice PDF" } pdf_body template value HTML template for the PDF content. Empty when left out. ["

Invoice

"] page_size enum Page size. Default a4. See Page sizes. "a4" page_custom_width code value Custom page width. Used only when page_size is custom_size. Empty when left out. ["210"] page_custom_height code value Custom page height. Used only when page_size is custom_size. Empty when left out. ["297"] page_orientation enum Page orientation: portrait or landscape. Default portrait. "portrait" page_margins enum Page margin preset. Default normal. See Page margins. "normal" page_custom_margin_top code value Custom top margin. Used only when page_margins is custom_margins. Empty when left out. ["20"] page_custom_margin_right code value Custom right margin. Used only when page_margins is custom_margins. Empty when left out. ["15"] page_custom_margin_bottom code value Custom bottom margin. Used only when page_margins is custom_margins. Empty when left out. ["20"] page_custom_margin_left code value Custom left margin. Used only when page_margins is custom_margins. Empty when left out. ["15"] pdf_header_custom_margin_top code value Custom top margin of the header. Used only when page_margins is custom_margins. Empty when left out. ["10"] pdf_footer_custom_margin_bottom code value Custom bottom margin of the footer. Used only when page_margins is custom_margins. Empty when left out. ["10"] page_numbers_enabled boolean Whether Tape adds page numbers. Default false. true page_number_style enum Numbering style of the page numbers. Default decimal. See Page number styles. "decimal" page_number_start code value The number of the first page. Empty when left out. ["1"] header_and_footer_enabled boolean Whether Tape adds the header and footer. Default false. true pdf_header template value HTML template for the header on the first page. Empty when left out. ["

Acme Inc.

"] pdf_header_following_pages_enabled boolean Whether the following pages get their own header. Default false. false pdf_header_following_pages template value HTML template for the header on the following pages. Empty when left out. ["

Invoice, continued

"] pdf_footer template value HTML template for the footer on the first page. Empty when left out. ["

Thank you for your business.

"] pdf_footer_following_pages_enabled boolean Whether the following pages get their own footer. Default false. false pdf_footer_following_pages template value HTML template for the footer on the following pages. Empty when left out. ["

Acme Inc.

"] options_expanded boolean Editor only: whether the advanced options section shows expanded. Default false. false pdf_header_expanded boolean Editor only: whether the header section shows expanded. Default true. true pdf_footer_expanded boolean Editor only: whether the footer section shows expanded. Default true. true pdf_body_expanded boolean Editor only: whether the body section shows expanded. Default true. Stays true while header_and_footer_enabled is false. true
page_size takes one of these lower-case tokens: letter tabloid legal a3 a4 a5 envelope_10 custom_size: uses page_custom_width and page_custom_height.
page_margins takes one of these lower-case tokens: normal narrow moderate wide custom_margins: uses the four page_custom_margin_* values and the header and footer margins.
page_number_style takes one of these lower-case tokens: decimal: 1, 2, 3 decimal_leading_zero: 01, 02, 03 lower_latin: a, b, c upper_latin: A, B, C lower_roman: i, ii, iii upper_roman: I, II, III

The four *_expanded keys only control which sections the automation editor shows expanded. They don't change the PDF. meta/action lists them in the config_schema. Tape keeps them on read and write, so a read-modify-write preserves them. While header_and_footer_enabled is false, Tape sets pdf_body_expanded to true. In that state the editor has no control to open a closed body section.

The action stores the file in the variable from custom_variable_def. A later action reads it with a custom reference that has the same custom_type and label. This send_email entry attaches the invoice: { "type": "send_email", "config": { "to_address": ["juliet@acme.com"], "subject": ["Your invoice"], "attach_files_variable_defs": [ { "kind": "variable", "source": "custom", "custom_type": "single_file", "label": "Invoice PDF" } ] } }
documents.s: Use the file in a later action

documents.t: The defaults are the ones in the Config table. Without custom_variable_def, the output variable has the label PDF. Tape ignores the custom sizes and margins unless page_size is custom_size or page_margins is custom_margins. Code values for sizes, margins and page_number_start must resolve to a number. Tape reads custom sizes and margins in millimeters, so ["210"] by ["297"] is A4. The action writes no reliable success entry to the run log. Don't use the log to confirm that the PDF was rendered.
To add or change this action through the API, your token needs the automations:edit capability. See Capabilities. You must administer the workspace that the automation's database app belongs to.

send_email attach the generated PDF to an email. Dynamic values build template values and code values, and use the PDF output variable. Action examples configs to copy for the common actions. Actions all 35 action types.

When a listing is marked as sold, this action calls the automation that notifies the buyer's agent and passes a closing note: { "type": "current_record_call_automation", "config": { "automation_id": 4021, "call_arguments": [ { "variable_def": { "custom_type": "any", "label": "Closing note" }, "assignment_type": "set", "value": ["Sold at asking price. Listing ", { "kind": "variable", "source": "meta", "meta_type": "app_record_id", "app_id": 87 }] } ] } }

Property Type Description Example value automation_id integer Required. ID of the automation to call. The schema lets you save without it, but validation then reports action_automation_missing. 4021 call_arguments array of call arguments Values for the inputs that the called automation declares. Empty when left out. [] To find automation_id, see List automations. It returns the ID of each automation as id.

Each entry in call_arguments binds one input of the called automation: Property Type Description Example value variable_def object Required. The input to fill, as { "custom_type", "label" }. The label must match a custom variable that the called automation's trigger declares. { "custom_type": "any", "label": "Closing note" } assignment_type enum Where the value comes from: set uses value, set_code uses code. Default set. "set" value template value The value for set. Empty when left out. ["Sold"] code code value The expression for set_code. Empty when left out. ["1 + 1"] id string Stable ID of the entry. Tape creates one when you leave it out and returns it on read. "a1b2c3" custom_type takes one of any, single_file, multi_file, single_link, html_table_rows. The called automation declares the input in its trigger: { "type": "automation_called", "config": { "custom_variable_defs_enabled": true, "custom_variable_defs": [{ "custom_type": "any", "label": "Closing note" }] } }

No key is required by the schema. Tape saves the action without automation_id or call_arguments. The target automation must exist. Otherwise validation reports action_automation_missing. Property Type Description Example value comment_content template value Required. Text of the comment. A plain string works too. Tape turns it into an array. ["Invoice approved."] author_id integer | reference User Tape attributes the comment to: a user ID, or a reference to the creator, the last modifier or a user field. When a new hire is added, this action creates a weblink that lets them confirm their start date. The link runs the confirmation automation and expires after a week: { "type": "current_record_generate_automation_weblink", "config": { "automation_id": 4023, "call_arguments": [ { "variable_def": { "custom_type": "any", "label": "Confirmed via" }, "assignment_type": "set", "value": ["Onboarding email"] } ], "custom_variable_def": { "custom_type": "single_link", "label": "Weblink" }, "weblink_expiration": "one_week" } }

Property Type Description Example value automation_id integer Required. ID of the automation that the weblink runs. The schema lets you save without it, but validation then reports action_automation_missing. 4023 call_arguments array of call arguments Values for the inputs that the target automation declares. Empty when left out. [] custom_variable_def object The variable that holds the generated weblink, as { "custom_type", "label" }. Both keys are required in the object. Default { "custom_type": "single_link", "label": "Weblink" }. { "custom_type": "single_link", "label": "Weblink" } weblink_expiration enum When the weblink stops working. Default never. See Expiration values. "one_week" To find automation_id, see List automations. It returns the ID of each automation as id. Each call_arguments entry has the same shape as in current_record_call_automation: variable_def (required): the input to fill, as { "custom_type", "label" }. assignment_type: set uses value (a template value), set_code uses code (a code value). Default set. id: stable ID of the entry. Tape creates one when you leave it out and returns it on read. custom_variable_def.custom_type takes one of any, single_file, multi_file, single_link, html_table_rows. The weblink is a link, so use single_link.

weblink_expiration takes one of these lower-case tokens. The editor name is in brackets. never (Never): the weblink keeps working. on_click (On click): the weblink stops working after the first click. one_day (In a day): the weblink stops working after one day. one_week (In a week): the weblink stops working after one week. one_month (In a month): the weblink stops working after one month. one_year (In a year): the weblink stops working after one year. Copying from the generate-weblink endpoint? POST /v1/automation/weblink/generate is a different surface. Its parameter is expiration_type, its tokens are upper-case (NEVER, ONE_DAY, ONE_WEEK, ONE_MONTH, ONE_YEAR), and it has no on_click (the endpoint uses expire_after_first_click for that). In this action's config, use weblink_expiration with lower-case tokens.

The action stores the weblink in the variable from custom_variable_def. A later action reads it with a custom reference that has the same custom_type and label. This send_email entry puts the link into the email body: { "type": "send_email", "config": { "to_address": ["juliet@acme.com"], "subject": ["Please confirm your start date"], "message_body": [ "

Welcome to Acme. Confirm your start date here: ", { "kind": "variable", "source": "custom", "custom_type": "single_link", "label": "Weblink" }, "

" ] } }
documents.s: Use the weblink in a later action

Otherwise validation reports action_automation_invalid. Each call_arguments label must match a custom variable of the target's trigger, with custom_variable_defs_enabled set to true. When a property listing changes, this action stamps a review note and sets the category option In review: { "type": "current_record_update", "config": { "field_assignments": [ { "field_type": "single_text", "variable_def": { "kind": "variable", "source": "field", "field_id": 4021, "field_type": "single_text", "previous": false, "collection": false, "triggering": false }, "assignment_type": "set", "field_value": ["Listing changed, review the asking price"] }, { "field_type": "single_category", "variable_def": { "kind": "variable", "source": "field", "field_id": 4022, "field_type": "single_category", "previous": false, "collection": false, "triggering": false }, "assignment_type": "set", "field_category_option_id": 2 } ], "silent": true } }

Property Type Description Example value field_assignments array of field assignments Values Tape writes into the current record, one entry per field. Empty when left out. [] author_id integer | reference User Tape attributes the change to: a user ID, or a reference to the creator, the last modifier or a user field. Left out, the automation itself is the author. { "kind": "variable", "source": "meta", "meta_type": "last_modified_by", "app_id": 87 } trigger_webhooks boolean Whether the change fires outbound webhooks. Default false. false trigger_other_flows boolean Whether the change starts other automations. Default false. false silent boolean Whether Tape sends no notifications for the change. Default false. true To find the field IDs, see App and field IDs. To find the option ID for field_category_option_id, see Retrieve a single app. It returns the options in config.settings.options of the field. author_id, trigger_webhooks, trigger_other_flows and silent are shared by every action that changes records. In the action menu of the automation editor, they are Author, Trigger webhooks, Trigger automations and Silent. To find a user ID for author_id, see Retrieve organization users.

Each entry of field_assignments sets one field of the current record. There are 20 assignment shapes, one per field type. They share these members: field_type (required): the type of the target field, for example single_text or single_category. It selects the shape of the entry. variable_def (required): a field reference to the target field, with source: "field", field_id and field_type. assignment_type: how Tape produces the value. The modes depend on the field type. A single_text entry takes set, unset or set_code. A value member that fits the mode: field_value for set on a text field, field_category_option_id for set on a category field, code for set_code. unset carries no value. code holds a JavaScript expression, for example [<reference>, ".price"]. For a text field, the expression must return text, for example ["String(", <reference>, ".price)"]. A number fails the action when the automation runs. field_value is a template value and can hold references, for example to a custom variable. id: stable ID of the entry. Tape creates one when you leave it out and returns it on read. meta/action describes the populated shape only loosely. Copy the shapes from the example above and check the live config_schema before you send filled assignments.

No key is required by the schema. Left out or [], field_assignments changes no field value. The action still logs a success step and updates the record's last_modified_on and last_modified_by. The action changes the record the run works on. To change other records, use referenced_records_update or collected_records_update. Without a trigger that has a record, validation reports the broken reason action_invalid. periodic and webhook_received have no record. Tape refuses an entry with 400 when its mode needs a value that the entry doesn't send. For example, set without field_value on a text field. Without author_id, the automation itself is the author. A user ID that Tape can't find gives the broken reason action_user_missing. Tape returns silent on every read. It's false when you left it out. Keep trigger_other_flows at false to avoid a loop when the automation triggers on record updates.
