referenced_records_update update the records related to the current record. collected_records_update update every record in a collection. Dynamic values build template values and references. Action examples configs to copy for the common actions. Actions all 35 action types.

This action reads the deal value of a sales record and stores a 3 % commission in the variable Commission: { "type": "custom_code", "config": { "code": [ "const dealValue = Number(", { "kind": "variable", "source": "field", "field_id": 601, "field_type": "number", "previous": false, "collection": false, "triggering": false }, ");\n", { "kind": "variable", "source": "custom", "custom_type": "any", "label": "Commission" }, " = Math.round(dealValue * 0.03);" ], "custom_variable_defs": [ { "custom_type": "any", "label": "Commission" } ] } }

Property Type Description Example value code code value Required. The JavaScript the action runs. String literals mixed with variable references. A plain string works too. ["const total = 1 + 1;"] custom_variable_defs array of variable declarations Custom variables this action declares. Its own code and later actions can use them. Empty when left out. [{ "custom_type": "any", "label": "Commission" }]
Each entry of custom_variable_defs needs a label and a custom_type. custom_type takes one of these lower-case tokens: any single_file multi_file single_link html_table_rows

Assign the result to a declared variable, as in the example. A later action reads it with a custom reference that has the same custom_type and label: { "kind": "variable", "source": "custom", "custom_type": "any", "label": "Commission" }
documents.s: Use the variable in a later action

documents.t: code is the only required key. code is a code value. It holds string literals and variable references only. Tape doesn't resolve template values in it. Tape runs code as a block of statements inside the automation's script. It isn't a single expression like the assignment_code of custom_variable. The write path doesn't check the syntax. A broken script saves and passes validate. The error shows up only in the run log. custom_variable_defs defaults to []. On read, Tape leaves it out when the action declares no variables. A custom reference resolves only when this action or an earlier one declares a variable with the same custom_type and label. Otherwise validation reports action_variable_missing. See Errors & broken reasons.
To add or change this action through the API, your token needs the automations:edit capability. See Capabilities. You must administer the workspace that the automation's database app belongs to.

custom_variable compute one value with a single expression. Dynamic values code values, variable references and variable declarations. Libraries Node.js libraries you can call in code without importing them. Run & simulate validate and simulate the automation before it goes live. Action examples configs to copy for the common actions. Actions all 35 action types.

This action estimates the yearly yield of a solar system from its size in kWp and stores the result in the variable Annual yield (kWh): { "type": "custom_variable", "config": { "assignment_code": [ "Math.round(Number(", { "kind": "variable", "source": "field", "field_id": 702, "field_type": "number", "previous": false, "collection": false, "triggering": false }, ") * 950)" ], "custom_variable_defs": [ { "custom_type": "any", "label": "Annual yield (kWh)" } ] } }

Property Type Description Example value assignment_code code value Required. One JavaScript expression. Tape stores its value in the declared variable. A plain string works too. ["1 + 1"] custom_variable_defs array of variable declarations The variable that receives the value. Each entry is { "custom_type", "label" }, and both keys are required. Empty when left out. [{ "custom_type": "any", "label": "Total" }]

custom_type takes one of these lower-case tokens: any single_file multi_file single_link html_table_rows Why does my action save but do nothing? With an empty or missing custom_variable_defs, this action still validates and saves. When the automation runs, Tape skips it without a per-action log, as it does with an empty assignment_code. Declare one variable so the action has a target.

Tape stores the value in the first variable of custom_variable_defs. A later action reads it with a custom reference that has the same custom_type and label: { "kind": "variable", "source": "custom", "custom_type": "any", "label": "Annual yield (kWh)" }
documents.s: Use the variable in a later action

documents.t: assignment_code is the only required key. It has no default. custom_variable_defs defaults to []. Tape evaluates assignment_code as one expression. Write 1 + 1, not return 1 + 1;. A top-level return fails when the automation runs, with Illegal return statement. To store an object literal, wrap it in parentheses: ["({ total: ", …, " })"]. Without them, JavaScript reads the braces as a block. Declare one variable per action. The action's own assignment_code can't reference the variable. The write path doesn't check the syntax. A broken expression saves and passes validate. The error shows up only in the run log. For a block of statements instead of one expression, use custom_code.

custom_code run several statements and fill more than one variable. for_loop loop over a custom variable. Dynamic values code values and custom references. Libraries Node.js libraries you can call in assignment_code. Action examples configs to copy for the common actions. Actions all 35 action types.
This action waits 30 seconds, for example to give a teammate time to finish editing a task before the next action reads it: { "type": "delay", "config": { "delay_ms": 30000 } }
Property Type Description Example value delay_ms enum (integer) Required. How long the run pauses, in milliseconds. See Delay values. 30000
delay_ms takes one of these numbers: 15000: 15 seconds. 30000: 30 seconds. 45000: 45 seconds. 60000: 60 seconds.

delay_ms is the only key, and it's required. It has no default. Tape accepts only 15000, 30000, 45000 and 60000. It rejects any other value. The run pauses for the given time, then goes on with the next action. For a longer wait, use the date_field_arrived or periodic trigger. With a trigger that has a record, Tape reloads the current record after the pause. Later actions see its latest field values.

A customer opens the weblink to confirm the installation date of their solar system. The page thanks them and shows the installation number: { "type": "display_webpage", "config": { "join_type": "replace_previous", "fullscreen": false, "remove_branding": true, "webpage_body": [ "

Thanks, your installation is confirmed

Installation ", { "kind": "variable", "source": "meta", "meta_type": "app_record_id", "app_id": 87 }, "

" ] } }

Property Type Description Example value join_type enum How this page joins a page that an earlier action displayed. Default add_below. See Join types. "add_below" fullscreen boolean Shows the page in fullscreen. Kept only when you set it. false remove_branding boolean Removes the Tape branding from the page. Kept only when you set it. true webpage_body template value HTML body of the page. Empty when left out. ["

Thanks

"] In the editor, fullscreen is Fullscreen and remove_branding is Remove Tape info.

join_type takes one of these lower-case tokens. The editor name is in brackets. add_below (Add below): adds this page below the page shown before. add_above (Add above): adds this page above the page shown before. replace_previous (New page): replaces the page shown before. Tape rejects any other value with 400.

No key is required. Tape saves the action with an empty config. Without join_type, Tape uses add_below, the same value the editor sets. Without webpage_body, the page is empty. fullscreen and remove_branding come back on read only when you set them. Without the weblink_clicked trigger, validation reports the broken reason action_invalid. References in webpage_body that don't resolve show up as broken reasons when you validate.

current_record_generate_automation_weblink create the weblink that starts this automation. redirect_user send the person to another URL instead. Dynamic values put record data into webpage_body. Triggers set up weblink_clicked. Actions all 35 action types.
Inside the else branch of a conditional, this action stops the run as failed when a job application has no CV attached: { "type": "exit", "config": { "exit_type": "failure" } }
Property Type Description Example value exit_type enum Required. How the run ends: success or failure. "success"

exit_type is the only key, and it's required. It has no default, because a successful end and a failed end mean different things. Tape stops the run at this action. Later actions don't run. success ends the run with status completed. failure ends the run with status failed and failure_reason: "exit_on_purpose". The run object tells this deliberate stop apart from an action error, which has a different failure_reason.
To add or change this action through the API, your token needs the automations:edit capability. See Capabilities. You must administer the workspace that the automation's database app belongs to.

conditional end the run only when a condition holds. Automation run read status and failure_reason of a run. Discovery read the live config shape of every action. Action examples configs to copy for the common actions. Actions all 35 action types.

An earlier action collected invoices from database app 42. This action keeps only the invoices whose Payment status is Overdue: { "type": "filter_record_collection", "config": { "record_collection": { "kind": "variable", "source": "action", "action_type": "record_collection", "app_id": 42 }, "match_condition": { "operator": "and", "rows": [ { "subject": { "kind": "variable", "source": "field", "field_id": 512, "field_type": "single_category", "previous": false, "collection": true, "triggering": false }, "operator": "is_any_of", "value": { "type": "ids", "ids": [9001] } } ] } } }

Property Type Description Example value record_collection reference Required. The collection to filter, created by an earlier action. The schema lets you save without it, but validation then reports action_invalid. { "kind": "variable", "source": "action", "action_type": "record_collection", "app_id": 42 } match_condition filter group | null The condition the records must match. An empty AND group when left out or null. { "operator": "and", "rows": [] } To find the field IDs for match_condition, see App and field IDs. To find the option IDs for ids, see Retrieve a single app. It returns them in config.settings.options of the field.

Each subject is a field of the collection's database app, scoped to the collection: "collection": true. A subject outside the collection's database app fails validation with filter_variable_missing. GET /v1/automation/meta/filter returns the operators for each field type. See Filters for the group shape and the value union.

record_collection has no default. Without it, Tape saves the action, and validation reports action_invalid. A record_collection without a matching earlier action fails validation with action_variable_missing. Without match_condition, the filter keeps every record. An empty condition reads back as null. Later actions that reference the same collection get the filtered records.

To add or change this action through the API, your token needs the automations:edit capability. See Capabilities. You must administer the workspace that the automation's database app belongs to. An earlier action in the automation must create the collection in record_collection, for example collect_app_records.

sort_record_collection put the filtered records in order. Filters the filter group used by match_condition. Dynamic values build the record_collection reference. Action examples a collect action followed by an update of the collection. Actions all 35 action types.

An earlier collect_app_records action collected the open invoices of database app 12345. The loop skips invoices with the category option Paid (9001) and emails a payment reminder for each other one: { "type": "for_loop", "config": { "iterable": { "kind": "variable", "source": "action", "action_type": "record_collection", "app_id": 12345 }, "continue_condition": { "operator": "and", "rows": [ { "subject": { "kind": "variable", "source": "field", "field_id": 512, "field_type": "single_category", "previous": false, "collection": true, "triggering": false }, "operator": "is_any_of", "value": { "type": "ids", "ids": [9001] } } ] }, "action_rows": [ { "type": "send_email", "config": { "to_address": [ { "kind": "variable", "source": "field", "field_id": 514, "field_type": "multi_email", "previous": false, "collection": true, "triggering": false } ], "subject": [ "Payment reminder for invoice ", { "kind": "variable", "source": "meta", "meta_type": "app_record_id", "collection": true, "app_id": 12345 } ], "message_body": ["

This invoice is overdue.

"] } } ] } }

Property Type Description Example value iterable reference What the loop goes through: a record_collection from an earlier collect_* action, a multi-value field or a custom variable. { "kind": "variable", "source": "action", "action_type": "record_collection", "app_id": 12345 } action_rows array of nested actions The loop body. Tape runs it once per item. Empty when left out. [{ "type": "send_email", "config": { … } }] break_condition filter group | null Stops the loop when it matches. Off when left out. { "operator": "and", "rows": [ … ] } continue_condition filter group | null Skips to the next item when it matches. Off when left out. { "operator": "and", "rows": [ … ] } To find the field IDs, see App and field IDs. To find the option IDs for ids, see Retrieve a single app. It returns them in config.settings.options of the field.

Tape loads the item. Inside the loop, references with collection: true to fields and metadata of the collection's database app point to this item. For a custom variable, a custom reference to that variable points to this item. To read one property of it, use a code value such as [<reference>, ".price"]. This works in field assignments and template values. The assignment_code of a custom_variable inside the loop body doesn't see the item yet and reads undefined. Tape checks continue_condition. When it matches, Tape skips the body and moves to the next item. Tape runs the actions in action_rows. Tape checks break_condition. When it matches, the loop stops. An item that matches break_condition still runs the body once. Then the loop stops.

No key is required. An empty config is valid, but the loop does nothing. The whole loop lives in config, like every other action. Send the collection as iterable. The internal name iterable_variable_def isn't part of the API. Leave break_condition or continue_condition out to switch it off. There are no *_enabled flags. A condition sent as null or as an empty group has no effect and reads back as null. Without iterable, Tape skips the loop when the automation runs. validate checks that iterable resolves. A reference with no matching earlier action, for example a collect_* action placed after the loop, reports action_variable_missing. validate doesn't check that the value can be looped over. A single-value field, or an action output that isn't a record_collection, passes validate and fails when the automation runs. Use only a record_collection, a multi-value field or a custom variable. An iterable that's empty or null when the automation runs gives zero iterations, without an error. A custom variable that holds an array gives one iteration per entry. Any other value gives one iteration with the whole value.

To add or change this action through the API, your token needs the automations:edit capability. See Capabilities. You must administer the workspace that the automation's database app belongs to. When iterable references a collection or custom variable, an earlier action must create it, for example collect_app_records, custom_variable or http_call.

collect_app_records create the record collection to loop over. Dynamic values references such as iterable. Filters the filter group used by break_condition and continue_condition. Action examples configs to copy for the common actions. Actions all 35 action types.

When an invoice in database app 87 is approved, this action posts the invoice number to the accounting system and saves the response: { "type": "http_call", "config": { "http_call_type": "post", "http_call_url": ["https://accounting.acme.com/api/invoices"], "http_call_headers": [ { "key": "Content-Type", "value": ["application/json"] } ], "http_call_body": ["{\"invoice\": \"", { "kind": "variable", "source": "meta", "meta_type": "app_record_id", "app_id": 87 }, "\", \"status\": \"approved\"}"], "http_call_follow_redirects": false, "custom_variable_defs": [ { "custom_type": "any", "label": "HTTP response" } ] } }

Property Type Description Example value http_call_type enum Required. HTTP method: get, post, put, patch or delete. "post" http_call_url template value Required. Request URL. ["https://accounting.acme.com/api/invoices"] http_call_body template value Request body. Empty when left out. ["{\"status\": \"approved\"}"] http_call_headers array of headers Request headers. Empty when left out. [] http_call_follow_redirects boolean Follows 3xx redirects. Default false. false custom_variable_defs array of variable declarations Variables this action declares. Empty when left out. [{ "custom_type": "any", "label": "HTTP response" }] custom_variable_defs[].custom_type takes one of any, single_file, multi_file, single_link, html_table_rows. Each declaration also needs a label.

Each entry in http_call_headers is one request header: Property Type Description Example value key string Required. Header name. "Content-Type" value template value Required. Header value. Send "" or [] for a blank value. ["application/json"] id string Stable ID of the entry. Tape creates one when you leave it out and returns it on read. "h1"

Tape stores the response body in the first variable of custom_variable_defs. A later action reads it with a custom reference that has the same custom_type and label: { "kind": "variable", "source": "custom", "custom_type": "any", "label": "HTTP response" } Without a declared variable, Tape sends the request and keeps no response. The editor declares one variable called HTTP response. A response with Content-Type: application/json arrives as parsed JSON. Any other response arrives as a string. To loop over a JSON array in the response, pass the reference as iterable of a for_loop. When the array sits inside an object, first pick it out with a custom_variable, for example [<reference>, ".items"], and loop over that variable. To branch on the response, give a conditional a filter row with code, for example { "code": [<reference>, " != null"] }. A custom reference as subject returns 400.
documents.s: Use the response in a later action

documents.t: http_call_type and http_call_url are required. Neither has a default. Every other key has a default: an empty body, no headers, no redirects and no declared variables. http_call_url, http_call_body and each header value are template values. References in them resolve when the automation runs. With an empty http_call_url, Tape skips the action when the automation runs. Outbound requests have SSRF protection. Tape refuses hosts that resolve to private or internal addresses. With http_call_follow_redirects set to false, Tape doesn't follow 3xx responses. Tape keeps only the response body, not the status code. A 4xx or 5xx response doesn't fail the action. A network error does. Tape sends http_call_body as text and adds no Content-Type. Set the header yourself, as in the example. A custom reference resolves only when its custom_type and label match a declaration in custom_variable_defs.

To add or change this action through the API, your token needs the automations:edit capability. See Capabilities. You must administer the workspace that the automation's database app belongs to. The target server accepts requests from Tape's IP addresses.

authenticated_http_call send a request through an OAuth 2.0 connection. IP addresses where requests come from and which hosts Tape refuses. for_loop loop over a list in the response. custom_variable pick one value out of the response. Dynamic values template values and custom references. Action examples the smallest http_call config to copy. Actions all 35 action types.

When a deal is won in a CRM, this action creates a kick-off task in the Tasks database app: { "type": "record_create", "config": { "app_id": 4021, "field_assignments": [ { "field_type": "single_text", "variable_def": { "kind": "variable", "source": "field", "field_id": 51207, "field_type": "single_text", "previous": false, "collection": false, "triggering": false }, "assignment_type": "set", "field_value": ["Kick-off call for deal ", { "kind": "variable", "source": "meta", "meta_type": "app_record_id", "app_id": 87 }] }, { "field_type": "single_category", "variable_def": { "kind": "variable", "source": "field", "field_id": 51208, "field_type": "single_category", "previous": false, "collection": false, "triggering": false }, "assignment_type": "set", "field_category_option_id": 3 } ], "author_id": { "kind": "variable", "source": "meta", "meta_type": "created_by", "app_id": 87 }, "trigger_other_flows": false } }

Property Type Description Example value app_id integer ID of the database app Tape creates the record in. 4021 field_assignments array of field assignments Values Tape writes into the new record, one entry per field. Left out or [], Tape creates an empty record. [] author_id integer | reference User Tape attributes the new record to: a user ID, or a reference to the creator, the last modifier or a user field. Left out, the automation itself is the author. 812 trigger_webhooks boolean Whether the new record fires outbound webhooks. Default false. false trigger_other_flows boolean Whether the new record starts other automations. Default false. false silent boolean Whether Tape sends no notifications for the new record. Default false. true To find app_id and the field IDs, see App and field IDs. To find the option ID for field_category_option_id, see Retrieve a single app. It returns the options in config.settings.options of the field. author_id, trigger_webhooks, trigger_other_flows and silent are shared by every action that changes records. In the action menu of the automation editor, they are Author, Trigger webhooks, Trigger automations and Silent. To find a user ID for author_id, see Retrieve organization users.

Each entry of field_assignments sets one field of the new record. There are 20 assignment shapes, one per field type. They share these members: field_type (required): the type of the target field, for example single_text or single_category. It selects the shape of the entry. variable_def (required): a field reference to the target field, with source: "field", field_id and field_type. assignment_type: how Tape produces the value. The modes depend on the field type. A single_text entry takes set, unset or set_code. A value member that fits the mode: field_value for set on a text field, field_category_option_id for set on a category field, code for set_code. unset carries no value. id: stable ID of the entry. Tape creates one when you leave it out and returns it on read. meta/action describes the populated shape only loosely. Copy the shapes from the example above and check the live config_schema before you send filled assignments.

A later action reads the new record with a created_record reference. With "property": "id", it returns the record ID: { "kind": "variable", "source": "action", "action_type": "created_record", "app_id": 4021, "property": "id" }
documents.s: Use the new record in a later action

documents.t: No key is required by the schema. Send app_id anyway. Without it, the action saves but creates no record. An app_id of a deleted app gives the broken reason action_app_missing. An app_id that never existed makes validate and activate return 404. Tape refuses an entry with 400 when its mode needs a value that the entry doesn't send. For example, set without field_value on a text field. Without author_id, the automation itself is the author. A user ID that Tape can't find gives the broken reason action_user_missing. Tape returns silent on every read. It's false when you left it out. Keep trigger_other_flows at false to avoid a loop when the automation triggers on the same database app.

To add or change this action through the API, your token needs the automations:edit capability. See Capabilities. You must administer the workspace that the automation's database app belongs to. The target database app must exist in your organization.

current_record_update change the record the run works on. Dynamic values build template values and references. Errors & broken reasons what each broken reason means. Action examples configs to copy for the common actions. Actions all 35 action types.

A manager opens the weblink to approve a task. This action sends the manager to a confirmation page with the task number: { "type": "redirect_user", "config": { "redirect_url": ["https://acme.com/approvals/done?task=", { "kind": "variable", "source": "meta", "meta_type": "app_record_id", "app_id": 87 }] } }
Property Type Description Example value redirect_url template value Required. The URL to send the person to. ["https://acme.com/approvals/done"]

redirect_url is the only key, and it's required. It has no default. redirect_url is a template value. References in it resolve when the automation runs. The redirect happens when the person opens the weblink and the automation reaches this action. Validation doesn't check the trigger for this action. A wrong trigger doesn't show up as a broken reason, so pick weblink_clicked yourself.

To add or change this action through the API, your token needs the automations:edit capability. See Capabilities. You must administer the workspace that the automation's database app belongs to. The automation needs the weblink_clicked trigger.

current_record_generate_automation_weblink create the weblink that starts this automation. display_webpage show a page instead of a redirect. Dynamic values put record data into redirect_url. Triggers set up weblink_clicked. Actions all 35 action types.

When a solar project changes, this action updates every related installation: { "type": "referenced_records_update", "config": { "app_id": 1044, "field_assignments": [ { "field_type": "single_text", "variable_def": { "kind": "variable", "source": "field", "field_id": 4021, "field_type": "single_text", "previous": false, "collection": false, "triggering": false }, "assignment_type": "set", "field_value": ["Permit approved"] } ], "silent": true } }

Property Type Description Example value app_id integer Required. ID of the database app that holds the related records. It must relate to the trigger's database app, in either direction. The schema lets you save without it, but validation then reports action_app_missing. 1044 field_assignments array of field assignments The values to set on each related record, one entry per field. Empty when left out. See Field assignments. [] author_id integer | reference User Tape attributes the change to: a user ID, or a reference to the creator, the last modifier or a user field. Left out, the automation itself is the author. 812 trigger_webhooks boolean Whether the change fires outbound webhooks. Default false. false trigger_other_flows boolean Whether the change starts other automations. Default false. false silent boolean Whether Tape sends no notifications for the change. Default false. true To find app_id and the field IDs, see App and field IDs. author_id, trigger_webhooks, trigger_other_flows and silent are shared by every action that changes records. In the action menu of the automation editor, they are Author, Trigger webhooks, Trigger automations and Silent. To find a user ID for author_id, see Retrieve organization users.

Each entry in field_assignments sets one field on every related record. field_type tells the 20 field-type shapes apart, for example single_text or number. variable_def is a reference to the target field. assignment_type picks how Tape produces the value. set uses field_value, set_code uses code. The unused value stays empty. meta/action describes the populated shape only loosely. Copy the shapes from current_record_update and check the live config_schema before you send filled assignments.

No key is required by the schema. Validation needs app_id. Tape updates the records in app_id that relate to the current record, in both directions. An app_id that doesn't relate to the trigger's database app fails validation with action_app_invalid. Validation doesn't check the trigger for this action. With a trigger that has no record, such as periodic, Tape skips the action when the automation runs. Left out or [], field_assignments changes no field value. The action still logs a success step for each related record. If the current record has no related records in app_id, the action does nothing and writes no step to the run log. Later actions can use the updated records as a record collection of app_id. Without author_id, the automation itself is the author. A user ID that Tape can't find gives the broken reason action_user_missing. Tape returns silent on every read. It's false when you left it out.

To add or change this action through the API, your token needs the automations:edit capability. See Capabilities. You must administer the workspace that the automation's database app belongs to. The trigger must run on a record of a database app. The database app in app_id must relate to it.

collected_records_update update every record in a collection. current_record_update update only the record the run works on. Dynamic values build references and template values. Errors & broken reasons what action_app_missing and action_app_invalid mean. Action examples configs to copy for the common actions. Actions all 35 action types.

This action adds up the amounts of all collected open invoices: { "type": "rollup_iterable_values", "config": { "rollup_type": "sum", "rollup_variable_def": { "kind": "variable", "source": "field", "field_id": 123, "field_type": "number", "collection": true, "previous": false, "triggering": false }, "custom_variable_def": { "custom_type": "any", "label": "Open invoice total" } } }

Property Type Description Example value rollup_type enum Required. The aggregation to run. See Rollup types. "sum" rollup_variable_def reference Required. The field whose values Tape aggregates, as a field reference with collection: true. An earlier collect action must put it in scope. The schema lets you save without it, but validation then reports action_variable_missing. { "kind": "variable", "source": "field", "field_id": 123, "field_type": "number", "collection": true, "previous": false, "triggering": false } custom_variable_def object The output variable that holds the result. Default { "custom_type": "any", "label": "Rollup" }. { "custom_type": "any", "label": "Open invoice total" } To find the field ID for rollup_variable_def, see App and field IDs.

rollup_type takes one of these lower-case tokens: count_all: counts all values. count_empty: counts the empty values. count_not_empty: counts the values that aren't empty. percent_empty: share of empty values, in percent. percent_not_empty: share of values that aren't empty, in percent. sum: adds up the values. average: the mean of the values. median: the median of the values. min: the smallest value. max: the largest value.

The action stores the result in the variable from custom_variable_def. A later action reads it with a custom reference that has the same custom_type and label: { "kind": "variable", "source": "custom", "custom_type": "any", "label": "Open invoice total" }
documents.s: Use the result in a later action

documents.t: rollup_type is the only key the schema requires. It has no default. Validation also needs rollup_variable_def. Without it, validation reports action_variable_missing. Leave custom_variable_def out to get the default label Rollup.

To add or change this action through the API, your token needs the automations:edit capability. See Capabilities. You must administer the workspace that the automation's database app belongs to. An earlier action in the automation must collect the records whose field you roll up.

Dynamic values build field references and use the output variable. Errors & broken reasons what action_variable_missing means. Action examples a full collect payload to start from. Actions all 35 action types.

This action tells juliet@acme.com about a new lead and puts the record ID in the subject: { "type": "send_email", "config": { "to_address": ["juliet@acme.com"], "subject": ["New record: ", { "kind": "variable", "source": "meta", "meta_type": "app_record_id", "app_id": 87 }], "message_body": ["

A new lead came in.

"], "smtp_account_id": 812 } }

Property Type Description Example value to_address template value Required. Recipient address or addresses. ["juliet@acme.com"] subject template value Required. Subject line. ["New lead"] reply_address template value Reply-to address. Empty when left out. ["sales@acme.com"] cc_address template value CC address or addresses. Empty when left out. ["romeo@acme.com"] bcc_address template value BCC address or addresses. Empty when left out. ["archive@acme.com"] from_address template value Sender address. Empty when left out. ["sales@acme.com"] from_name template value Sender display name. Empty when left out. ["Acme Sales"] message_body template value HTML body. Empty when left out. ["

Hello

"] smtp_account_id integer ID of the SMTP account to send from. Left out, Tape uses the organization's default SMTP account. See Sender address. Same ID as smtp_settings_id of the email endpoint. 812 attach_files_variable_defs array of references File variables Tape can attach: attachment or image fields, file custom variables such as the PDF from create_pdf, or the files of the trigger. Empty when left out. [] attach_files_match_type enum Which of those files Tape attaches. Default all. See Attachment modes. "all" attach_files_match_condition filter group | null Limits the attached files in the filtered and most_recent_filtered modes. An empty AND group when left out. null To find smtp_account_id, select the account in this action in the automation editor, then retrieve the automation. The API has no endpoint that lists SMTP accounts. Without the automation API, see Sender address for a way through the editor.

attach_files_match_type takes one of these lower-case tokens: all: attaches every candidate file. Ignores the condition. most_recent: attaches the most recent file. Ignores the condition. filtered: attaches the files that match attach_files_match_condition. most_recent_filtered: attaches the most recent file that matches attach_files_match_condition.

to_address and subject are the only required keys. Every other address, name and body defaults to empty. Without message_body, Tape sends the email with an empty body. Every email an automation sends counts against the organization's shared 24-hour send quota.
To add or change this action through the API, your token needs the automations:edit capability. See Capabilities. You must administer the workspace that the automation's database app belongs to.

collected_records_send_email send one email per record in a collection. create_pdf create a PDF to attach. Dynamic values build template values and references. Filters the filter group used by attach_files_match_condition. Action examples configs to copy for the common actions. Actions all 35 action types.

An earlier action collected deals from database app 42. This action sorts them by Amount, highest first, and then by Close date: { "type": "sort_record_collection", "config": { "record_collection": { "kind": "variable", "source": "action", "action_type": "record_collection", "app_id": 42 }, "sorts": [ { "variable_def": { "kind": "variable", "source": "field", "field_id": 4055, "field_type": "number", "previous": false, "collection": true, "triggering": false }, "direction": "desc" }, { "variable_def": { "kind": "variable", "source": "field", "field_id": 4061, "field_type": "single_date", "previous": false, "collection": true, "triggering": false }, "direction": "asc" } ] } }

Property Type Description Example value record_collection reference Required. The collection to sort, created by an earlier action. The schema lets you save without it, but validation then reports action_invalid. { "kind": "variable", "source": "action", "action_type": "record_collection", "app_id": 42 } sorts array of sort entries The sort order, applied in the order given. Empty when left out. [{ "variable_def": { … }, "direction": "asc" }] To find the field IDs for sorts, see App and field IDs.

Each entry in sorts is an object: Property Type Description Example value variable_def reference Required. The field or record metadata to sort by. It must belong to the collection's database app, with "collection": true. { "kind": "variable", "source": "field", "field_id": 4055, "field_type": "number", "previous": false, "collection": true, "triggering": false } direction enum Required. asc for ascending, desc for descending. "desc" id string Stable ID of the entry. Tape creates one when you leave it out and returns it on read. "sort-1" To sort by record metadata, use a meta reference with "collection": true: record ID (app_record_id), created on (created_at), created by (created_by), last modified on (last_modified_at) or last modified by (last_modified_by). For example: { "kind": "variable", "source": "meta", "meta_type": "created_at", "app_id": 42, "collection": true }.

record_collection has no default. Without it, Tape saves the action, and validation reports action_invalid. A record_collection without a matching earlier action fails validation with action_variable_missing. Without sorts, Tape stores an empty list, and the action doesn't change the order. variable_def and direction are required in every sort entry. A missing one returns 400. A sort key outside the collection's database app fails validation with action_variable_missing. A meta sort key without "collection": true, or with record_id, fails validation with action_variable_missing. Tape applies the entries in order. Each later entry breaks ties of the entries before it. Tape sorts the collection in place. Later actions that reference it get the new order.

To add or change this action through the API, your token needs the automations:edit capability. See Capabilities. You must administer the workspace that the automation's database app belongs to. An earlier action in the automation must create the collection in record_collection, for example collect_app_records.

filter_record_collection narrow the collection before you sort it. for_loop go through the sorted records one by one. Dynamic values build the record_collection reference and the sort keys. Action examples configs to copy for the common actions. Actions all 35 action types.

The Automation endpoints use the standard Tape error envelope. On this resource: Status When 400 A malformed body, a path ID that isn't an integer, or a run body that doesn't match the automation's trigger. The two Advanced / sandbox endpoints also return 400 for a missing automation or record. 401 The request carries no credential, or the credential doesn't act on behalf of a user where the endpoint needs one, for example an automation API key. 403 A personal access token or OAuth access token lacks the capability the endpoint needs. The response carries WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="insufficient_scope". See Capabilities. 404 The automation, app, workspace, revision or record isn't available to you. See The 404 collapse. Manual run and simulate also return 404 when the target record is missing or you can't view it. 409 A conflict with the automation's state: activating, running or simulating a broken automation.

Besides a malformed envelope, the input schema of a definition rejects the following when you write it: An action without a config key, or with a config that lacks a member its config_schema requires. An empty config: {} passes only for types without required members, for example current_record_update or collect_app_records. custom_code without code returns 400. A malformed dynamic-value reference: an unknown source on a kind: "variable" reference, an unknown value_type on a kind: "value" reference, or a field reference without field_type. An unknown enum value, for example an invalid assignment_type inside a field_assignments or call_arguments entry, or any config enum value that isn't one of the listed lower-case values. A filter or actions tree nested deeper than the maximum block depth. A malformed filter comparison, in the top-level filter or in a condition inside an action: a value tagged for a channel the field doesn't have, an empty comparison value, a value-arity mismatch: a value on an operator with arity none such as is_empty, or a missing value on an operator that needs one. An explicitly empty top-level filter group (rows: []). Send filter: null to run without a filter. A malformed value union in a filter condition: a payload key that belongs to a different channel than its type tag (each type branch accepts only its own keys), a relative date value with an operator or unit outside the listed values, a scalar amount (it must be a code-value array), an unknown member. Problems of meaning don't return 400 on write. Examples: a member that only validation requires, a referenced ID that doesn't exist, or an operator outside a field's channel. They show up as broken-reason codes when you validate or activate, and some only when the automation runs. One exception: an action app_id that never existed (not a deleted app) makes validate and activate return 404.
documents.s: What returns 400 in a definition body

documents.t: Tape IDs are unique across all organizations, so existence and access collapse into a single 404. An automation that is missing, soft-deleted, in another organization (not 403), in a workspace you don't administer or outside your personal access token's content access returns the same 404. The API never reveals which IDs exist.

An automation's broken_reason is { errors: [...] } or null. It's also null when broken is true because Tape marked the automation broken during a run. GET /v1/automation/{id}/validate returns { valid, errors } with the same entry shape, computed fresh. Each error entry: Property Type Description code string Machine-readable reason. See Broken-reason codes. message string English description. Not translated. deactivated boolean true when the fault is inside a deactivated block, which doesn't break the automation. false on filter and action entries in an active block. Absent on trigger entries. Treat a missing value as false: test !entry.deactivated, not === false. block_id / action_id string | null The node at fault. action_id is null for a top-level fault, for example a filter or field assignment reason. app_id / field_id / view_id / automation_id / user_id / record_id / option_id integer The referenced entity at fault, depending on code. match_type string Present for filter_match_type_invalid: the invalid filter match type. assignment_type string Present for field_assignment_type_invalid: the invalid field assignment type. call_argument string Present for action_call_argument_invalid: the ID of the invalid call argument. Why can broken lag behind the current definition? broken shows the last verdict Tape stored: create, update, activate and validate never write it, and a failed activate returns 409 with the object unchanged. Call validate for a current verdict. The automation object has the full broken model.

The codes use public names, never internal ones. Where shows where the fault sits. Description is the English message that Tape returns with the code. Code Where Description trigger_variable_missing Trigger The trigger references a variable that no longer exists. trigger_app_missing Trigger The trigger references an app that no longer exists. trigger_date_field_not_date Trigger The date-arrived trigger references a calculation field that does not produce a date. trigger_periodic_week_days_empty Trigger The weekly periodic trigger has no weekdays selected. trigger_periodic_month_days_empty Trigger The monthly periodic trigger has no days selected. trigger_updated_fields_empty Trigger The record-updated trigger has an empty list of watched fields. filter_match_type_invalid Filter A filter condition uses an operator that is not valid in this context. filter_variable_missing Filter A filter condition references a variable that no longer exists. filter_value_missing Filter Reserved. A filter condition references a value that no longer exists. No validation path returns it, see the note below. filter_value_variable_missing Filter A filter condition's value references a variable that no longer exists. filter_value_value_missing Filter A filter condition's value references a value that no longer exists. filter_user_missing Filter A filter condition references a user that no longer exists. filter_app_missing Filter A filter condition references an app that no longer exists. filter_record_missing Filter A filter condition references a record that no longer exists. filter_option_missing Filter A filter condition references a select option that no longer exists. field_assignment_type_invalid Field assignment A field assignment has an invalid type. field_assignment_end_date_disabled Field assignment A field assignment sets an end date on a field that has end dates disabled. field_assignment_variable_missing Field assignment A field assignment references a field that no longer exists. field_assignment_value_missing Field assignment A field assignment references a value that no longer exists. field_assignment_value_variable_missing Field assignment A field assignment's value references a variable that no longer exists. field_assignment_value_variable_invalid Field assignment A field assignment's value references a variable that is not valid here. field_assignment_value_value_missing Field assignment A field assignment's value references a value that no longer exists. field_assignment_user_missing Field assignment A field assignment references a user that no longer exists. field_assignment_app_missing Field assignment A field assignment references an app that no longer exists. field_assignment_record_missing Field assignment A field assignment references a record that no longer exists. field_assignment_option_missing Field assignment A field assignment references a select option that no longer exists. checklist_property_value_variable_missing Checklist property A checklist property assignment references a variable that no longer exists. checklist_property_value_value_missing Checklist property A checklist property assignment references a value that no longer exists. checklist_property_user_missing Checklist property A checklist property assignment references a user that no longer exists. action_invalid Action An action is invalid. action_variable_missing Action An action references a variable that no longer exists. action_value_missing Action An action references a value that no longer exists. action_user_missing Action An action references a user that no longer exists. action_app_missing Action An action references an app that no longer exists. action_app_invalid Action An action references an app that is not valid here. action_view_missing Action An action references an app view that no longer exists. action_automation_missing Action An action calls an automation that no longer exists. action_automation_invalid Action An action calls an automation that is not callable here. action_call_argument_invalid Action An action passes a call argument that the target automation does not accept. What about filter_value_missing? filter_value_missing is still part of the published AutomationBrokenReasonCode type, but no validation path returns it. Treat it as reserved: your code can keep handling it, but don't expect it. validate checks only meaning, and create and update already reject a malformed value with 400. A value that references a deleted field or variable returns filter_value_variable_missing. A value that resolves to empty isn't a validate fault: it matches every record when the automation runs.

Run & simulate validate an automation on demand. Automation object broken and broken_reason on the object. Filters avoid 400 with matching value tags. Automation run why a run failed, in failure_reason and error_message. Errors the error envelope and codes for the whole API.

Filter — "Priority is High AND Amount ≥ 1000" { "operator": "and", "rows": [ { "subject": { "kind": "variable", "source": "field", "field_id": 512, "field_type": "single_category", "previous": false, "collection": false, "triggering": false }, "operator": "is_any_of", "value": { "type": "ids", "ids": [9001] } }, { "subject": { "kind": "variable", "source": "field", "field_id": 513, "field_type": "number", "previous": false, "collection": false, "triggering": false }, "operator": "greater_or_equal_than", "value": { "type": "number", "number": ["1000"] } } ] } A group combines its rows, nested groups or conditions, with and (match all) or or (match any). The root group has no id. Property Type On Description id string Nested nodes Opaque node ID. Optional on input, Tape creates one when you leave it out. Present on every read. operator string Group and or or. rows array Group Nested groups and conditions. subject object Condition A reference to the value being tested: a field, record metadata, a trigger output or an action's file collection. See v1 limitations. operator string Condition One of the operators below. value object Condition The tagged comparison value, see The value union. Absent for operators without a value. code array Condition A raw code condition, a code dynamic value. A script condition has code instead of subject, operator and value. General behavior An automation without a filter has filter: null and runs every time. To run without a filter, send filter: null explicitly. An explicitly empty top-level group (rows: []) returns 400. It narrows nothing and would fire on every record. An empty group is still allowed inside an action, for example a conditional condition that is true every time, or a match_condition that keeps everything. The trigger filter already limits which records the automation runs on. Where else is this tree used? The same public tree (operator: "and" | "or", rows) appears everywhere conditions do: an automation's filter, a control-flow action's condition, break_condition and continue_condition, a condition inside an action's config, for example the match_condition of collect_app_records or filter_record_collection. All of them use the same lower-case operator and rows. See Actions.

Each operator has a value_arity: none (no value, for example is_empty), single or multiple. The valid operators differ per field type. GET /v1/automation/meta/filter?field_type=… returns the exact set. Operator Arity Operator Arity is single has_any_of multiple is_not single has_all_of multiple contains single has_none_of multiple does_not_contain single is_exactly multiple starts_with single is_any_of multiple ends_with single is_none_of multiple greater_than single has_changed_to_any_of multiple greater_or_equal_than single is_empty none less_than single is_not_empty none less_or_equal_than single is_completed none is_before single is_incomplete none is_after single has_changed none glob_pattern single has_changed_to single

glob_pattern (label Matches pattern) checks whether file names match a glob pattern, for example "*.pdf". It works only on subjects that carry files: single_attachment, multi_attachment, multi_image, an action's file collection, webhook payload files and comment attachments. Tape rejects it in collect_app_records, collect_referenced_records, collected_records_collect_referenced_records and in the search_condition of a relation field assignment.

has_changed, has_changed_to and has_changed_to_any_of compare a field with the previous revision of the record. They're valid only under a record_updated trigger, or after a current_record_get_previous_revision action on the same app. Otherwise validate reports the automation as invalid. has_changed (label Has changed) takes no value. has_changed_to (label Has changed to) works on subjects with a single choice: status, single category, single user, single relation, last modified by, and on a checklist. has_changed_to_any_of (label Has changed to any of) works on subjects with multiple choices: multi category, multi user, multi relation.

The condition value is tagged by type, so you can read it without knowing the rules for each field: type Payload Meaning text text: a template dynamic value Text or template comparison. number number: a code dynamic value Number comparison as a code expression. ids ids: array of number or reference A set of option, status, relation or user IDs. date date: { base?, operator, unit, amount } Relative date. operator is "plus" or "minus", unit is "hour", "day", "week" or "month". See Relative dates. boolean boolean Boolean comparison. Comes from a webhook payload property subject. Sends back without change. entity_type entity_type: string Comparison of the comment or reply entity type. Sends back without change. Retrieve a single app returns the option IDs for ids in config.settings.options of each field.

base is optional. Without it, Tape uses the current_date global. Tape stores it on write, so it reads back and sends back unchanged. Set a base reference to count from something other than today. operator and unit only accept the listed values. Anything else returns 400. Leave them out to keep the defaults plus and day. amount is a code dynamic value: an array of strings (for example ["1"]) or a plain string ("1", returned as ["1"]). A plain number (1) returns 400. A read returns the array form, so a retrieved definition sends back unchanged.

Tape reads a value by its tag, but writes it by field. On create and update, Tape picks the value channel from the type of the subject field: number and unique ID → number date fields → date category, status, relation and user → ids text → text On create and update: A value whose type doesn't match the field's channel returns 400. The check goes through all levels of nested groups. The response names the condition (by its id, or by its JSON path, for example filter.rows[1].rows[0]) and the tag it expected. An empty comparison value returns 400 the same way. So does an arity mismatch: a value on an operator with arity none such as is_empty, or a missing value on an operator that needs one. Existing rows aren't checked again. Definitions saved before this check, or in the automation editor in Tape, can still hold an empty comparison. An operator outside the field type's channel is not rejected if it's otherwise well-formed, for example a text operator on a number field with a number value. It passes validate and never matches when the automation runs. meta/filter returns only operators, not the accepted tag. Match the tag to the field yourself, and use only the operators it returns for the field's type. Why does my filter match every record? A value built from a reference (a field, a variable or the output of an earlier action) passes the write check, but it can resolve to empty for a record. An empty value matches everything, so under the default and group the filter matches every record. Guard such references. A simulation skips the filter, a manual run applies it.
documents.s: Match the value type to the field

documents.t: A subject needs a condition it can be tested with. On create and update, a condition's subject can be a field reference, most record metadata references (app_record_id, created_at, last_modified_at, created_by, last_modified_by), a trigger output reference (for example webhook_payload_property) or the file collection of an earlier action. All of these are writable and send back unchanged. Tokens that only carry a value and can't be tested (meta_type record_id, record_url, revision, all_comments, the raw webhook_payload) and global or custom references return 400 on write. Collection-change conditions are read-only. Has been added and Has been deleted on an attachment, image or checklist field, and Changed item contains on a checklist field, have no public operator. They read as an { id, subject } without an operator and can't be sent back unchanged. Other change-tracking conditions use the public operators has_changed, has_changed_to and has_changed_to_any_of and send back without problems. A GET followed by an unchanged PUT fails only for an automation with such a collection-change condition, so remove these conditions first. All other subjects send back unchanged, including the boolean and entity_type value kinds.

Discovery the operators for each field type. Dynamic values subjects and values as references. Actions conditions in conditional and for_loop. Revisions roll back a definition with filters. Run & simulate run one record by hand or as a simulation.

Property Type Description Example value id integer ID of the automation. 4021 app_id integer The app the automation belongs to. Only database apps can have automations. 87 workspace_id integer The workspace the app belongs to. 12 name string Name of the automation. "Email the owner on a new high-priority lead" description string Optional. Absent when the automation has none. "Notifies the record owner whenever a lead is created." paused boolean Whether the automation is paused. See Status and lifecycle. false broken boolean Whether the definition can't run. Shows the last verdict Tape stored, not your current edit. See The broken flag. false broken_reason object | null { errors: [...] } when Tape recorded reasons, otherwise null. Can be null even when broken is true, see The broken flag. The entries have the same shape as in validate. null trigger object | null The single trigger { type, config }, or null. { "type": "record_created", "config": {} } filter object | null The root filter group, or null when there is no filter. See the example above. actions array The ordered list of actions. [] when there are none. See the example above. created_at string Creation time, YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss, in your timezone. "2024-05-14 11:12:31" created_at_utc string Same instant as created_at, in UTC. "2024-05-14 09:12:31" updated_at string Last-modified time, YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss, in your timezone. "2024-05-20 18:03:08" updated_at_utc string Same instant as updated_at, in UTC. "2024-05-20 16:03:08" The object has no status field. The state is the pair paused and broken. It also has no owner or author field in this release.

broken shows the last verdict Tape stored. Create, update, activate and validate never write it, and a failed activate returns 409 with the object unchanged. So a newly saved definition that can't run still reads broken: false, and broken_reason can differ from what validate returns. Tape does set broken: true when a run finds that a valid automation stopped working, for example because: its filter can't be built anymore, a field it watches is deleted, a connection it uses is removed. Until such a run, the object still reads broken: false: activate refuses with 409, but a manual run or a simulation is accepted and fails. Once broken is true: the trigger doesn't fire the automation, a manual run or a simulation returns 409, broken_reason can be null. Call validate for a current verdict.

id, app_id and workspace_id are plain JSON integers. A revision ID is a 64-bit value, sent as a string. Node IDs inside filter and actions are opaque strings: treat them as handles, not numbers. Tape keeps an ID you send and creates a UUID when you leave it out.
Automation API concepts, capabilities and the lifecycle. Triggers the trigger block. Filters the filter block. Actions the actions block. Errors & broken reasons what broken_reason can contain.

Label is the name that meta/trigger returns. Name in Tape is the name in the automation editor. type Label Name in Tape Fires when … record_created Record created Record created A record is created in the app. record_updated Record updated Record updated A record is updated, optionally only when specific fields change. record_deleted Record deleted Record deleted A record is deleted. record_comment_or_reply_created Comment or reply created Comment added A comment or reply is added to a record. date_field_arrived Date arrived Date arrives A date from a field is reached, optionally with an offset. automation_called Automation called Automation calls Another automation calls this one. periodic Periodic On schedule A recurring schedule is due. webhook_received Webhook received Webhook received An inbound webhook comes in. weblink_clicked Weblink clicked Web link clicked Someone opens a generated weblink.

This trigger fires only when the field with ID 512 changes: Trigger { "type": "record_updated", "config": { "trigger_on_changes_field_ids": [512] } } Each type has its own config shape, described by its config_schema. Values can be dynamic where the type allows it. Which field changes fire record_updated? trigger_on_changes_field_ids has three states: null or left out: fires on a change to any field. A list with field IDs: fires only on changes to those fields. An empty []: never fires. validate reports trigger_updated_fields_empty. app_id is not a config field. Tape takes the app from the automation itself and ignores a legacy config.app_id. See Create an automation. Why does Tape reject a config field it returned? Some config fields are set by Tape and read-only, for example the webhook_url of a webhook_received trigger. They appear when you read a config, and Tape rejects them on write. The config_schema marks them with "readOnly": true (standard JSON Schema), so remove them before you send a config. What are the _enabled flags for? Some config values only take effect when a boolean next to them, <field>_enabled, is true. The automation_called and weblink_clicked triggers pair triggering_app_ids with triggering_app_ids_enabled, and custom_variable_defs with custom_variable_defs_enabled. A minimal {} config is accepted, because all members are optional. Send the paired _enabled flag whenever you set its value.

To set or replace a trigger, use PUT /v1/automation/{automation_id}/trigger, where the whole body is the trigger. Or include trigger when you create or update an automation. To remove a trigger, send trigger: null in an update.

Discovery read the config_schema of each trigger. Dynamic values the outputs a trigger hands to the run. Run & simulate the run body each trigger expects. Advanced / sandbox fire automation_called and weblink_clicked. Actions which actions need which trigger.
Use this endpoint to list the full history of an automation. GET/v1/automation/{automation_id}/revisionapi.tapeapp.com
Use this endpoint to read one revision of an automation. GET/v1/automation/{automation_id}/revision/{revision_id}api.tapeapp.com

A revision is a read snapshot. Its envelope is wider than the update body accepts, so a PUT of the whole revision fails with 400. The first revision in the list is the current state. Pausing and activating add revisions too. Pick the revision whose filter and actions you want back. Send back only its definition members: name, trigger, filter and actions. The PUT needs automations:edit. Then validate the automation: an older definition can point to fields that no longer exist. The envelope keys id, automation_id, created_at, created_at_utc, paused and broken aren't writable. The update body rejects unknown keys. A filter or action condition with a collection-change condition (Has been added, Has been deleted or Changed item contains) has no writable form. Remove it first. See Filters. Conditions with has_changed, has_changed_to and has_changed_to_any_of are writable. So are conditions on fields, record metadata, trigger outputs and action outputs. The server-assigned webhook_url of a webhook_received trigger is on the live automation object, but not in a revision. It never causes a 400 on rollback. Why doesn't a rollback restore the description? A revision has no description. description keeps its current value, so reset it separately if you need to revert it too.

A revision is a snapshot of the automation's definition at one edit. idstring The revision ID, a 64-bit value returned as a string. Example value "90071992547409929" automation_idinteger The automation this revision belongs to. Example value 4021 created_atstring When the revision was created, YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss, in your timezone. Example value "2024-05-20 18:03:08" created_at_utcstring Same instant as created_at, in UTC. Example value "2024-05-20 16:03:08" namestring The name at this revision. Example value "Email the owner on a new high-priority lead" paused / brokenboolean The state at this revision. Example value false triggerobject | null The trigger at this revision. Example value { "type": "record_created", "config": {} } filterobject | null The filter at this revision. Example value null actionsarray The actions at this revision. Example value [] A revision has fewer fields than the automation object. It has no description, broken_reason, updated_at, app_id or workspace_id.

An automation ID that isn't an integer returns 400. A credential that doesn't act on behalf of a user, for example an automation API key, returns 401. A token without automations:read returns 403. An automation or revision that isn't available to you returns 404. A revision_id that is unknown, malformed or belongs to another automation returns the same 404. See Errors & broken reasons for the Automation API and Errors for all error codes.
Manage send a revision's definition back with update. Filters which conditions can't be written back. Automation object the full live object.
Use this endpoint to send an email to one or more recipients. POST/v1/email/sendapi.tapeapp.com

attachment_ids accepts these file IDs: files in attachment or image fields of records. See Attachment field value. files you uploaded with the File resource. files attached to record comments or replies. You need access to every file you attach.

Without your own email server, Tape sends from noreply@automations.tapeapp.com. If you set reply_to, Tape sends from reply@automations.tapeapp.com. Set from_name to show your own sender name. To send from your own address, add an SMTP account in the Send an email action of an automation: Open an automation and add the action Send an email. Select Show more, open the Account menu and select Add account. On the SMTP tab, enter the user name, password, server address and port, then select Save account. To make the account the default of your organization, open the Account menu, select the three dots next to the account and select Set as default. Tape then sends through your organization's default SMTP account. To pick another one, set smtp_settings_id. The API has no endpoint that lists SMTP accounts, and the Account menu doesn't show the ID. To find it in the automation editor: In a Send an email action, select the account in the Account menu. In the action menu, select Duplicate. In the action menu of the copy, select Turn into → Execute script. The script shows the ID in smtp_settings_id. Remove the copy. The automation API returns the same ID as smtp_account_id of the action. Set the sender address in from_address. Without it, Tape uses the user name of the SMTP server. Your SMTP server must be allowed to send emails for this address. Otherwise, delivery fails. The example sends an email from juliet@acme.com to two recipients, with two people in copy. It attaches the file with ID 42, a file in an attachment field of a record. cURL JSON Request curl -X POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/email/send \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ --data '{ "from_address": "juliet@acme.com", "from_name": "Juliet from Acme", "to": ["riley@acme.com", "sam@acme.com"], "subject": "Offer for 12 Harbor Street", "html": "

The signed offer is attached.

", "cc": ["will@acme.com", "nora@acme.com"], "attachment_ids": [42] }' Request { "from_address": "juliet@acme.com", "from_name": "Juliet from Acme", "to": ["riley@acme.com", "sam@acme.com"], "subject": "Offer for 12 Harbor Street", "html": "

The signed offer is attached.

", "cc": ["will@acme.com", "nora@acme.com"], "attachment_ids": [42] } Response { "status": "SUCCESSFULLY_SCHEDULED" }
Tape enforces these limits for each email: Maximum total attachment size 20 MB

Sending an email costs the base request cost of 10 credits, whatever the number of recipients in to, cc and bcc. One email to several recipients uses fewer credits than separate emails to each of them. Recipients in to and cc see each other. Put recipients in bcc if they shouldn't, and check that your choice fits your privacy policy.

Each field value has a type and a field_type. The type is the kind of data returned, like text, category or phone. The field_type is the exact type of the field, like single_text or multi_phone. The field type table lists all values. The field_type says whether a field holds one value or several values. A single_category field value never has more than one option. Switching a field from single_category to multi_category converts the field and all its values. Read-only field values Tape computes the values of calculation, unique_id, created_on, created_by, last_modified_on and last_modified_by fields. You can't write them. calculation and unique_id values appear in the fields of a record. Tape ignores them in create and update requests. created_on, created_by, last_modified_on and last_modified_by values don't appear in fields. Read them from the record properties of the same name. A unique_id value holds the number of the record within its app and the formatted ID: Unique ID field value object { "field_id": 7, "external_id": "deal_id", "label": "Deal ID", "type": "unique_id", "field_type": "unique_id", "values": [{ "value": 12, "formatted": "DEAL-0012" }] } value is the number of the record within its app, the same number as the record's app_record_id. formatted adds the prefix, the suffix and the leading zeros from the field settings.

Use the create record endpoint and the update record endpoint to write field values. Request { "fields": { "first_name": "Juliet", "2": "

Called about the solar roof offer.

" } } General behavior Send the values in the fields object. Use the field ID or the field's slug (returned as external_id in records) as the key. Find the app ID, field IDs and slugs in the app's Developer window, see Find the app ID and field IDs, or in the fields of Retrieve a single app. Each field type accepts its own input formats. See Formats by field type. When you create a record, send a value for every required field ("required": true in the field's config). A missing value returns 400. In an update, fields that aren't in the request keep their values. To clear a value, send null. Some field types also accept an empty value. Clearing a required field returns 400 for these field types: multi_text, single_category, multi_category, single_date, range_date, single_user, multi_user, single_attachment, multi_attachment, multi_image, single_location and status. You can't clear a status value at all. Tape doesn't stop you from clearing a required field of the types single_text, number, single_relation, multi_relation, checklist, multi_email, multi_link and multi_phone in an update. Send a value instead. A new record still needs a value for them. A cleared field isn't in the fields of the response. Requirements: records:edit to write field values, records:read to read them. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key. The token from the Quickstart only reads records.

Its examples read your token from $TAPE_TOKEN and use example IDs like 1. Replace them with your own. Know the field only by its name in Tape, like Member or Files? The API reads and writes the script in its stored form. In the stored form, every reference to a field is a token: @[Display name](variable_name) The variable name in parentheses holds the field IDs and says which field Tape reads. The display name in square brackets only labels the token. In Tape, the calculation editor shows these tokens as JavaScript names, for example Price or Tasks.Title.all. Tape converts between both forms when the editor opens and saves the script.
documents.s: Writing scripts for calculation fields via the API

documents.t: To reference a field of the same app, use its field ID. Find it in the Developer view of the app. @[Field name](field_<field ID>) The example references a number field "Price" with ID 1: @[Price](field_1) The calculation editor shows this as Price. Spaces in field names become underscores, so "Living Area" shows as Living_Area. For a Date field with an end date, add _start_date or _end_date, for example @[Sprint](field_5_end_date). The calculation editor shows Sprint.start and Sprint.end. To reference the ID of the record, use @[Record ID](meta_recordId). The calculation editor shows Record_ID. Relation fields can't be referenced with field_. Use the tokens below to read the related records.
documents.s: Referencing fields of the same app as the calculation field

documents.t: If the app has a relation field (single_relation or multi_relation), the script can read fields of the related records. These tokens carry two IDs: first the field on the related records, then the relation field. The examples use a projects app with the calculation field. Its relation field "Tasks" (ID 654) links each project to task records. The tasks app has a field "Title" (ID 123) and a field "Hours" (ID 321). Referencing a single field of all related records​ To get the values of one field of all related records, use: @[All of Field name](out_<field ID>_<relation field ID>) The example gets the titles of all tasks of the project: @[All of Title](out_123_654) The token becomes an array with the values. Records without a value are left out. The calculation editor shows this as Tasks.Title.all. A script that ends with the array itself stores no value. Turn it into text or a number first, for example with .join(", ") or .length. Referencing a single field of all related records with nulls​ To keep the records without a value, use: @[All of Field name with nulls](outn_<field ID>_<relation field ID>) The example gets the titles of all tasks, with null for tasks without a title: @[All of Title with nulls](outn_123_654) The token becomes an array with one entry per related record. The calculation editor shows this as Tasks.Title.allWithNull. Referencing a single field of all relating records​ Relating records are records of another database app whose relation field points to this record. For these tokens, the relation field ID is the ID of the relation field in the other app. In the example, the tasks app has a relation field "Project" (ID 655) that links each task to a project. In the projects app, the script gets the titles of all tasks that link to the project: @[All of Title](in_123_655) The token becomes an array with the values. Records without a value are left out. The calculation editor names the namespace after the other app and shows this as Tasks.Title.all. Referencing a single field of all relating records with nulls​ To keep the relating records without a value, use inn_: @[All of Title with nulls](inn_123_655) The token becomes an array with one entry per relating record, with null for records without a value. The calculation editor shows this as Tasks.Title.allWithNull. Referencing a number field of all related records (incoming or outgoing)​ For number fields, a token can return the sum, the average, the minimum or the maximum of all values instead of an array. Add the aggregation after out_ or in_: Sum Outgoing relation @[Sum of Hours](out_sum_321_654) Incoming relation @[Sum of Hours](in_sum_321_655) Calculation editor Tasks.Hours.sum Average Outgoing relation @[Average of Hours](out_avg_321_654) Incoming relation @[Average of Hours](in_avg_321_655) Calculation editor Tasks.Hours.avg Minimum Outgoing relation @[Minimum of Hours](out_min_321_654) Incoming relation @[Minimum of Hours](in_min_321_655) Calculation editor Tasks.Hours.min Maximum Outgoing relation @[Maximum of Hours](out_max_321_654) Incoming relation @[Maximum of Hours](in_max_321_655) Calculation editor Tasks.Hours.max Date fields support the minimum and the maximum. Tokens with nulls (outn_, inn_) don't take an aggregation. An aggregation on another field type, for example out_sum_ on a text field, returns 500 with unknown. The example script returns the hours of all tasks of the project as text: @[Sum of Hours](out_sum_321_654) + " hours"

You can't create calculation fields together with a new app. Create the app first. Then add the calculation fields with an app update. Find the app ID and the field IDs in the Developer view of the app. General behavior Tape runs the script with sample values to work out return_type. Here, the script returns a number. Tape computes the values of the existing records in the background. A new calculation field doesn't trigger webhooks or automations. Set trigger_webhooks or trigger_automations to true to change that. In a field update, leaving them out keeps their values. An empty script or a script that fails to run doesn't fail the request. Tape saves the field and marks it as invalid. A new calculation field doesn't show its description as help text yet (show_description is false). To show it, send the description again in a field update. A field with field_id updates that field. In a field update, a script you leave out stays as it is. Send always_hidden, hidden_if_empty and description with every field you update. Tape sets left-out switches to false and hides the help text without description. See Create and update fields. Fields that aren't in the request stay unchanged. Requirements: apps:edit, and Full access to the app. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key. Errors Every field you update needs config.label, even if the label stays the same. Without it, Tape rejects the request with 400 and input_validation. The message reads, for example, Invalid input: data/fields/0/config must have required property 'label'. A return_type that doesn't match the result of the script returns 400 with the message inferred result type from script execution does not match provided return type. A script that references fields that don't exist, or calculation fields that reference each other in a loop, returns 400.
