Find the app ID and the field IDs in the Developer view of the app. Find the option IDs in config.settings.options of the field, for example with Retrieve a single app. General behavior A field with field_id updates that field. A field without field_id creates a new field and needs a field_type. An option with id changes that option. To rename it, send its id with the new text. An option without id creates a new option. Options you leave out of options stay unchanged. To set a new order, send all existing options in that order. An option you send without the other options moves to the end of the list, also when you only rename it. To keep the order, send all options in the order you want. To delete options, list their IDs in settings.options_to_delete, for example "options_to_delete": [{ "id": 4 }]. Tape also accepts plain IDs: [4]. An option that is also in options stays. Without layout, the field keeps its layout. Send required, always_hidden and hidden_if_empty with every field you update. Tape sets left-out switches to false. show_description stays as it is, with or without description. See Create and update fields. Fields that aren't in the request stay unchanged. Requirements: apps:edit, and Full access to the app. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key. All field types share these properties: Property Type Description Example value field_id number ID of the field. 2 slug string Identifier of the field within its app. Tape creates it from the label when you create the field. Renaming the field keeps the slug. Use the field ID or the slug as the key of a field value in record requests. Records return the slug as external_id. "notes" external_id string Deprecated. Same as slug, kept for backwards compatibility. Use slug. "notes" label string Name of the field in Tape. "Notes" type string Kind of data the field holds. See Field type. "text" field_type string Exact type of the field. See Field type. "multi_text" config.label string Name of the field. Required when you create or update a field. "Notes" config.slug string Same as slug. "notes" config.external_id string Deprecated. Same as slug, kept for backwards compatibility. Use slug. "notes" config.description string Help text of the field. "Notes about the contact." config.show_description (read-only) boolean Whether Tape shows the description as help text inside the record. true config.required boolean Whether a record needs a value for this field. You can still clear single_text, number, relation, checklist, email, link and phone fields in an update. false config.hidden_if_empty boolean Whether Tape hides the field inside the record when it has no value. false config.always_hidden boolean Whether Tape hides the field inside the record, even when it has a value. false config.primary boolean Whether the field is the primary field of the app. The value of the primary field names a record wherever Tape refers to it. Any field type can be the primary field. An app has at most one primary field, and some apps have none. false config.settings object Settings of the field type. The structure depends on field_type. See the page of each field type. { "formatted": true, "format": "html" }

Each field has a field_type and a type. The field_type is the exact type of the field. The type is the kind of data it holds, so several field types share one type. For field types that can hold one value or several values, the prefix of the field_type says which: single_category holds one option, multi_category holds several. A single_category field value never has more than one option. Switching a field from single_category to multi_category converts the field and all its values. field_type Field in Tape type single_text Single line text text multi_text Multi line text text single_category Single select category multi_category Multiple select category status Status category single_date Date date range_date Date with an end date date number Number number calculation Calculation calculation single_relation Relation to one record app multi_relation Relation to several records app single_user Member, one member contact multi_user Member, several members contact single_attachment Files, one file file multi_attachment Files, several files file multi_image Image file multi_email Email email multi_phone Phone phone multi_link Link embed checklist Task list checklist single_location Location location unique_id Unique ID unique_id created_on Created on created_at created_by Created by created_by last_modified_on Last edited on last_modified_at last_modified_by Last edited by last_modified_by When you create a field, send one of these values as field_type. Tape rejects any other value with 400. Tape fills calculation, unique_id, created_on, created_by, last_modified_on and last_modified_by fields. You can create and configure these fields, but you can't write their values.

Find the Tape field type for each Podio field type. The Podio external_id of a field is the slug in Tape. Podio field type Tape field_type Note text single_text, multi_text multi_text holds rich text (HTML). number number money number No money type. The currency is the field's unit, not part of the value. duration number No duration type. Store the duration as a number, for example in seconds. progress number No progress type. Store 0 to 100, for example with the unit %. category single_category, multi_category, status date single_date, range_date contact single_user, multi_user Users of your organization only, guests included. Keep external contacts without a Tape account as records and link them with a relation field. app (app reference) single_relation, multi_relation image multi_image embed multi_link location single_location calculation calculation Read-only. phone (tel) multi_phone email multi_email Files of an item single_attachment, multi_attachment A record has no file list of its own. Add an attachment field. The type keeps the Podio names app, contact and embed. New in Tape: status, checklist, unique_id and the fields for creation and last edit.

Use the create app endpoint to create fields together with a new app. Use the update app endpoint to create new fields in an app, change existing fields or delete fields with fields_to_delete. The page of each field type has a full example. Find the workspace ID, the app ID and the field IDs in the Developer view of the app. To change the order of the fields, use Update an app's field order. General behavior A field with field_id updates that field. A field without field_id creates a new field and needs a field_type. Every field you update needs config.label, even if the label stays the same. Send required, always_hidden and hidden_if_empty with every field update. Tape sets the ones you leave out to false. A Status field is the exception: without required, it stays required. A new single_text or multi_text field with a description shows it as help text. A new field of another type starts with show_description set to false. Send description with every field update to show the help text or keep it visible. Without description, Tape sets show_description to false. Single select, Multiple select and Status fields keep their show_description as it is in both cases. To change one property, read the field first with Retrieve a single app and send back what you keep. A relation field without settings loses its linked apps. Without primary, Tape makes the first field of a new app the primary field. It skips unique_id, created_on, created_by, last_modified_on and last_modified_by fields, unless the request has only fields of these types. Adding fields to an app that has fields leaves its primary field unchanged. Set primary to true to make a field the primary field. The field that was the primary field before loses the role. In a field update, leaving out primary keeps the primary field as it is. Fields that aren't in the request stay unchanged. Requirements: apps:edit. Creating an app needs a workspace role that may edit apps in the workspace, updating one needs Full access to the app. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key. Errors A field update without config.label returns 400 with input_validation and a message such as Invalid input: data/fields/0/config must have required property 'label'. A field update without config returns 400 with validation. A request that sets primary to true on more than one field returns 400. A field update that sets primary to false on the primary field, without a new primary field, returns 400. An app with a primary field keeps one.

Tape tries to create thumbnail images in several sizes for each uploaded file. Use them for profile pictures, file previews and similar places: small: JPG, 100px wide and 100px high medium: JPG, 200px wide and 200px high large: JPG in the original width and height of the image An example thumbnail object: { "small": "https://s3.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com/tape-thumbnails/def09e9319ca30e9ab2bc13e061982", "medium": "https://s3.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com/tape-thumbnails/82f3c2669deca95c16d1ad955734e0", "large": "https://s3.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com/tape-thumbnails/f8f105f4daaced0f3f714b5ebb76ae" }
Tape enforces these limits for all upload endpoints: Maximum file size 100MB

The credits of an upload depend on the file size, added up over all files of a request. An upload costs at least 2x the credits of a normal request. A file of 50MB costs 3x credits, a file of 100MB costs 4x credits: Uploading 1KB: 2x credits Uploading 50MB: 3x credits Uploading 100MB: 4x credits Uploading 150MB: 5x credits Uploading 200MB: 6x credits Uploading 300MB: 8x credits ... Uploading several files in one request costs fewer credits than uploading each file on its own.

Tape returns a detailed error message for most failed uploads. No file provided validation error { "status_code": 400, "endpoint": "/v1/file/upload", "error_code": "validation", "error_message": "No file provided to upload endpoint via multipart/form-data field name: 'file'" }

Attachment field value attach an uploaded file to a record. Record comment attach an uploaded file to a comment. Email send an uploaded file as an email attachment. Request limits how credits work. Capabilities what records:edit allows.

Send your filters as an array in filters. A record matches only if it matches every filter (AND). There is no OR. Each field filter is a JSON object with these keys: Property Type Description Example value field_id integer or string ID of the field to filter on. Required. The slug (external_id) returns a 400. "1" field_type string Type of the field, for example single_text, status or single_date. Required for view filters. Optional for filtered records, where field_id identifies the field, but send it anyway. "single_text" type string Legacy data type that goes with the field type, for example text, status or date. Required. A filter without it returns a 400. "text" match_type string The operator, for example contains, equal or before. Each section below lists the operators a field type accepts. "contains" values array The operands, as { "value": … } objects. Leave it out for empty and not_empty. [{ "value": "John" }] Some field types accept more optional keys, for example for relative dates, weekdays, the "@me" flag or task list entries. See Operand keys. This example matches all records whose field 1 contains the text "John" and whose status field 2 is set to option 123: JSON Combined filter { "filters": [ { "field_id": "1", "field_type": "single_text", "match_type": "contains", "values": [{ "value": "John" }], "type": "text" }, { "field_id": "2", "field_type": "status", "match_type": "equal", "values": [{ "value": 123 }], "type": "status" } ] } Send this body to POST /v1/record/filter/app/{app_id}. Every field in a record or in Retrieve a single app carries its field_id and field_type. Category and status fields list their option IDs there, in config.settings.options. Sort and page in the query string with sort_by, sort_desc, limit and cursor, see Pagination. To filter by creation date, last change or record number without a field, use the metadata filters.

Use this filter for Single line text fields (single_text). JSON Single text filter { "filters": [ { "field_id": "1", "field_type": "single_text", "match_type": "contains", "values": [{ "value": "John" }], "type": "text" } ] } General behavior contains, not_contains, starts_with and ends_with ignore case. equal and not_equal are exact matches and case-sensitive. Every operator trims leading and trailing whitespace from the match value. empty and not_empty take no values. Match types Match type Description equal Matches all records whose field value is equal to the match value. not_equal Matches all records whose field value is not equal to the match value. contains Matches all records whose field value contains the match value. not_contains Matches all records whose field value does not contain the match value. starts_with Matches all records whose field value starts with the match value. ends_with Matches all records whose field value ends with the match value. empty Matches all records whose field value is empty. not_empty Matches all records whose field value is not empty.

Use this filter for Multi line text fields (multi_text). JSON Multi text filter { "filters": [ { "field_id": "1", "field_type": "multi_text", "match_type": "contains", "values": [{ "value": "John" }], "type": "text" } ] } General behavior The filter matches against the unformatted (plain text) value of the field. contains, not_contains, starts_with and ends_with ignore case. equal and not_equal are exact matches and case-sensitive. Every operator trims leading and trailing whitespace. empty and not_empty take no values. Match types Match type Description equal Matches all records whose unformatted field value is equal to the match value. not_equal Matches all records whose unformatted field value is not equal to the match value. contains Matches all records whose unformatted field value contains the match value. not_contains Matches all records whose unformatted field value does not contain the match value. starts_with Matches all records whose unformatted field value starts with the match value. ends_with Matches all records whose unformatted field value ends with the match value. empty Matches all records whose field value is empty. not_empty Matches all records whose field value is not empty.

Use this filter for Number fields (number). JSON Number filter { "filters": [ { "field_id": "1", "field_type": "number", "match_type": "smaller", "values": [{ "value": 12.34 }], "type": "number" } ] } Send the number to compare against as a bare numeric value in values[0].value. Leave out values for empty and not_empty. Match types Match type Description equal Matches all records whose field value is equal to the provided match value. not_equal Matches all records whose field value is not equal to the provided match value. smaller Matches all records whose field value is smaller than the provided match value. smaller_or_equal Matches all records whose field value is smaller than or equal to the match value. larger Matches all records whose field value is larger than the provided match value. larger_or_equal Matches all records whose field value is larger than or equal to the match value. empty Matches all records whose field value is empty. not_empty Matches all records whose field value is not empty.

Use this filter for Unique ID fields (unique_id). JSON Unique ID filter { "filters": [ { "field_id": "1", "field_type": "unique_id", "match_type": "larger_or_equal", "values": [{ "value": 1000 }], "type": "number" } ] } A Unique ID field shows the record number Tape counts up per database app. This is the record's app_record_id: the first record in a database app is 1, the second 2, and so on. General behavior Send the match value as a bare number without a prefix. The filter compares the underlying number, so type is "number", not "unique_id". Leave out values for empty and not_empty. Every record has a record number. empty matches no records, and not_empty matches every record. Your database app has no Unique ID field? Use the app_record_id metadata filter. It filters on the same number without a field. Match types The match types are the same as for number: Match type Description equal Matches the record whose number is equal to the provided match value. not_equal Matches all records whose number is not equal to the provided match value. smaller Matches all records whose number is smaller than the provided match value. smaller_or_equal Matches all records whose number is smaller than or equal to the provided match value. larger Matches all records whose number is larger than the provided match value. larger_or_equal Matches all records whose number is larger than or equal to the provided match value. empty Matches no records, because every record has a number. not_empty Matches every record.

Use this filter for Single select fields (single_category). JSON Single category filter { "filters": [ { "field_id": "1", "field_type": "single_category", "match_type": "any", "values": [{ "value": 1 }, { "value": "Not Started" }], "type": "category" } ] } General behavior Send the numeric ID of an option or its label as the match value. Label matching ignores case and leading and trailing whitespace. A label that matches more than one option returns an error. Use the option ID instead. equal takes exactly one option. More than one returns a 400. Use any for several options. When you read the filter back, operands come as option IDs. empty and not_empty take no values. Match types Match type Description equal Matches all records whose field value references the option specified. not_equal Matches all records whose field value does not reference the option specified. any Matches all records whose field value references any of the options specified. none Matches all records whose field value references none of the options specified. empty Matches all records whose field value is empty. not_empty Matches all records whose field value is not empty.

Use this filter for Multiple select fields (multi_category). JSON Multi category filter { "filters": [ { "field_id": "1", "field_type": "multi_category", "match_type": "contains", "values": [{ "value": 1 }, { "value": "Not Started" }], "type": "category" } ] } A multi_category field holds a set of options, so the match types compare sets: equal needs exactly the given options. Order doesn't matter. contains needs all given options. The field may hold more. any and none test for overlap with the given options. General behavior Send the numeric ID of an option or its label. Label matching ignores case and leading and trailing whitespace. An ambiguous label returns an error. Use the option ID instead. When you read the filter back, operands come as option IDs. empty and not_empty take no values. Match types Match type Description equal Matches all records whose field value references exactly the options specified and no others. contains Matches all records whose field value references all of the options specified (and may reference more). any Matches all records whose field value references at least one of the options specified. none Matches all records whose field value references none of the options specified. empty Matches all records whose field value is empty. not_empty Matches all records whose field value is not empty.

Use this filter for Status fields (status). JSON Status filter { "filters": [ { "field_id": "1", "field_type": "status", "match_type": "any", "values": [{ "value": 1 }, { "value": "Not Started" }], "type": "status" } ] } General behavior Send the numeric ID of a status option or its label. Label matching ignores case and leading and trailing whitespace. An ambiguous label returns an error. Use the option ID instead. When you read the filter back, operands come as option IDs. completed, incomplete, empty and not_empty take no values. completed and incomplete test whether the status option the record has is marked as completed. Match types Match type Description equal Matches all records whose field value references the status option specified. not_equal Matches all records whose field value does not reference the status option specified. any Matches all records whose field value references any of the status options specified. none Matches all records whose field value references none of the status options specified. empty Matches all records whose field value is empty. not_empty Matches all records whose field value is not empty. completed Matches all records whose referenced status option is marked as completed. incomplete Matches all records whose referenced status option is not marked as completed.

Use this filter for Relation fields that hold one record (single_relation). JSON Single relation filter { "filters": [ { "field_id": "1", "field_type": "single_relation", "match_type": "any", "values": [{ "value": 1 }], "type": "app" } ] } Send the IDs of the related records as match values. When you read the filter back, operands come as record IDs. empty and not_empty take no values. Match types Match type Description equal Matches all records whose field value references the record specified. not_equal Matches all records whose field value does not reference the record specified. any Matches all records whose field value references any of the records specified. none Matches all records whose field value references none of the records specified. empty Matches all records whose field value is empty. not_empty Matches all records whose field value is not empty.

Use this filter for Relation fields that hold several records (multi_relation). JSON Multi relation filter { "filters": [ { "field_id": "1", "field_type": "multi_relation", "match_type": "contains", "values": [{ "value": 1 }, { "value": 2 }], "type": "app" } ] } A multi_relation field holds a set of related records, so the match types compare sets: equal needs exactly the given records. Order doesn't matter. contains needs all given records. The field may hold more. any and none test for overlap. Send the IDs of the related records as match values. When you read the filter back, operands come as record IDs. empty and not_empty take no values. Match types Match type Description equal Matches all records whose field value references exactly the records specified and no others. contains Matches all records whose field value references all of the records specified (and may reference more). any Matches all records whose field value references at least one of the records specified. none Matches all records whose field value references none of the records specified. empty Matches all records whose field value is empty. not_empty Matches all records whose field value is not empty.

Use this filter for Member fields that hold one member (single_user). JSON Single user filter { "filters": [ { "field_id": "1", "field_type": "single_user", "match_type": "any", "values": [{ "value": 1 }], "type": "contact" } ] } General behavior Send the user IDs to filter by. Retrieve organization users lists them. To add yourself, set include_active_user (the "@me" reference). See Operand keys. When you read the filter back, operands come as user IDs. empty and not_empty take no values and don't work with include_active_user. Match types Match type Description equal Matches all records whose field value references the user specified. not_equal Matches all records whose field value does not reference the user specified. any Matches all records whose field value references any of the users specified. none Matches all records whose field value references none of the users specified. empty Matches all records whose field value is empty. not_empty Matches all records whose field value is not empty.

Use this filter for Member fields that hold several members (multi_user). JSON Multi user filter { "filters": [ { "field_id": "1", "field_type": "multi_user", "match_type": "contains", "values": [{ "value": 1 }, { "value": 2 }], "type": "contact" } ] } A multi_user field holds a set of users, so the match types compare sets: equal needs exactly the given users. Order doesn't matter. contains needs all given users. The field may hold more. any and none test for overlap. General behavior Send the user IDs to filter by. To add yourself, set include_active_user (the "@me" reference). See Operand keys. When you read the filter back, operands come as user IDs. empty and not_empty take no values and don't work with include_active_user. Match types Match type Description equal Matches all records whose field value references exactly the users specified and no others. contains Matches all records whose field value references all of the users specified (and may reference more). any Matches all records whose field value references at least one of the users specified. none Matches all records whose field value references none of the users specified. empty Matches all records whose field value is empty. not_empty Matches all records whose field value is not empty.

Use this filter for Created by fields (created_by). The field holds the user who created the record. JSON Created by filter { "filters": [ { "field_id": "1", "field_type": "created_by", "match_type": "any", "values": [{ "value": 1 }], "type": "contact" } ] } General behavior Send the user IDs to filter by. To add yourself, set include_active_user (the "@me" reference). See Operand keys. any with include_active_user selects the records you created. When you read the filter back, operands come as user IDs. The type is contact, as for a user field. It's not created_by. empty and not_empty take no values and don't work with include_active_user. Match types Match type Description equal Matches all records created by the user specified. not_equal Matches all records not created by the user specified. any Matches all records created by any of the users specified. none Matches all records created by none of the users specified. empty Matches all records whose field value is empty. not_empty Matches all records whose field value is not empty.

Use this filter for Last edited by fields (last_modified_by). The field holds the user who last changed the record. JSON Last modified by filter { "filters": [ { "field_id": "1", "field_type": "last_modified_by", "match_type": "any", "values": [{ "value": 1 }], "type": "contact" } ] } General behavior Send the user IDs to filter by. To add yourself, set include_active_user (the "@me" reference). See Operand keys. any with include_active_user selects the records you changed last. When you read the filter back, operands come as user IDs. The type is contact, as for a user field. It's not last_modified_by. empty and not_empty take no values and don't work with include_active_user. Match types Match type Description equal Matches all records last modified by the user specified. not_equal Matches all records not last modified by the user specified. any Matches all records last modified by any of the users specified. none Matches all records last modified by none of the users specified. empty Matches all records whose field value is empty. not_empty Matches all records whose field value is not empty.

Use this filter for Date fields with one date (single_date). JSON Single date filter { "filters": [ { "field_id": "1", "field_type": "single_date", "match_type": "before", "relative_date_type": "exact_date", "values": [{ "value": { "date": "2020-01-01T00:00:00.000Z" } }], "type": "date" } ] } Put the target date in the nested values[0].value.date as an ISO 8601 string. A bare value (values[0].value: "2020-01-01") also works on input, but a GET returns the nested form, which you can send back unchanged. Leave out values for empty and not_empty. Tape resolves the date to match from values[0].value.date, the relative_date_type and, for the num_days_*, num_weeks_* and num_months_* types, values[0].value.offset_amount. For example, num_days_before with an offset of 1 and a date of 2020-01-01 resolves to 2019-12-31. today, tomorrow and yesterday need no value (all values). Four operators select a period instead of a single day. Each reads its own operand key (values under Operand keys): within pairs with relative_date_range_type and matches a named or bounded range, for example current_week, past_num_days or exact_range. For exact_range, send the start in values[0].value.date and the end in the top-level end_date. For next_num_days and past_num_days, send the count in offset_amount. on_weekday pairs with weekday (monday to sunday). in_quarter_of_year pairs with quarter_of_year (q1 to q4). in_month_of_year pairs with month_of_year (january to december). Does a date filter include the target day? Tape expands the date to a full day, from start of day to end of day in your timezone. The time of day in the value doesn't count. So not all boundary operators include the day: before matches strictly before the start of the target day. The day itself is excluded. after matches strictly after the end of the target day. The day itself is excluded. on_or_before includes the whole day up to its end. on_or_after includes the whole day from its start. equal matches the whole target day. not_equal matches everything outside it. Match types Match type Description equal Matches all records whose field date falls on the target day. not_equal Matches all records whose field date does not fall on the target day. before Matches all records whose field date is before the start of the target day (day excluded). on_or_before Matches all records whose field date is on or before the target day (whole day included). after Matches all records whose field date is after the end of the target day (day excluded). on_or_after Matches all records whose field date is on or after the target day (whole day included). within Matches all records whose field date falls within the range selected by relative_date_range_type. on_weekday Matches all records whose field date falls on the supplied weekday. in_quarter_of_year Matches all records whose field date falls in the supplied quarter_of_year. in_month_of_year Matches all records whose field date falls in the supplied month_of_year. empty Matches all records whose field value is empty. not_empty Matches all records whose field value is not empty.

Use this filter for Date fields with a start and an end date (range_date). JSON Range date filter { "filters": [ { "field_id": "1", "field_type": "range_date", "match_type": "within", "relative_date_range_type": "exact_range", "values": [{ "value": { "date": "2020-01-01T00:00:00.000Z" } }], "end_date": "2020-12-31T00:00:00.000Z", "type": "date" } ] } The field stores a start and an end date. Operands and operand keys are the same as for Single date. Leave out values for empty and not_empty. The typical combination is within with relative_date_range_type: "exact_range". It tests the stored range against a window from values[0].value.date (start) to the top-level end_date (end). How do range operators compare dates? Tape expands each date to a full day, from start of day to end of day in your timezone. The time of day doesn't count. Each operator then tests the stored [start, end] interval against the target day or window: equal and within match any range that overlaps it, not only ranges that equal it or sit inside it. before, after, on_or_before and on_or_after compare the ends of the range with the day boundary. Match types Match type Description equal Matches all records whose range overlaps the target day. not_equal Matches all records whose range does not overlap the target day. before Matches all records whose range starts before the start of the target day. on_or_before Matches all records whose range falls on or before the target day. after Matches all records whose range falls after the end of the target day. on_or_after Matches all records whose range falls on or after the target day. within Matches all records whose range overlaps the range selected by relative_date_range_type. on_weekday Matches all records whose range falls on the supplied weekday. in_quarter_of_year Matches all records whose range falls in the supplied quarter_of_year. in_month_of_year Matches all records whose range falls in the supplied month_of_year. empty Matches all records whose field value is empty. not_empty Matches all records whose field value is not empty.

Use this filter for Created on fields (created_on). It filters by the creation date of the record. Your database app has no Created on field? Use the created_at metadata filter. It works in every database app, with or without the field. JSON Created at filter { "filters": [ { "field_id": "1", "field_type": "created_on", "match_type": "on_or_after", "relative_date_type": "exact_date", "values": [{ "value": { "date": "2020-01-01T00:00:00.000Z" } }], "type": "date" } ] } The field_type is created_on, and the type is date. Operands, operators and operand keys are the same as for Single date. Leave out values for empty and not_empty. Need exact timestamps? Tape ignores the time of day and expands the date to a full day in your timezone. before and after exclude that day, on_or_before and on_or_after include it. The created_at metadata filter compares exact timestamps and includes the bound for all four operators. Match types Match type Description equal Matches all records whose creation date falls on the target day. not_equal Matches all records whose creation date does not fall on the target day. before Matches all records created before the start of the target day (day excluded). on_or_before Matches all records created on or before the target day (whole day included). after Matches all records created after the end of the target day (day excluded). on_or_after Matches all records created on or after the target day (whole day included). within Matches all records whose creation date falls within the range selected by relative_date_range_type. on_weekday Matches all records whose creation date falls on the supplied weekday. in_quarter_of_year Matches all records whose creation date falls in the supplied quarter_of_year. in_month_of_year Matches all records whose creation date falls in the supplied month_of_year. empty Matches all records with no creation date. not_empty Matches all records that have a creation date.

Use this filter for Last edited on fields (last_modified_on). It filters by the date of the last change to the record. Your database app has no Last edited on field? Use the last_modified_at metadata filter. It works in every database app, with or without the field. JSON Last modified at filter { "filters": [ { "field_id": "1", "field_type": "last_modified_on", "match_type": "on_or_after", "relative_date_type": "num_weeks_before", "values": [{ "value": { "offset_amount": 1 } }], "type": "date" } ] } The field_type is last_modified_on, and the type is date. In the example, num_weeks_before with offset_amount: 1 resolves to one week ago. Operands, operators and operand keys are the same as for Single date. Leave out values for empty and not_empty. Need exact timestamps? Tape ignores the time of day and expands the date to a full day in your timezone. before and after exclude that day, on_or_before and on_or_after include it. The last_modified_at metadata filter compares exact timestamps and includes the bound for all four operators. Match types Match type Description equal Matches all records whose last-modified date falls on the target day. not_equal Matches all records whose last-modified date does not fall on the target day. before Matches all records last modified before the start of the target day (day excluded). on_or_before Matches all records last modified on or before the target day (whole day included). after Matches all records last modified after the end of the target day (day excluded). on_or_after Matches all records last modified on or after the target day (whole day included). within Matches all records whose last-modified date falls within the range selected by relative_date_range_type. on_weekday Matches all records whose last-modified date falls on the supplied weekday. in_quarter_of_year Matches all records whose last-modified date falls in the supplied quarter_of_year. in_month_of_year Matches all records whose last-modified date falls in the supplied month_of_year. empty Matches all records with no last-modified date. not_empty Matches all records that have a last-modified date.

Use this filter for Calculation fields (calculation). JSON Calculation filter { "filters": [ { "field_id": "1", "field_type": "calculation", "match_type": "smaller", "values": [{ "value": 12.34 }], "type": "calculation" } ] } A calculation field returns a text, a number or a date, depending on its script. The result type decides which match types make sense. Send the same operand as for the matching field type: Number result: use the number operators with a bare number in values[0].value, as for a Number field. Text result: use the text operators with a string in values[0].value, as for a Single text field. Date result: use the date operators with the nested values[0].value.date (with optional offset_amount) and the date operand keys, as for a Single date field (see Operand keys). General behavior empty and not_empty work for every result type. Leave out values. within, on_weekday, in_quarter_of_year and in_month_of_year work only when the calculation returns a date. The relative dates today, tomorrow and yesterday work only when the calculation returns a date. Using a date-only operator on a text or number calculation returns a 400. A text operator on a number calculation, for example contains, returns a 500 with unknown. The date comparisons before, after, on_or_before and on_or_after can do the same. Use only the operators of the result type. Match types The table lists the match types of all result types together. Match type Applies to Description empty any Matches all records whose field value is empty. not_empty any Matches all records whose field value is not empty. equal number, text, date Matches all records whose field value is equal to the provided match value (day-granular for a date result). not_equal number, text, date Matches all records whose field value is not equal to the provided match value. smaller number Matches all records whose field value is smaller than the provided match value. smaller_or_equal number Matches all records whose field value is smaller than or equal to the match value. larger number Matches all records whose field value is larger than the provided match value. larger_or_equal number Matches all records whose field value is larger than or equal to the match value. contains text Matches all records whose field value contains the provided match value. not_contains text Matches all records whose field value does not contain the provided match value. starts_with text Matches all records whose field value starts with the provided match value. ends_with text Matches all records whose field value ends with the provided match value. before date Matches all records whose field date is before the start of the target day (day excluded). on_or_before date Matches all records whose field date is on or before the target day (whole day included). after date Matches all records whose field date is after the end of the target day (day excluded). on_or_after date Matches all records whose field date is on or after the target day (whole day included). within date Matches all records whose field date falls within the range selected by relative_date_range_type. on_weekday date Matches all records whose field date falls on the supplied weekday. in_quarter_of_year date Matches all records whose field date falls in the supplied quarter_of_year. in_month_of_year date Matches all records whose field date falls in the supplied month_of_year.

Use this filter for Email fields (multi_email). JSON Multi email filter { "filters": [ { "field_id": "1", "field_type": "multi_email", "match_type": "fully_includes", "values": [{ "value": "juliet@acme.com" }], "type": "email" } ] } General behavior An email field can hold several addresses. A record matches when at least one address meets the condition. not_contains matches when no address contains the value. empty matches when there are no addresses. Matching ignores case and leading and trailing whitespace in the match value. Match types Match type Description fully_includes Matches records that have at least one email entry equal to the match value in full. contains Matches records that have at least one email entry containing the match value. not_contains Matches records where none of the email entries contain the match value. starts_with Matches records that have at least one email entry starting with the match value. ends_with Matches records that have at least one email entry ending with the match value. empty Matches records whose field value is empty (no email entries). Omit values. not_empty Matches records whose field value is not empty (at least one email entry). Omit values.

Use this filter for Phone fields (multi_phone). JSON Multi phone filter { "filters": [ { "field_id": "1", "field_type": "multi_phone", "match_type": "starts_with", "values": [{ "value": "+49" }], "type": "phone" } ] } General behavior A phone field can hold several numbers. A record matches when at least one number meets the condition. not_contains matches when no number contains the value. empty matches when there are no numbers. Matching ignores case and leading and trailing whitespace in the match value. Match types Match type Description fully_includes Matches records that have at least one phone entry equal to the match value in full. contains Matches records that have at least one phone entry containing the match value. not_contains Matches records where none of the phone entries contain the match value. starts_with Matches records that have at least one phone entry starting with the match value. ends_with Matches records that have at least one phone entry ending with the match value. empty Matches records whose field value is empty (no phone entries). Omit values. not_empty Matches records whose field value is not empty (at least one phone entry). Omit values.

Use this filter for Link fields (multi_link). JSON Multi link filter { "filters": [ { "field_id": "1", "field_type": "multi_link", "match_type": "contains", "values": [{ "value": "github.com" }], "type": "embed" } ] } General behavior The type for a link field is embed, not link. A link field can hold several links. The filter matches the URL of each link and ignores case and surrounding whitespace. A record matches when at least one URL meets the condition. Link fields have no exact match. equal and fully_includes return a 400. Use contains, starts_with or ends_with instead. Match types Match type Description contains Matches records that have at least one link whose URL contains the match value. not_contains Matches records where none of the link URLs contain the match value. starts_with Matches records that have at least one link whose URL starts with the match value. ends_with Matches records that have at least one link whose URL ends with the match value. empty Matches records whose field value is empty (no links). Omit values. not_empty Matches records whose field value is not empty (at least one link). Omit values.

Use this filter for Location fields (single_location). JSON Single location filter { "filters": [ { "field_id": "1", "field_type": "single_location", "match_type": "contains", "values": [{ "value": "Berlin" }], "type": "location" } ] } General behavior The filter matches free text in the formatted address. This is street address, postal code, city, state, country and the original formatted address, joined together. You can't filter on a single part, such as the city or the country alone. Matching ignores case and leading and trailing whitespace in the match value. Match types Match type Description contains Matches records whose formatted address contains the match value. not_contains Matches records whose formatted address does not contain the match value (records with no address set also match). empty Matches records whose field value is empty (no address set). A coordinate-only value counts as not empty. Omit values. not_empty Matches records whose field value is not empty (an address or coordinates are set). Omit values.

Use this filter for Files fields that hold one file (single_attachment). JSON Single attachment filter { "filters": [ { "field_id": "1", "field_type": "single_attachment", "match_type": "contains", "values": [{ "value": "invoice" }], "type": "file" } ] } General behavior The type for an attachment field is file. The filter matches the file name, never the file ID. Send the match value as a string. Matching ignores case and leading and trailing whitespace in the match value. Match types Match type Description equal Matches records whose attached file name equals the match value. not_equal Matches records whose attached file name does not equal the match value. contains Matches records whose attached file name contains the match value. not_contains Matches records whose attached file name does not contain the match value. starts_with Matches records whose attached file name starts with the match value. ends_with Matches records whose attached file name ends with the match value. empty Matches records with no file attached. Omit values. not_empty Matches records with a file attached. Omit values.

Use this filter for Files fields that hold several files (multi_attachment). JSON Multi attachment filter { "filters": [ { "field_id": "1", "field_type": "multi_attachment", "match_type": "contains", "values": [{ "value": "invoice" }], "type": "file" } ] } General behavior As for Single attachment, the type is file and the filter matches file names. Send a string. The field can hold several files, so every match type checks all of them. equal and not_equal compare the match value with each file name exactly. Match types Match type Description equal Matches records where at least one attached file name equals the match value. not_equal Matches records where no attached file name equals the match value (records with no attachments also match). contains Matches records where an attached file name contains the match value. not_contains Matches records where none of the attached file names contain the match value. starts_with Matches records where at least one attached file name starts with the match value. ends_with Matches records where at least one attached file name ends with the match value. empty Matches records with no files attached. Omit values. not_empty Matches records with at least one file attached. Omit values.

Use this filter for Image fields (multi_image). JSON Multi image filter { "filters": [ { "field_id": "1", "field_type": "multi_image", "match_type": "ends_with", "values": [{ "value": ".png" }], "type": "file" } ] } General behavior Image fields share the type file with attachment fields. field_type tells them apart. The filter matches the image file name. Send a string. The field can hold several images, so every match type checks all of them. equal and not_equal compare the match value with each file name exactly. Matching ignores case and leading and trailing whitespace in the match value. Match types Match type Description equal Matches records where at least one image file name equals the match value. not_equal Matches records where no image file name equals the match value (records with no images also match). contains Matches records where an image file name contains the match value. not_contains Matches records where none of the image file names contain the match value. starts_with Matches records where at least one image file name starts with the match value. ends_with Matches records where at least one image file name ends with the match value. empty Matches records with no images. Omit values. not_empty Matches records with at least one image. Omit values.

Use this filter for Task list fields (checklist). Choose the entry property to filter on with entry_property: title, assignee, status or due_date. JSON Task list filter { "filters": [ { "field_id": "1", "field_type": "checklist", "entry_property": "title", "match_type": "contains", "values": [{ "value": "Design review" }], "type": "checklist" } ] } A task list holds entries (subtasks in Tape). Each entry has a title, an optional assignee, a completion status and an optional due date. Every match type checks all entries: title with contains matches a record when any entry title contains the value. Without entry_property, the filter applies to the whole field and supports only empty and not_empty: the task list has no entries, or at least one entry. The type is checklist for every task list filter. This table shows the match types and the operand for each entry_property. Any other combination returns a 400. entry_property Allowed match_type Operand (omitted) empty, not_empty none, leave out values title contains, not_contains, empty, not_empty values: [{ "value": "<text>" }] (a string); leave out values for empty / not_empty assignee equal, not_equal, empty, not_empty values: [{ "value": <user_id> }, …] (one or more user IDs) and/or include_active_user: true; leave out values for empty / not_empty status equal values: [{ "value": <boolean> }]: true = completed, false = incomplete due_date equal, not_equal, empty, not_empty, before, after, on_or_before, on_or_after, within a date operand, see Operand keys; leave out values for empty / not_empty General behavior status uses a boolean, not a match type. The Status field uses the match types completed and incomplete. A task list status filter uses match_type: "equal" with a boolean: false for incomplete entries, true for completed entries. include_active_user works only for the assignee. Use the "@me" flag include_active_user: true only with entry_property: "assignee", and only with equal or not_equal, not with empty or not_empty. See Operand keys. due_date has no exact_range. within needs a relative_date_range_type. Unlike date fields, task lists don't support exact_range, because there is no exact end date to store. Use a bounded range such as next_num_days or current_week. Example: incomplete entries (status with a boolean value) JSON Task list filter: incomplete entries { "filters": [ { "field_id": "1", "field_type": "checklist", "entry_property": "status", "match_type": "equal", "values": [{ "value": false }], "type": "checklist" } ] } Example: due within the next 7 days (due_date with within and a relative range) JSON Task list filter: due within the next 7 days { "filters": [ { "field_id": "1", "field_type": "checklist", "entry_property": "due_date", "match_type": "within", "relative_date_range_type": "next_num_days", "values": [{ "value": { "offset_amount": 7 } }], "type": "checklist" } ] } Example: assigned to me (assignee with include_active_user) JSON Task list filter: assigned to me { "filters": [ { "field_id": "1", "field_type": "checklist", "entry_property": "assignee", "match_type": "equal", "include_active_user": true, "type": "checklist" } ] } Match types Match type Valid entry_property Description equal assignee, status, due_date An entry matches the operand: assigned to the given user / completion equals the boolean / due date equals the date. not_equal assignee, due_date Negation of equal. contains title An entry title contains the match value. not_contains title No entry title contains the match value. empty (omitted), title, assignee, due_date Field level: the task list has no entries. Entry level: the title, assignee or due date of an entry is empty. Omit values. not_empty (omitted), title, assignee, due_date Complement of empty. Omit values. before due_date An entry's due date is before the resolved date. after due_date An entry's due date is after the resolved date. on_or_before due_date An entry's due date is on or before the resolved date. on_or_after due_date An entry's due date is on or after the resolved date. within due_date An entry's due date falls within the given range. Requires relative_date_range_type.

Operand keys are optional properties next to values that refine the condition. Most apply to date filters: Single date, Range date, Created at, Last modified at, calculations that return a date, and task list due_date filters. Use each key only with the field types listed below. Tape ignores a key that doesn't fit, without an error: weekday on a text filter changes nothing. Where does offset_amount go? All operand keys below are top-level properties of the filter object, except offset_amount. It goes inside the value at values[0].value.offset_amount. At the top level, Tape ignores it, so a num_days_before filter with only a top-level offset_amount returns a 400. Operand key Where it goes Applies to Used with relative_date_type top-level date filters, checklist due_date resolves the target date for a comparison relative_date_range_type top-level date filters, checklist due_date match_type: within end_date top-level date filters within with relative_date_range_type: exact_range weekday top-level date filters match_type: on_weekday quarter_of_year top-level date filters match_type: in_quarter_of_year month_of_year top-level date filters match_type: in_month_of_year include_active_user top-level user filters, checklist assignee boolean "@me" flag entry_property top-level checklist selects the entry sub-property offset_amount nested in values[0].value date filters, checklist due_date the num_* / next_num_days / past_num_days types

Resolves a comparison (equal, before, after, on_or_before, on_or_after and so on) to a single date. Supported values: relative_date_type Value to provide Meaning today, tomorrow, yesterday none the corresponding day exact_date values[0].value.date (ISO-8601 string) an absolute calendar date num_days_before, num_days_after values[0].value.offset_amount (integer) N days before / after num_weeks_before, num_weeks_after values[0].value.offset_amount (integer) N weeks before / after num_months_before, num_months_after values[0].value.offset_amount (integer) N months before / after General behavior For single_date and range_date fields, Tape applies the num_* offset to the date in values[0].value.date. For created_on, last_modified_on and task list due_date filters, Tape applies the offset to the current date and ignores any date you send. exact_date accepts only an ISO 8601 string. A numeric epoch doesn't work. end_date accepts an epoch number.

Selects a date range for match_type: within. Supported values: relative_date_range_type Value to provide current_week, current_month, current_year, past_week, past_month, past_year, next_week, next_month, next_year none next_num_days, past_num_days values[0].value.offset_amount (integer) exact_range values[0].value.date (start) and end_date (end) exact_range works only on date fields. Task list due_date filters support every value except exact_range.
The end of the range for a within filter with exact_range on a date field. Send an ISO date string or an epoch number. The start of the range comes from values[0].value.date.
One of monday, tuesday, wednesday, thursday, friday, saturday, sunday. Use it with match_type: on_weekday on date fields to match records whose date falls on this weekday.
One of q1, q2, q3, q4. Use it with match_type: in_quarter_of_year on date fields.
One of january, february, march, april, may, june, july, august, september, october, november, december. Use it with match_type: in_month_of_year on date fields.

A boolean "@me" flag for the user your credential belongs to. Set include_active_user: true to match that user without a fixed user ID. It works with user filters (single_user, multi_user, created_by, last_modified_by) and with task list assignee filters. For a task list, it works only with entry_property: "assignee" and only with equal or not_equal, not with empty or not_empty. You can combine it with user IDs in values.

Only for task lists: the entry property the filter applies to (title, assignee, status or due_date). Without it, the filter applies to the whole field and supports only empty and not_empty (see Checklist).

An integer inside the value object at values[0].value.offset_amount, not a top-level key. It gives the count for the num_days_*, num_weeks_* and num_months_* relative date types and for the next_num_days and past_num_days range types.

Metadata filters match properties every record has, so they need no field in the database app. Set only type and leave out field_id and field_type: type Filters on Match value created_at When the record was created nested, { "date": "…" } last_modified_at When the record was last modified nested, { "date": "…" } app_record_id The app-specific ID of the record (the app_record_id property) bare value, for example 123 Put metadata filters in the same filters array as field filters. They combine with the same AND. Where does the timestamp match value go? created_at and last_modified_at read the match value from values[0].value.date, a nested object. Field filters and app_record_id use a bare value at values[0].value.

Use this filter to find records by creation time, without a Created on field in the database app. JSON Created at metadata filter: bounded window { "filters": [ { "type": "created_at", "match_type": "on_or_after", "values": [{ "value": { "date": "2026-07-01T00:00:00.000Z" } }] }, { "type": "created_at", "match_type": "on_or_before", "values": [{ "value": { "date": "2026-07-02T00:00:00.000Z" } }] } ] } General behavior Absolute UTC dates only. Send a full ISO 8601 timestamp as value.date. Leave out relative_date_type or set it to exact_date. A relative value such as num_days_before or num_weeks_after returns a 400. Tape accepts offset_amount but ignores it. Don't rely on it. All bounds are inclusive. Every match type compares with >= or <=. after works like on_or_after, and before like on_or_before. Use two filters for a window: one lower bound and one upper bound, as in the example. Repeating a bound in the same direction narrows the window: the latest lower bound and the earliest upper bound win. It never widens it. Invalid input returns a 400 instead of being dropped: an unsupported match_type, a missing or unreadable date, or a year outside 1 to 9999. Match types Match type Description after, on_or_after, larger, larger_or_equal Matches records created on or after the value. before, on_or_before, smaller, smaller_or_equal Matches records created on or before the value. Any other match type (equal, empty, not_empty and so on) returns a 400. For a database app with a Created on field, see Created at.

Use this filter to find records by the time of their last change. It works like Created at (metadata) in every respect: same match types, inclusive bounds, absolute dates only and the same 400 behavior. Use type: "last_modified_at". JSON Last modified at metadata filter { "filters": [ { "type": "last_modified_at", "match_type": "on_or_after", "values": [{ "value": { "date": "2026-07-01T00:00:00.000Z" } }] } ] } Why don't unedited records match? A record nobody edited after creating it has no last-modified timestamp, so no last_modified_at filter matches it. To get everything created or modified since a point in time, merge two requests as in Pattern: incremental sync.

Use this filter to find records by their app-specific ID. This is the sequential app_record_id every record returns: the first record in a database app is 1, the second 2, and so on. JSON App record ID metadata filter { "filters": [ { "type": "app_record_id", "match_type": "larger_or_equal", "values": [{ "value": 1000 }] } ] } General behavior The match value is a bare value at values[0].value, not a nested object. The value must be a number. A missing or non-numeric value returns a 400 for every match type, including empty and not_empty. Any match type not in the table returns a 400. Every record has an app_record_id. empty matches nothing, and not_empty matches every record. Match types Match type Description equal Matches the record whose app_record_id equals the value. not_equal Matches all records whose app_record_id does not equal the value. larger Matches all records whose app_record_id is larger than the value. larger_or_equal Matches all records whose app_record_id is larger than or equal to the value. smaller Matches all records whose app_record_id is smaller than the value. smaller_or_equal Matches all records whose app_record_id is smaller than or equal to the value. empty Matches no records, because every record has an app_record_id. not_empty Matches every record.

Use the timestamp metadata filters to get only the records that changed since your last run. You don't need Created on or Last edited on fields. Filters have no OR, so "created or modified since T" takes two requests: Created since T Modified since T Request 1: records created since T { "filters": [ { "type": "created_at", "match_type": "on_or_after", "values": [{ "value": { "date": "2026-07-22T00:00:00.000Z" } }] } ] } Request 2: records modified since T { "filters": [ { "type": "last_modified_at", "match_type": "on_or_after", "values": [{ "value": { "date": "2026-07-22T00:00:00.000Z" } }] } ] } Merge the results and remove duplicates by record_id. Request 2 misses records nobody edited after creation. Request 1 catches them. Why does my sync return fewer records now? Earlier, the API accepted the created_at and last_modified_at metadata filters but ignored them and returned all records. Now it applies them, so an integration that relied on the old behavior gets fewer records.

Record send your filters and get the records that match. View store filters in a view. Field value the value format of every field type. Date & timezone how the API reads and returns dates. Search find records by text in any field, across all your database apps or only in some (app_ids). Capabilities what records:read and apps:edit allow.

A graphic icon is an icon provided by Tape. Its id identifies it. Tape supports most icons of Google's Material Design icon library. To find the ID of an icon there, select the icon, select Android and copy the ID from the text field. For example, hourglass_empty is the icon of an hourglass. An id Tape doesn't support returns 400 with validation. Send this object to set a graphic icon: Icon { "id": "hourglass_empty", "type": "graphic" } Property Type Description Example value type string "graphic" for a graphic icon. "graphic" id string ID of the icon in the Material Design icon library. "hourglass_empty"

An emoji icon is a Unicode emoji. Its emoji property identifies it. Send this object to set an emoji icon, here the telephone receiver emoji (U+1F4DE). The example writes it as a JSON escape. You can also send the emoji character itself. Icon { "emoji": "\ud83d\udcde", "type": "emoji" } Property Type Description Example value type string "emoji" for an emoji icon. "emoji" emoji string The emoji, as a JSON escape or as the character itself. "\ud83d\udcde" Can I send a string instead of an object? Yes. Tape reads an emoji as an emoji icon and any other text as the id of a graphic icon.

App set the icon when you create or update an app. Workspace set the icon when you create or update a workspace. Record read the icon of a record's app in app.icon, as a plain string instead of an icon object.
Use this endpoint to get the name, plan and other details of your organization. GET/v1/orgapi.tapeapp.com

User list and search the users of your organization. Workspace list the workspaces of your organization. Date & timezone how Tape formats created_on and created_on_utc. Capabilities what organization:read allows.

A record holds the field values of one entry in a database app. Retrieve a record returns the full object: Record { "record_id": 1, "app_record_id": 1, "record_url": "https://tapeapp.com/acme/record/1", "app_id": 1, "app": { "app_id": 1, "name": "Contacts", "record_name": "Contact", "workspace_id": 1, "workspace": { "workspace_id": 1, "name": "CRM", "external_id": "crm", "org_id": 1 }, "icon": "event_available" }, "title": "Clara Weber", "created_on": "2022-03-01 12:00:00", "created_on_utc": "2022-03-01 11:00:00", "last_modified_on": "2022-03-02 09:30:00", "last_modified_on_utc": "2022-03-02 08:30:00", "deleted_on": null, "deleted_on_utc": null, "created_by": { "type": "user", "id": 600, "user_id": 600, "org_id": 1, "mail": ["juliet@acme.com"], "email": "juliet@acme.com", "name": "Juliet Adams" }, "last_modified_by": { "type": "user", "id": 600, "user_id": 600, "org_id": 1, "mail": ["juliet@acme.com"], "email": "juliet@acme.com", "name": "Juliet Adams" }, "fields": [ { "field_id": 1, "external_id": "full_name", "label": "Full Name", "type": "text", "field_type": "single_text", "values": [ { "value": "Clara Weber" } ] } ], "current_revision": { "type": "update", "revision": 1, "record_id": 1, "created_on": "2022-03-02 09:30:00", "created_on_utc": "2022-03-02 08:30:00", "created_by": { "type": "user", "id": 600, "user_id": 600, "org_id": 1, "mail": ["juliet@acme.com"], "name": "Juliet Adams" } }, "initial_revision": { "type": "creation", "revision": 0, "record_id": 1, "created_on": "2022-03-01 12:00:00", "created_on_utc": "2022-03-01 11:00:00", "created_by": { "type": "user", "id": 600, "user_id": 600, "org_id": 1, "mail": ["juliet@acme.com"], "name": "Juliet Adams" } } } The example is shortened: it leaves out app.config and revisions. It comes from a user whose timezone is one hour ahead of UTC. List endpoints, such as Retrieve records for an app, return the same object without revisions and with comment_count. record_idnumber The record ID. Unique across all apps. Example value 1 app_record_idnumber The running number of the record in its database app. Example value 1 record_urlstring Link to the record in Tape. Example value "https://tapeapp.com/acme/record/1" app_idnumber The database app the record belongs to. Example value 1 appobject Preview of the database app: app_id, name, record_name, workspace_id, workspace, icon, plus a legacy config copy of all of them except app_id. Example value { "app_id": 1, "name": "Contacts", … } titlestring The computed title of the record. May be missing. Example value "Clara Weber" created_onstring | null When the record was created, as YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss in your timezone. See Date & timezone. Example value "2022-03-01 12:00:00" created_on_utcstring | null The same moment as created_on, in UTC. Example value "2022-03-01 11:00:00" last_modified_onstring | null When the record last changed, in your timezone. Example value "2022-03-02 09:30:00" last_modified_on_utcstring | null The same moment as last_modified_on, in UTC. Example value "2022-03-02 08:30:00" deleted_onstring | null When the record was deleted, in your timezone. null unless the record is in the trash. Example value null deleted_on_utcstring | null The same moment as deleted_on, in UTC. Example value null created_byobject | null The author who created the record. See Authors. Example value { "type": "user", "id": 600, … } last_modified_byobject | null The author who last changed the record. See Authors. Example value { "type": "user", "id": 600, … } fieldsarray The field values of the record. A field without a value isn't listed. See Field values. Example value [{ "field_id": 1, "values": [ … ] }] current_revisionobject | null The latest revision of the record. See Record revision. Example value { "type": "update", "revision": 1, … } initial_revisionobject | null The first revision of the record. Example value { "type": "creation", "revision": 0, … } revisionsarray The latest revisions of the record. Only in responses about one record. To read all revisions, use Record revision. Example value [{ "type": "update", … }] comment_countnumber Number of comments on the record, without replies. Only in list responses. Example value 2

created_by and last_modified_by hold one of three kinds of author. Check type to know which one you have. "user" A user. user_id is the same as id. Properties id, user_id, org_id, mail, email, name, and phone if set "workflow" An automation. automation_id is the same as id. workflow_id is deprecated. Properties id, automation_id, workflow_id, mail, name "share_session" A visitor who changed the record through a share link. Only in last_modified_by. share_session_id is a UUID string, mail is empty, and name is a generated label that isn't unique. Properties share_session_id, mail, name Create a record​ Use this endpoint to create a record in a database app. POST/v1/record/app/{app_id}api.tapeapp.com cURL JSON Request curl -X POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/app/1 \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ --data '{ "fields": { "full_name": "Clara Weber" } }' Request { "fields": { "full_name": "Clara Weber" } } Response { "record_id": 1, "app_id": 1, "title": "Clara Weber", "created_on": "2022-03-01 12:00:00", "fields": [ { "field_id": 1, "external_id": "full_name", "label": "Full Name", "type": "text", "field_type": "single_text", "values": [ { "value": "Clara Weber" } ] } ] } Before you start Open the database app in Tape, select ••• (Follow, export and more…) at the top, then select Developer. The window shows the App ID and, for every field, its Field ID and External ID (the field's slug). See Find the app ID and field IDs. Use a token with the capabilities Read records and Edit records (records:read, records:edit). The token from the Quickstart only reads records. Capabilities can't be added to a token later, so create a new token with every capability you need, for example Edit comments to comment on records. Prefer the API? Retrieve all available apps returns every app_id. Retrieve a single app returns every field with its field_id and slug. Both need apps:read. Don't see Developer? You need Full access to the app. Send the field values in the fields object, one key per field. Use the field ID or the field's slug (returned as external_id in records) as the key. The response has status 201. The example sets one single_text field. For every other field type, see Field values. To set a text field, send a string. To set a category field, send the label or the ID of the option: Request { "fields": { "full_name": "Clara Weber", "pipeline_stage": "Contacted" } } See Text field value and Category field value for every format. Requirements: records:edit. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token, a user API key or an automation API key. Errors A request without a value for a required field returns 400 with validation, also for checklist, email, link and phone fields. An empty value, such as [] or null, counts as missing. Query parameters silentboolean Don't send notifications for this change (default: false). hookboolean Run webhooks for this change (default: true). workflowboolean Trigger automations for this change (default: true). reject_unreferencable_relation_targetsboolean Reject the request with 400 if a relation value points to a record that can't be referenced. Otherwise, that reference is dropped (default: false). reject_unresolvable_option_valuesboolean Reject the request with 400 if a category or status value matches no option. Otherwise, a category value is skipped. A status value without a match returns 400 in any case, because a status field can't be empty (default: false). apply_user_timezone_on_date_inputsboolean Read date values without a UTC offset in your timezone instead of UTC (default: false). Retrieve a record​ Use this endpoint to read one record with all its field values. GET/v1/record/{record_id}api.tapeapp.com Request curl https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/1 \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" Response { "record_id": 1, "app_id": 1, "title": "Clara Weber", "created_on": "2022-03-01 12:00:00", "fields": [ { "field_id": 1, "external_id": "full_name", "label": "Full Name", "type": "text", "field_type": "single_text", "values": [ { "value": "Clara Weber" } ] } ] } The response is shortened and shows one single_text field. A record also returns app_record_id (its number in the app), record_url, created_by and its revisions. See The record object. A field without a value isn't in fields. A calculation whose result became empty is the exception: it stays with an empty values array. Don't know a record ID? Open the record in Tape, select ••• (Follow, export and more…), then select Developer. The window shows the Record ID. Or list the records of a database app with Retrieve records for an app. Requirements: records:read. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token, a user API key or an automation API key. Errors A deleted record returns 400 with record_deleted: { "status_code": 400, "endpoint": "/v1/record/17", "error_code": "record_deleted", "error_message": "[RecordDeletedException] Record with ID 17 is deleted!" } Query parameters include_deletedboolean Include records that are deleted but still in a trash you can access (default: false). Update a record​ Use this endpoint to change the field values of a record. PUT/v1/record/{record_id}api.tapeapp.com cURL JSON Request curl -X PUT https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/1 \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ --data '{ "fields": { "full_name": "Andrea Lim" } }' Request { "fields": { "full_name": "Andrea Lim" } } Response { "record_id": 1, "title": "Andrea Lim", "created_on": "2022-03-01 12:00:00", "fields": [ { "field_id": 1, "external_id": "full_name", "label": "Full Name", "type": "text", "field_type": "single_text", "values": [ { "value": "Andrea Lim" } ] } ] } Send only the fields you want to change in the fields object. The response contains the updated record. The example changes one single_text field. For every other field type, see Field values. Requirements: records:edit. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token, a user API key or an automation API key. Query parameters silentboolean Don't send notifications for this change (default: false). hookboolean Run webhooks for this change (default: true). workflowboolean Trigger automations for this change (default: true). reject_unreferencable_relation_targetsboolean Reject the request with 400 if a relation value points to a record that can't be referenced. Otherwise, that reference is dropped (default: false). reject_unresolvable_option_valuesboolean Reject the request with 400 if a category or status value matches no option. Otherwise, a category field is cleared. A status value without a match returns 400 in any case, because a status field can't be empty (default: false). apply_user_timezone_on_date_inputsboolean Read date values without a UTC offset in your timezone instead of UTC (default: false). Delete a record​ Use this endpoint to move a record to the trash. DELETE/v1/record/{record_id}api.tapeapp.com Request curl -X DELETE https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/1 \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" Response { "record_id": 1, "title": "Clara Weber", "created_on": "2022-03-01 12:00:00", "deleted_on": "2022-03-01 13:00:00", "fields": [ { "field_id": 1, "external_id": "full_name", "label": "Full Name", "type": "text", "field_type": "single_text", "values": [ { "value": "Clara Weber" } ] } ] } To delete the record permanently, set skip_trash to true. Requirements: records:edit. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token, a user API key or an automation API key. Errors A record that is already deleted returns 400 with record_deleted: { "status_code": 400, "endpoint": "/v1/record/1", "error_code": "record_deleted", "error_message": "[RecordDeletedException] Record with ID 1 is deleted!" } Query parameters silentboolean Don't send notifications for this change (default: false). hookboolean Run webhooks for this change (default: true). workflowboolean Trigger automations for this change (default: true). skip_trashboolean Delete the record permanently instead of moving it to a trash (default: false). Restore a record​ Use this endpoint to bring a deleted record back from the trash. POST/v1/record/{record_id}/restoreapi.tapeapp.com Request curl -X POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/1/restore \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" Response { "record_id": 1, "title": "Clara Weber", "created_on": "2022-03-01 12:00:00", "fields": [ { "field_id": 1, "external_id": "full_name", "label": "Full Name", "type": "text", "field_type": "single_text", "values": [ { "value": "Clara Weber" } ] } ] } The record must be in a trash you can access. Requirements: records:edit. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token, a user API key or an automation API key. Query parameters silentboolean Don't send notifications for this change (default: false). hookboolean Run webhooks for this change (default: true). Retrieve records for an app​ Use this endpoint to list the records of a database app, page by page. GET/v1/record/app/{app_id}api.tapeapp.com Request curl https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/app/1?limit=2 \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" Response { "total": 2, "cursor": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJibGFiRGVmSWQiOjgsInZhbHVlcyI6WzE1OV0sImV4cCI6MTY1MDYxODc3OH0.iY5TnLSBDGCnFXbStcrLPTmP6MATnS_JKywbvC4tx3g", "records": [ { "record_id": 2, "title": "Clara Weber", "created_on": "2022-03-23 08:48:42", "app": { "app_id": 1, "icon": "event_available", "name": "Contacts", "record_name": "Contact", "workspace_id": 1 }, "fields": [ { "field_id": 1, "external_id": "full_name", "label": "Full Name", "type": "text", "field_type": "single_text", "values": [ { "value": "Clara Weber" } ] } ] }, { "record_id": 1, "title": "Andrea Lim", "created_on": "2022-03-23 08:43:03", "app": { "app_id": 1, "icon": "event_available", "name": "Contacts", "record_name": "Contact", "workspace_id": 1 }, "fields": [ { "field_id": 1, "external_id": "full_name", "label": "Full Name", "type": "text", "field_type": "single_text", "values": [ { "value": "Andrea Lim" } ] } ] } ] } To get the next page, send the returned cursor with your next request. See Pagination. Requirements: records:read. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token, a user API key or an automation API key. Query parameters limitinteger Number of records to return (default: 50). Min 1 Max 500 cursorstring Cursor of the next page. sort_bystring The field ID or the field's slug (returned as external_id in records) to sort by. sort_descboolean Sort in descending order (default: false). Retrieve filtered records for an app​ Use this endpoint to list only the records of a database app that match your filters.
