documents.t: Record read and change the current state of a record. Field value the value format in from, to and fields. Webhook receive the revision_id of every record change. Errors all error codes of the API. Capabilities what records:read allows.

Both endpoints need a credential that belongs to a user: a user API key, a personal access token or an OAuth access token. An automation API key returns a 400: Response { "status_code": 400, "endpoint": "/v1/search", "error_code": "validation", "error_message": "Invalid API key for accessing endpoint '/v1/search' (this endpoint can only be accessed with a user API key)" } Every search uses the permissions of the user behind the credential, and an automation API key has no user. Organization guests get a 401. Tape filters results by permission on every request, for records and apps. Two credentials of two users can return different results, and a different number of results, for the same query. Search never shows anything you can't open in Tape. Missing app or record results? A personal access token or an OAuth access token can search with either the apps:read or the records:read capability. You don't need both. A token with only one of them gets a 200 with only the result type it may see. With records:read alone, you get record results and no app results, even if types asks for both. A token with neither gets a 403. A personal access token restricted to selected workspaces and apps gets a 200 with only the results inside its content access. A user API key has neither restriction. It gets both result types across everything its owner can see.

The base request cost is 10 credits. A search costs 50 credits (5× base) with either endpoint. On the standard budget of 2,000 credits per minute, that's about 40 searches per minute. GET /v1/search 50 (5× base) POST /v1/search 50 (5× base) Every page costs another 50 credits. Prefer a large limit over many small pages.

Every response has the same two keys: resultsarray The matches, in the requested order. Empty when nothing matched. Example value [{ "type": "app", "app": { … } }] cursorstring | null Send it back to get the next page. null means this was the last page. Example value "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..." There is no total, because counting matches would double the cost of every search. Page until cursor is null. Each entry in results has exactly two keys: type, and a payload named after it. Check type to know which payload you have. "app" An app preview, including the name of the workspace it lives in. Payload key app "record" A record preview, without its field values. Payload key record Apps and records come in one results array, mixed by relevance, not in separate lists. To get only one kind, narrow the search with types: ?types=record on GET, or filter.types on POST.

The app payload is the same as an entry from GET /v1/app, including workspace_name. app_idinteger The app ID. Example value 4821 workspace_idinteger The workspace the app lives in. Example value 913 workspace_namestring The workspace's name. Empty string if the workspace is being deleted. Example value "Sales" slugstring The app's URL slug. Example value "customer-onboarding" external_idstring Deprecated. Identical to slug. Example value "customer-onboarding" namestring The app's name. Example value "Customer Onboarding" record_namestring Singular noun for one of the app's records, for example Project. Example value "Onboarding" item_namestring Deprecated. Identical to record_name. Example value "Onboarding" typestring One of database, dashboard, form. Legacy apps without a type report database. Example value "database" descriptionstring Optional. Missing when the app has no description. Example value "Every new customer, start to finish" positionnumber The app's position within its workspace. Fractional: Tape reorders apps by inserting between neighbors, so expect values like 107.125125118059. Example value 3 configobject Legacy-compatible copy of name, item_name and description. Example value { "name": "Customer Onboarding", … }

The record payload is the same as a record preview from GET /v1/record/field/{field_id}/find. record_idinteger The global record ID. Use it to fetch the record. Example value 170471696 app_record_idinteger The record's running number within its database app. Example value 42 record_urlstring Link to the record in Tape. Example value "https://tapeapp.com/acme/record/170471696" app_idinteger The database app the record belongs to. Example value 4821 appobject Preview of the database app, including its workspace. Example value { "app_id": 4821, "name": "Customer Onboarding", … } titlestring The record's computed title. May be missing. Example value "Acme Corp onboarding" created_onstring YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss, in your timezone. Example value "2026-08-03 09:14:22" created_on_utcstring The same moment as created_on, in UTC. Example value "2026-08-03 07:14:22" deleted_onstring Only for a record in the trash. In your timezone. Example value "2026-08-12 10:00:00" deleted_on_utcstring The same moment as deleted_on, in UTC. Example value "2026-08-12 08:00:00" created_byobject | null The user or automation that created the record. Example value { "type": "user", "user_id": 5501, … } current_revisionobject | null The record's latest revision. Example value { "type": "update", "revision": 7, … } initial_revisionobject | null The record's first revision. Example value { "type": "creation", "revision": 0, … } A record preview has no fields, last_modified_on, last_modified_by or comment_count. Fetch the record itself if you need them. Search​ Use this endpoint to search all apps and records you can see. GET/v1/searchNewapi.tapeapp.com Request curl -G https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/search \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \ --data-urlencode "text=onboarding" \ --data-urlencode "limit=20" Response { "results": [ { "type": "app", "app": { "app_id": 4821, "workspace_id": 913, "workspace_name": "Sales", "slug": "customer-onboarding", "external_id": "customer-onboarding", "name": "Customer Onboarding", "record_name": "Onboarding", "item_name": "Onboarding", "type": "database", "description": "Every new customer, start to finish", "position": 3, "config": { "description": "Every new customer, start to finish", "item_name": "Onboarding", "name": "Customer Onboarding" } } }, { "type": "record", "record": { "record_id": 170471696, "app_record_id": 42, "app_id": 4821, "app": { "app_id": 4821, "name": "Customer Onboarding", "record_name": "Onboarding", "workspace_id": 913, "workspace": { "workspace_id": 913, "name": "Sales", "external_id": "sales", "org_id": 77 }, "icon": "event_available", "config": { "name": "Customer Onboarding", "record_name": "Onboarding", "workspace_id": 913, "workspace": { "workspace_id": 913, "name": "Sales", "external_id": "sales", "org_id": 77 }, "icon": "event_available" } }, "title": "Acme Corp onboarding", "created_on": "2026-08-03 09:14:22", "created_on_utc": "2026-08-03 07:14:22", "created_by": { "id": 5501, "user_id": 5501, "org_id": 77, "type": "user", "mail": ["juliet@acme.com"], "email": "juliet@acme.com", "name": "Juliet Adams" }, "current_revision": { "type": "update", "revision": 7, "record_id": 170471696, "created_on": "2026-08-10 16:02:11", "created_by": { "id": 5501, "user_id": 5501, "org_id": 77, "type": "user", "mail": ["juliet@acme.com"], "name": "Juliet Adams" } }, "initial_revision": { "type": "creation", "revision": 0, "record_id": 170471696, "created_on": "2026-08-03 09:14:22", "created_by": { "id": 5501, "user_id": 5501, "org_id": 77, "type": "user", "mail": ["juliet@acme.com"], "name": "Juliet Adams" } } } } ], "cursor": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..." } Send text to start a search, or cursor to continue one. The example returns one app and one record that match "onboarding". To get the next page, send the cursor back (Pagination). General behavior Send exactly one of text or cursor. Neither returns a 400. Both is accepted, but the cursor wins and Tape ignores text. types is comma-separated (?types=app,record). The repeated form ?types=app&types=record doesn't work. An unknown member returns a 400; Tape doesn't drop it. Narrowing types to one kind doesn't enlarge the page. A page still holds at most limit results, but the other kind no longer takes slots in it. URL-encode text. An unencoded & or = cuts your query short without an error. Records shared with you individually, in apps you can't open, match only if you set search_shared_content to true. Requirements: apps:read or records:read. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key. Errors See Errors. Query parameters textstringrequired* The text to search for. Between 1 and 100 characters, and must contain a searchable term. cursorstringrequired* Cursor from a previous response, to get the next page. Send it on its own. limitinteger Results per page. Between 1 and 100. Defaults to 50. typesstring Comma-separated kinds to return: app, record, or app,record. Leave it out to get both. sort_bystring One of ranking_score, created_on, last_modified_on. Defaults to ranking_score. sort_descboolean Order descending. Defaults to true. See Sorting. search_shared_contentboolean Also search records shared with you individually (through a grant on the record or a permission rule that matches you) in apps you can't open. Defaults to false. Records you can already reach through an app come back once. * Exactly one of text or cursor is required. Search with a filter​ Use this endpoint to search with a filter for workspaces, apps, authors or time windows. POST/v1/searchNewapi.tapeapp.com cURL JSON Request curl -X POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/search?limit=20 \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ --data '{ "text": "onboarding", "filter": { "types": ["record"], "workspace_ids": [913, 914], "last_modified_at_from": "2026-08-01 00:00:00" }, "sort_by": "last_modified_on" }' Request { "text": "onboarding", "filter": { "types": ["record"], "workspace_ids": [913, 914], "last_modified_at_from": "2026-08-01 00:00:00" }, "sort_by": "last_modified_on" } This is the same URL and the same search as GET /v1/search, sent as a JSON body. The request creates nothing, so it returns 200, not 201. The example finds records that mention "onboarding" in two workspaces and changed after a fixed moment. The response has the same shape as for GET /v1/search. General behavior The filter only restricts which apps and records count. It doesn't change how text matches. Filter members combine with AND. Each member is optional. A member you leave out means no restriction. The four date bounds are absolute and independent. Send only a _from for "since", only a _to for "until", or both for a closed window. A _from later than its _to returns a 400, not an empty result. So does a date that doesn't exist, such as 2026-02-30. Tape rejects unknown keys. workspaceIds instead of workspace_ids returns a 400, so the API never accepts a filter it doesn't apply. limit is the only query parameter. There is no cursor here. Continue a filtered search with GET /v1/search?cursor=…, because the cursor carries the filter. Set search_shared_content to true to also find records shared with you individually. Requirements: apps:read or records:read. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key. Errors See Errors. Body parameters textstringrequired The text to search for. Between 1 and 100 characters, and must contain a searchable term. filterobject Restrictions on which apps and records count. See below. sort_bystring One of ranking_score, created_on, last_modified_on. Defaults to ranking_score. sort_descboolean Order descending. Defaults to true. Must be a real JSON boolean, not a string. search_shared_contentboolean Also search records shared with you individually (through a grant on the record or a permission rule that matches you) in apps you can't open. Defaults to false. Records you can already reach through an app come back once. filter object typesstring[] Kinds to return: ["app"], ["record"] or both. Must not be empty or contain duplicates. Leave it out to get both. workspace_idsinteger[] Only results in one of these workspaces. At most 100 IDs. app_idsinteger[] Only records of one of these apps, and only these apps themselves. At most 100 IDs. created_by_user_idsinteger[] Only results created by one of these users. At most 100 IDs. created_at_fromstring Only results created at or after this moment. YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss, in your timezone. created_at_tostring Only results created at or before this moment. YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss, in your timezone. last_modified_at_fromstring Only results last changed at or after this moment. YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss, in your timezone. last_modified_at_tostring Only results last changed at or before this moment. YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss, in your timezone. created_at_from_utcstring Same as created_at_from, read as UTC. Wins if you send both. created_at_to_utcstring Same as created_at_to, read as UTC. Wins if you send both. last_modified_at_from_utcstring Same as last_modified_at_from, read as UTC. Wins if you send both. last_modified_at_to_utcstring Same as last_modified_at_to, read as UTC. Wins if you send both. To find these IDs, see Retrieve workspaces, Retrieve all available apps and Retrieve organization users. The unsuffixed bounds use the timezone created_on is returned in, so you can send a value from a result straight back. See Date & timezone. Query parameters limitinteger Results per page. Between 1 and 100. Defaults to 50. Polling for changes​ Use last_modified_at_from for an incremental sync. Send the time of your last successful poll to get only what changed since then. Request { "text": "invoice", "filter": { "types": ["record"], "app_ids": [4821], "last_modified_at_from": "2026-08-11 14:30:00" }, "sort_by": "last_modified_on", "sort_desc": false } Which bound should a sync loop send? Send last_modified_at_from_utc. A local time has no offset, so it's ambiguous when daylight saving time ends. Why do unchanged apps and records drop out? An app or record nobody changed after creating it has no last-modified timestamp, so it drops out as soon as you set either bound. A sync built only on last_modified_at_from never sees new records nobody touched yet. Add a search with created_at_from over the same window, or start with a search without a filter.
Use this endpoint to search all apps and records you can see. GET/v1/searchNewapi.tapeapp.com
Use this endpoint to search with a filter for workspaces, apps, authors or time windows. POST/v1/searchNewapi.tapeapp.com

Use last_modified_at_from for an incremental sync. Send the time of your last successful poll to get only what changed since then. Request { "text": "invoice", "filter": { "types": ["record"], "app_ids": [4821], "last_modified_at_from": "2026-08-11 14:30:00" }, "sort_by": "last_modified_on", "sort_desc": false } Which bound should a sync loop send? Send last_modified_at_from_utc. A local time has no offset, so it's ambiguous when daylight saving time ends. Why do unchanged apps and records drop out? An app or record nobody changed after creating it has no last-modified timestamp, so it drops out as soon as you set either bound. A sync built only on last_modified_at_from never sees new records nobody touched yet. Add a search with created_at_from over the same window, or start with a search without a filter.

Search uses cursor pagination, not limit and offset. To go through all results: Search with either endpoint. Read results. If cursor is null, you're done. Otherwise, call GET /v1/search with only that cursor, and read the next results. Request curl -G https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/search \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \ --data-urlencode "cursor=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..." A cursor is an opaque, signed token. It holds the whole search: text, filter, search_shared_content, sorting and page size. That means: Continue with GET, also for a search you started with POST. POST takes no cursor, because a cursor leaves nothing for a body to add. Send the cursor alone. Tape ignores text, sort_by or sort_desc sent with it. It also ignores limit: a continued search keeps the page size of the search that created the cursor, so all pages have the same size. Don't build, edit or store cursors. They're signed and can expire. Hand them straight back to the API. A page can have fewer entries than limit and still not be the last page. For example, Tape drops a record whose workspace is being deleted instead of failing the request. Trust cursor, not the length of results. Can a search stop before the last page? No, there is no partial mode. Tape rejects a search it can't page with a 400 instead of returning a cut-off first page, so a page with cursor: null means you've seen everything. What matches lists the queries Tape rejects.

ranking_score Relevance, best match first. The default. created_on When the app or record was created. last_modified_on When the app or record was last changed. sort_desc defaults to true: best match first for ranking_score, newest first for the two timestamps. Send false to reverse the order. With ranking_score, that puts the worst matches first, which you rarely want. Results with the same sort value are ordered by ID descending, whatever sort_desc says. This keeps paging stable. The API doesn't return the ranking score. You see relevance only in the order of the array.

Search runs over a text index for each app and each record, not over raw field values. So some behavior differs from a contains filter. Terms match as prefixes, and all terms must match. Each word of the query matches from the start of an indexed word: onboard finds "onboarding", but onboardings doesn't. With several words, a result must match every word. Matching ignores case and knows common stop words. More than titles is indexed. For a record, the index covers text and multi-line text fields, calculations, email, phone, link, location, unique ID, number, category, status, date and relation values, and its comments. A record can match on a comment, even though the result shows no comment data. For an app, the index covers its name, description and blocks. The index cuts long values at 2,000 characters per field. text is required and must contain a searchable term, with 1 to 100 characters. Text made only of punctuation or symbols, such as "..." or "!!!", returns a 400, not an empty result. To narrow by filter alone, search for a term you expect and add the filter. Does a short query return 400? Most organizations can search for any term of one character or more. In a few very large organizations, a query with fewer than four characters returns a 400 that names the minimum. It's an error, not an empty 200, so you can tell "query too short" apart from "nothing matched". Tape checks both rules only when a search starts. Continuing with a cursor doesn't check them again.

Every input problem returns 400. Common causes: Neither text nor cursor on GET /v1/search. text that is empty, longer than 100 characters, or has no searchable term. text shorter than the minimum your organization enforces. limit that isn't an integer, is above 100, or is below 1. sort_by outside the three accepted values. sort_desc that isn't boolean-like on GET, or not a real boolean on POST. types with anything other than app or record, or an empty types list. A date bound that is malformed, doesn't exist (2026-02-30), or a _from later than its _to. A POST body that is missing text, isn't valid JSON, has an unknown key, or has an ID array with more than 100 entries. An automation API key. Response { "status_code": 400, "endpoint": "/v1/search", "error_code": "validation", "error_message": "A search must provide either the \"text\" or the \"cursor\" query parameter (none provided)" } For body schema errors on POST /v1/search, error_code is input_validation, and error_message names the path that failed. Other errors: A request without a credential, or from an organization guest, returns 401. A personal access token or OAuth access token with neither apps:read nor records:read returns 403. Too many searches return 429. See Rate limit credits. A search never returns 404. Anything you can't see is missing from results. See Errors for all error codes.

Apps and records only. Search doesn't return workspaces, users, files, comments, tasks, views or automations, even though comment text feeds the record index. No total. Page until cursor is null. No relevance score and no highlights. You can't tell how well a result matched, or where. No browsing without a search term. Every request needs real text. A filter alone can't produce results. No relative date windows. Date bounds are absolute timestamps you compute yourself. No search in a single field. To match a specific field, use POST /v1/record/filter/app/{app_id}. Previews only. Search results have no field values.

Record fetch the full record of a search result. App fetch the full app of a search result. Filter filter the records of one database app by field. Date & timezone how the API reads date bounds and returns timestamps. Capabilities what apps:read and records:read allow. Request limits how credits and rate limits work.
Use this endpoint to check which user a credential belongs to and what it may do. GET/v1/userapi.tapeapp.com
Use this endpoint to list all users of your organization. GET/v1/org/userapi.tapeapp.com
Use this endpoint to find users of your organization by name. GET/v1/org/user/search?query={query}api.tapeapp.com
Use this endpoint to add a new user to your organization. POST/v1/org/userapi.tapeapp.com
Use this endpoint to send the invitation email to an organization user again. POST/v1/org/user/{user_id}/resend-invitationapi.tapeapp.com
Use this endpoint to send all pending invitation emails of your organization again. POST/v1/org/invitation/resend-pendingapi.tapeapp.com

Organization read the details of your organization. Workspace add users to workspaces. Capabilities what organization:read and organization.members:manage allow. Personal access tokens create a credential with only the capabilities you need.

The five /v1/view/... endpoints need a credential that acts on behalf of a user: a user API key, a personal access token or an OAuth access token. Send it as a bearer token. Permissions depend on that user. An automation API key returns 401 with the message App views can only be accessed with a user API key. The message names only the user API key, but a personal access token or an OAuth access token works too. The list endpoint on the app resource is the one exception. It also accepts an automation API key, subject to view access. Tape checks permissions in two layers against the app the view belongs to: Reading a view needs view access to the app. Creating, updating, deleting or promoting a view needs share access to the app (Can share or Full access), one level above edit access. Edit access to records is not enough to change how everyone in the app sees them.

The base request cost is 10 credits. This resource charges: GET /v1/app/{app_id}/views 50 (5× base) GET /v1/view/{view_id} 20 (2× base) POST /v1/view/app/{app_id} 50 (5× base) PUT /v1/view/{view_id} 50 (5× base) POST /v1/view/{view_id}/default 50 (5× base) DELETE /v1/view/{view_id} 50 (5× base)
The list endpoint returns a preview of each view. Every other endpoint returns the detail object, which adds the full definition, inside a { "view": … } envelope.

idnumber The view ID. Example value 88123 view_idnumber Same as id. Present for consistency with the rest of the API. Example value 88123 namestring | null Name of the view. null for a view that was never named. Example value "Open tickets" app_idnumber The app the view belongs to. Example value 4711 is_defaultboolean Exactly one view per app is true. Example value false layout"table" | "list" | "board" Layout of the view. See Field settings. Example value "table" privateboolean false for every view this API can create. See Limitations. Example value false

Everything in the preview, plus: sort_bynumber | null The field_id the view is sorted by. null means manual record order. Example value 55204 sort_descboolean true for descending. false when there is no sort. Example value false filtersarray The filters of the view, flat and combined with AND. See Filters. Example value [{ "field_id": 55203, … }] fieldsobject Display settings per field, keyed by field_id, for the current layout of the view. See Field settings. Example value { "55207": { "hidden": true } } split_byobject | null The split-by definition, or null. See Split by. Example value null show_progress"none" | "view" | "split_by" | "all" How the view renders progress bars. See Display configuration. Example value "none" tableobject | null Display settings of the table layout, or null unless layout is table. See Display configuration. Example value { "row_height": "medium", "wrap_cells": false } boardobject | null Board grouping, card preview and display settings, or null unless layout is board. See Display configuration. Example value null The fields object contains an entry for every field of the app. Fields without a stored setting appear with their effective default. This makes a GET → PUT round trip faithful: you can send a detail response back to Update a view unchanged. Retrieve a single view​ Use this endpoint to read a view with its full definition. GET/v1/view/{view_id}api.tapeapp.com Request curl https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/view/88123 \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" Response { "view": { "id": 88123, "view_id": 88123, "name": "Open tickets", "app_id": 4711, "is_default": false, "layout": "table", "private": false, "sort_by": 55204, "sort_desc": false, "filters": [ { "field_id": 55203, "field_type": "status", "type": "status", "match_type": "any", "values": [{ "value": 9001 }, { "value": 9002 }] }, { "field_id": 55201, "field_type": "single_text", "type": "text", "match_type": "contains", "values": [{ "value": "urgent" }] } ], "fields": { "55201": { "hidden": false, "width": 320 }, "55203": { "hidden": false, "width": 160 }, "55204": { "hidden": false }, "55207": { "hidden": true } }, "split_by": null, "show_progress": "none", "table": { "row_height": "medium", "wrap_cells": false }, "board": null } } General behavior width appears only for table views, and only for fields with a stored width. table is present only for table views, and board only for board views. The other one is null. Filter operands come back normalized to IDs. A status or category filter written with option names comes back as { "value": <option_id> }. A relation filter comes back as { "value": <record_id> }. Requirements: apps:read, and view access to the app. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key. Create a view​ Use this endpoint to add a view to an app. POST/v1/view/app/{app_id}api.tapeapp.com cURL JSON Request curl -X POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/view/app/4711 \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ --data '{ "name": "Open tickets", "layout": "table", "sort_by": 55204, "sort_desc": false, "filters": [ { "field_id": 55203, "field_type": "status", "type": "status", "match_type": "any", "values": [{ "value": 9001 }, { "value": 9002 }] } ], "fields": { "55201": { "hidden": false, "width": 320 }, "55203": { "hidden": false, "width": 160 }, "55207": { "hidden": true } }, "split_by": { "field_id": 55203, "sorting": "label_asc", "limit": 25 } }' Request { "name": "Open tickets", "layout": "table", "sort_by": 55204, "sort_desc": false, "filters": [ { "field_id": 55203, "field_type": "status", "type": "status", "match_type": "any", "values": [{ "value": 9001 }, { "value": 9002 }] } ], "fields": { "55201": { "hidden": false, "width": 320 }, "55203": { "hidden": false, "width": 160 }, "55207": { "hidden": true } }, "split_by": { "field_id": 55203, "sorting": "label_asc", "limit": 25 } } Send name and layout. Everything else is optional. The new view is never the default view until you promote it. The response is 201 with the { "view": … } envelope and the full detail object. General behavior null is not accepted for any key on create. Only an update can clear a value, because on create there is nothing to clear. An unknown or misspelled key returns 400. Requirements: apps:edit, and share access to the app. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key. Body parameters namestringrequired Max 200 characters; empty string allowed. layout"table" | "list" | "board"required No default, send one. filtersarray Max 100 entries; see Filters. sort_bynumber (field_id) Must be a field of this app. sort_descboolean Defaults to false; ignored without sort_by. fieldsobject keyed by field_id hidden required per entry; see Field settings. split_byobject See Split by. show_progress"none" | "view" | "split_by" | "all" Defaults to none; see Display configuration. tableobject table layout only; see Display configuration. boardobject board layout only; see Display configuration. Update a view​ Use this endpoint to change a view. PUT/v1/view/{view_id}api.tapeapp.com Request { "name": "Open tickets — EMEA" } Every key is optional. Send only what you want to change. Rename only. Everything else stays: Replace the filters and clear the sort: Request { "filters": [ { "field_id": 55201, "field_type": "single_text", "type": "text", "match_type": "starts_with", "values": [{ "value": "EMEA" }] } ], "sort_by": null } Switch the layout and give the list layout its own field settings: Request { "layout": "list", "fields": { "55201": { "hidden": false }, "55203": { "hidden": false }, "55207": { "hidden": true } } } The response is 200 with the { "view": … } envelope after the update. This is a partial update: key omitted the stored value is preserved key present with a value the stored value is replaced key present with null the stored value is cleared (two exceptions below) Collections are replaced in full, never merged. filters: an array replaces the entire filter list. There is no "add one filter" operation. To add a filter, retrieve the view, add it to the array you got back, and send the whole array with PUT. null clears all filters. fields: the map replaces the display settings of the effective layout of the view in full. Fields you leave out lose their stored settings and fall back to the default visibility of the layout. null clears them all. Two exceptions to "null clears": name: null preserves the name. An unnamed view reads as name: null, so the update accepts null to keep a read body PUT-able. There is no way to remove a name: null and "" both mean "leave it alone". width is ignored on layouts other than table. It is tolerated, not rejected. A client that reads a table view, switches layout to "list" and sends the body back doesn't need to strip width from every entry. Read-only keys are accepted and ignored. So that you can send a detail response back as is, the update body also tolerates id, view_id, app_id, is_default, private and sort_property. None of them has any effect. Sending is_default: true in a PUT body? Tape ignores is_default in an update body without an error. Promotion is a separate endpoint (POST /v1/view/{view_id}/default). General behavior The effective layout. If you change layout and send fields in the same request, the map goes to the new layout. The other layouts keep their settings. See Field settings. Display config. You can replace show_progress but never clear it. table and board each replace their config in full when sent. Leaving them out, or sending null, keeps the stored config, so a detail GET with table: null or board: null round-trips unchanged. See Display configuration. Settings the API doesn't expose stay intact: column footer statistics, the lane customization of a board, and the settings of the layouts the view is not in. The one exception is split-by drill-down filters (see Limitations). Sort direction. sort_desc on its own flips the direction of the existing sort and keeps the sort field. sort_by without sort_desc resets the direction to ascending, because sort_by replaces the whole sort. Requirements: apps:edit, and share access to the app. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key. Set the default view​ Use this endpoint to make a view the default view of its app. POST/v1/view/{view_id}/defaultapi.tapeapp.com Request curl -X POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/view/88123/default \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" The request takes no body. The response is 200 with the { "view": … } envelope and is_default: true. The previous default view of the app loses its default flag in the same operation, so the app keeps exactly one default view. General behavior You can't remove the default flag from a view. You can only promote a different one. Promoting a view that is already the default changes nothing and returns 200. Requirements: apps:edit, and share access to the app. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key. Delete a view​ Use this endpoint to delete a view. DELETE/v1/view/{view_id}api.tapeapp.com Request curl -X DELETE https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/view/88123 \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" Response { "view_id": 88123 } The view is soft-deleted, and every endpoint returns 404 for it afterwards. Records are never affected. Requirements: apps:edit, and share access to the app. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key. Errors Deleting the current default view of an app returns 400 with the message The default view of an app cannot be deleted. Set another view as the default first. Promote another view first, then delete it.
Use this endpoint to read a view with its full definition. GET/v1/view/{view_id}api.tapeapp.com
Use this endpoint to add a view to an app. POST/v1/view/app/{app_id}api.tapeapp.com
Use this endpoint to change a view. PUT/v1/view/{view_id}api.tapeapp.com
Use this endpoint to make a view the default view of its app. POST/v1/view/{view_id}/defaultapi.tapeapp.com
Use this endpoint to delete a view. DELETE/v1/view/{view_id}api.tapeapp.com

The filters of a view are a flat array, combined with AND, with no OR, grouping or nesting. The array order is the filter order (there is no position key). A view holds at most 100 filters. A view filter is the same filter object as in POST /v1/record/filter/app/{app_id}, with the same match_type values and operand keys. The filter reference lists every field type and its match types. Every filter entry has at least a field_id, a field_type, a type discriminator and a match_type: { "field_id": 55201, "field_type": "single_text", "type": "text", "match_type": "contains", "values": [{ "value": "urgent" }] } field_id, field_type and match_type are required. type is required in practice: leaving it out returns 400. values is the operand list. Its shape depends on the field type. Leave it out for empty and not_empty. Only field filters are accepted. The metadata filters of the record endpoint (created_at, last_modified_at, app_record_id) are not part of the stored filters of a view. Three facts apply to views only: References must resolve. Tape stores view filters, so an operand that names something invalid returns 400 instead of matching nothing. This applies to a single_relation or multi_relation filter that names a record that doesn't exist (Record(s) with ID … referenced by filters do not exist.), and to a user filter (single_user, multi_user, created_by, last_modified_by, checklist assignee) that names a user outside your organization. Deactivated organization members are still valid operands. include_active_user ("@me") resolves to the owner of the credential you authenticate with. A view saved with it changes per viewer, as in the app: { "field_id": 55208, "field_type": "single_user", "type": "contact", "match_type": "equal", "include_active_user": true } A relative date filter or a checklist filter uses the same operand keys as in the record filter reference: { "field_id": 55204, "field_type": "single_date", "type": "date", "match_type": "within", "relative_date_range_type": "next_week" }

fields is a JSON object keyed by field_id. The key is a string, because JSON object keys are strings. Each value is { "hidden": boolean, "width"?: number }. It applies to one layout at a time. A view stores display settings separately for each layout. fields addresses the current layout, or the new one on a write that also changes layout. Switch from table to list and back, and the original column widths and visibility return. hidden is required on every entry you write, though optional in the response. The default means visible on table and hidden on list and board, so an entry like { "55201": { "width": 200 } } on a list view would silently hide that field. A GET → PUT round trip is safe, because the read returns hidden for every field. width matters only for table. It is in pixels and must be between 100 and 1500. On list and board, it is never returned. On write, it is accepted and ignored there, not rejected. Defaults for fields you don't configure, which is what a GET reports for them: table visible (hidden: false), every field list, board visible for the first field of the app (its title field), hidden for all others Every field_id you name must belong to the app of the view, otherwise the response is 400. You can't set the field order: it follows the field order of the app.

split_by defines how a view groups its records into sections. The API exposes only this definition, never the sections. field_idnumber The field to split by. Required. Must belong to the app of the view. Example value 55203 periodday | weekday | week | month | year | null Bucket size. Only meaningful for date fields. Example value "month" sortinglabel_asc | label_desc | value_asc | value_desc | null Section order. Example value "label_asc" limitnumber 1–100, or null Maximum number of sections (capped at 100). Example value 25 You can split a view by a field of type single_category, multi_category, status, single_user, multi_user, single_relation, multi_relation, single_date, range_date, created_on, last_modified_on or calculation. Any other field type returns 400 (Invalid split_by field: a field of type '…' cannot be split by). On update, "split_by": null removes the split-by. Leaving out the key preserves it. Tape fills in sorting with label_asc for single_category, multi_category and status fields, so a GET can report a sorting you never sent. A GET can also report a period you never sent, for example month for a split by a relation field.
show_progress applies to every layout. table and board are layout-specific: a view in another layout reports them as null. Each config is replaced in full on write.
How the view renders progress bars: none No progress bars (the default on create). view One progress bar for the whole view. split_by One progress bar per split-by section. all Both.

Accepted on create and update only when the effective layout is table, otherwise the response is 400 'table' settings are only valid on a 'table' view. When you send the object, both fields are required. row_height"short" | "medium" | "tall" | "extra_tall" Row height. Example value "medium" wrap_cellsboolean Wrap cell content onto several lines instead of cutting it off. Example value true table config { "row_height": "medium", "wrap_cells": true }

Accepted on create and update only when the effective layout is board, otherwise the response is 400 'board' settings are only valid on a 'board' view. When you send the object, all seven fields are required. group_by_field_idnumber | null The field the board groups into lanes by. Must be a status or single_category field of the app, or null for a board without groups. Example value 55203 card_preview_field_idnumber | null The field shown as the preview image of each card. Must be a single_attachment, multi_attachment or multi_image field of the app, or null for no preview. Example value 55210 card_size"small" | "medium" | "large" Card size. Example value "medium" large_textboolean Show card text in the larger size. Example value false hide_empty_columnsboolean Hide lanes without records. Example value true color_columnsboolean Tint each lane with the color of its group-by option. Example value true fit_preview_imageboolean Scale the preview image to fill the card instead of fitting inside it. Example value false A group_by_field_id of the wrong type returns 400 Invalid board group_by field: a field of type '…' cannot group a board. A card_preview_field_id of the wrong type returns 400 Invalid board card_preview field: a field of type '…' cannot be a card preview. board config { "group_by_field_id": 55203, "card_preview_field_id": 55210, "card_size": "medium", "large_text": false, "hide_empty_columns": true, "color_columns": true, "fit_preview_image": false }

All errors use the standard error envelope of the API. Anything you can't see returns 404, with one message shape whatever the cause: the view ID doesn't exist, the view was deleted, the view is private to another user, you have no view access to the app, or (on create) the app ID doesn't exist or isn't visible to you. A 403 would confirm that an ID exists, so read 404 as "not found or not yours". A write to a view or app you can see, but without share access, returns 403. A request without a credential, with an invalid one or with an automation API key returns 401. See Authentication and permissions. A used-up credit budget returns 429. See Rate limit credits. A request body that isn't acceptable returns 400. Common causes: an unknown or misspelled key anywhere in the body (both request schemas are strict); name longer than 200 characters, or (on create) a missing name or layout; layout not one of table, list or board; more than 100 filters, or a filter without type or with a match_type the field type doesn't support; a fields key that is not a plain non-negative integer, a fields entry without hidden, or a width outside 100–1500; split_by without field_id, a limit outside 1–100, or a split-by field whose type can't be split by; an unknown period, sorting, field_type, match_type, show_progress, row_height or card_size value, or a table or board config without a required field; a field_id (in filters, sort_by, fields, split_by, or a board group_by_field_id or card_preview_field_id) that belongs to a different app; a table config on a view that is not a table view, or a board config on a view that is not a board view; a board group_by_field_id that is not a status or single_category field, or a card_preview_field_id that is not a single_attachment, multi_attachment or multi_image field; a relation filter that names a record that doesn't exist, or a user filter that names a user outside your organization; null for any key on create; the app already holds the maximum of 2000 views; deleting the current default view of the app (The default view of an app cannot be deleted.).

Each of these is a deliberate boundary of version 1: The checklist sort mode is not exposed. A view sorted by a checklist field also stores which part it sorts by (status, title, assignee or due date), and a GET → PUT resets that mode. The sort_property key is reserved for a future release and is accepted and ignored today. Don't round-trip views sorted by a checklist until it ships. Public views only. Every view this API creates is public. Your own private views are readable and writable by ID and report "private": true. Private views of other users return 404, and no private view appears in the list endpoint. No gallery layout. layout is table, list or board. The legacy gallery layout has no public value, and you can't read a view that still uses it through this API. Board lane customization and column statistics are preserved but not exposed. Every update keeps the custom lane order of a board and the column footer statistics of a table, but you can't read or set them here. The other display options are in Display configuration. Any update drops split-by drill-down filters. When a user clicks into a section of a split view, the app writes temporary filters derived from the split-by. GET never reports them, and any PUT removes them. The app creates them again from the split-by, so nothing a user set up is lost. No timestamps. Views have no creation or modification metadata. No order control. The list endpoint returns views in no guaranteed order. No endpoint changes the order of the views of an app.

To recreate a view on another app, read it and then create it. Views reference apps, fields, options, users and records by ID. IDs don't carry over between organizations, so first map every source ID to its target ID. List the views of the source app: GET /v1/app/{source_app_id}/views. For each view, retrieve the full definition: GET /v1/view/{view_id}. Rewrite the body for the target app: sort_by → the target field ID, or drop it; every filters[].field_id → the target field ID, and every operand in values: option IDs, user IDs and record IDs all need a new mapping; the keys of fields → target field IDs; split_by.field_id → the target field ID; board.group_by_field_id and board.card_preview_field_id → the target field IDs; drop id, view_id, app_id, is_default and private. A PUT tolerates them, but POST rejects them; drop every key whose value is null, for example sort_by, split_by or board of a table view. POST rejects null for any key; but if name is null, send a name or "" instead, because name is required on create. Create the view on the target app: POST /v1/view/app/{target_app_id} with name, layout and the rewritten fields, including show_progress and, for a table or board view, its table or board config. If the source view was the default view of its app (is_default: true), promote the new view. You can't set this in the create body. You need share access to the target app, not only edit access. Each app allows at most 2000 views, which a repeated or retried bulk migration can reach. These don't carry over. Set them up again by hand: the default flag (use the promote endpoint); private views (not visible in the source list); the checklist sort mode; column footer statistics and board lane customization; views in the gallery layout (not readable); the field order within a layout (taken from the field order of the target app).

documents.t: Record read the records a view shows. App list the public views of an app. Filter every filter type you can store in a view. Authentication pick the right credential for these endpoints. Capabilities what apps:read and apps:edit allow. Request limits how credits and rate limits work. Errors the error envelope and all error codes.
Use this endpoint to register a URL that receives events of one type from an app. POST/v1/hook/app/{app_id}api.tapeapp.com
Use this endpoint to send a verification code to the URL of a webhook. POST/v1/hook/{hook_id}/verify/requestapi.tapeapp.com
Use this endpoint to activate a webhook with the code it received. POST/v1/hook/{hook_id}/verify/validateapi.tapeapp.com
Use this endpoint to list all webhooks of an app. GET/v1/hook/app/{app_id}api.tapeapp.com
Use this endpoint to delete a webhook by its ID. DELETE/v1/hook/{hook_id}api.tapeapp.com
Every webhook has one type. It decides which events Tape sends to the webhook. To receive several types, create one webhook per type with the same URL.

The record.create type notifies you when someone creates a record in the database app of the webhook. Example of an incoming POST request: JSON HTTP Incoming request { "hook_id": 1, "record_id": 100, "revision_id": 0, "type": "record.create" } Incoming request POST https://webhook.example.org/example-webhook-endpoint Accept application/json, text/plain, */* Content-type application/json;charset=utf-8 User-agent Tape Webhook Content-length 68 Host webhook.example.org Connection close { "hook_id": 1, "record_id": 100, "revision_id": 0, "type": "record.create" }

The record.update type notifies you when someone updates a record in the database app of the webhook. To see which values changed, send revision_id to Retrieve revision delta. Example of an incoming POST request: JSON HTTP Incoming request { "hook_id": 1, "record_id": 100, "revision_id": 1, "type": "record.update" } Incoming request POST https://webhook.example.org/example-webhook-endpoint Accept application/json, text/plain, */* Content-type application/json;charset=utf-8 User-agent Tape Webhook Content-length 68 Host webhook.example.org Connection close { "hook_id": 1, "record_id": 100, "revision_id": 1, "type": "record.update" }

The record.delete type notifies you when someone deletes a record in the database app of the webhook. Example of an incoming POST request: JSON HTTP Incoming request { "hook_id": 1, "record_id": 100, "revision_id": 2, "type": "record.delete" } Incoming request POST https://webhook.example.org/example-webhook-endpoint Accept application/json, text/plain, */* Content-type application/json;charset=utf-8 User-agent Tape Webhook Content-length 68 Host webhook.example.org Connection close { "hook_id": 1, "record_id": 100, "revision_id": 2, "type": "record.delete" }

The record.restore type notifies you when someone restores a record in the database app of the webhook. Example of an incoming POST request: JSON HTTP Incoming request { "hook_id": 1, "record_id": 100, "revision_id": 3, "type": "record.restore" } Incoming request POST https://webhook.example.org/example-webhook-endpoint Accept application/json, text/plain, */* Content-type application/json;charset=utf-8 User-agent Tape Webhook Content-length 69 Host webhook.example.org Connection close { "hook_id": 1, "record_id": 100, "revision_id": 3, "type": "record.restore" }

The comment.create type notifies you when someone comments on a record in the database app of the webhook. Example of an incoming POST request: JSON HTTP Incoming request { "hook_id": 1, "record_id": 100, "comment_id": 500, "type": "comment.create" } Incoming request POST https://webhook.example.org/example-webhook-endpoint Accept application/json, text/plain, */* Content-type application/json;charset=utf-8 User-agent Tape Webhook Content-length 70 Host webhook.example.org Connection close { "hook_id": 1, "record_id": 100, "comment_id": 500, "type": "comment.create" }

The comment.delete type notifies you when someone deletes a comment on a record in the database app of the webhook. Example of an incoming POST request: JSON HTTP Incoming request { "hook_id": 1, "record_id": 100, "comment_id": 500, "type": "comment.delete" } Incoming request POST https://webhook.example.org/example-webhook-endpoint Accept application/json, text/plain, */* Content-type application/json;charset=utf-8 User-agent Tape Webhook Content-length 70 Host webhook.example.org Connection close { "hook_id": 1, "record_id": 100, "comment_id": 500, "type": "comment.delete" }

The app.update type notifies you when someone updates the app of the webhook, for example its fields or settings. Example of an incoming POST request: JSON HTTP Incoming request { "hook_id": 1, "app_id": 1, "type": "app.update" } Incoming request POST https://webhook.example.org/example-webhook-endpoint Accept application/json, text/plain, */* Content-type application/json;charset=utf-8 User-agent Tape Webhook Content-length 44 Host webhook.example.org Connection close { "hook_id": 1, "app_id": 1, "type": "app.update" }

A handler that changes a record in the same app starts a new event, which calls the handler again. Add the query parameter hook=false to every request your handler sends to change records, for example PUT /v1/record/{record_id}?hook=false. It works on create, update, delete, restore and the batch endpoints. Add silent=true to skip notifications, and workflow=false to skip automations.

Respond to every webhook request with a 2xx status code within 5 seconds. Handle heavy processing after you respond. Send an empty body or a short one, such as OK. A long body, such as an HTML page, counts as a failed request. After 100 failed requests in a row, the webhook becomes inactive. Request the verification again to activate it. Tape retries a request briefly after a timeout, a network error, a 429 or a 5xx response. Other status codes fail at once. Tape doesn't follow redirects. Use the final URL, including https. The same event can arrive more than once. Use record_id and revision_id to skip events you already handled. Tape sends webhooks only to ports 80 and 443. https://www.example.org:8080/webhook doesn't work. Use https://www.example.org/webhook.

Tape sends webhook requests at a limited rate. When many events happen at the same time, requests can arrive with a short delay. Can these limits change? Yes. Tape can adjust rate limits to balance demand and reliability, also with different limits per pricing plan.

Working with webhooks: build, verify and test a handler end to end. Record: read the record that an event points to. Record comment: read the comment of a comment.create event. App: read the app after an app.update event. Request limits: the limits of the API itself. Capabilities: what webhooks:manage allows. In the Help Center: App webhooks

Introduction conventions every request follows. Errors handle error responses. Request limits stay within the request budget.

The payload is a JSON object with one property, image_data, which holds a PNG image as a Base64 string. { "image_data": "" }
Automations where scripts run and what they can do. Libraries the Node.js libraries you can use to process the data. Execution types test the automation with a simulation first.

Automations use the same date and time formats as the Tape API: Format Shape Example Datetime YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss 2023-02-01 15:00:00 Date YYYY-MM-DD 2023-02-01 Time HH:mm:ss 15:00:00 These strings have no Z suffix and no offset. The variable name tells you the timezone: a name that ends in _utc holds UTC, the same name without _utc holds the same moment in the timezone of the automation.

Each date field gives you several variables, named after the record name of the app, then field and the field name. Example: an app named Tasks with the record name Task has a date field named Date, with time and without an end date: Variable Description Example value task_field_date_start_time Time in the timezone of the automation. 15:00:00 task_field_date_start_time_utc Same time in UTC. 14:00:00 task_field_date_start_date Date in the timezone of the automation. 2023-02-01 task_field_date_start_date_utc Same date in UTC. Can be a different day than the local date near midnight. 2023-02-01 task_field_date_formatted Date and time as one display string in the timezone of the automation, without seconds. Leaves out the time for a whole day. 2023-02-01 15:00 What about whole-day values? If the date field holds a whole day and no time, both _start_time variables are null. The local date and the _utc date are the same, because Tape doesn't convert a calendar day between timezones. See Calendar days. Use the UTC values when you set or update field values, as Timezones explains.

Use the built-in date_fns library to format dates. Call its format function: date_fns.format(new Date(task_field_date_start_date), 'y') // the year Test your format strings in the interactive date-fns playground.

Automations run in UTC, and Tape's built-in actions handle this for you. Example: an action that copies a date from one record to another keeps the date and time people see in Tape. Take care when you set dates in code, for example in Perform a calculation or Execute a script. The script reads every date string as UTC. Example: a user in Amsterdam (UTC+1 in winter) wants to set a date field to 15:00 local time: var_target_datetime = new Date('2023-02-01 15:00'); The script reads 2023-02-01 15:00 as 15:00 UTC. After the record update, the user sees 16:00 instead of 15:00. Convert the local time to UTC first with zonedTimeToUtc from date_fns_tz, and pass the timezone of the user: var_target_datetime = date_fns_tz.zonedTimeToUtc(new Date('2023-02-01 15:00'), 'Europe/Amsterdam'); Now the record shows 1 February 2023, 15:00 in the user's timezone. To use the timezone of the automation instead, pass current_workflow_timezone. An automation with this conversion looks like this:

Date & timezone: formats, calendar days and UTC values. Libraries: all libraries you can use in scripts, with versions. Automations: execution variables like current_workflow_timezone. Code editor: autocompletion for date_fns and date_fns_tz. In the Help Center: Dates and time zones in automations

The trigger of the automation starts the run. Example: an automation uses the trigger Record created. Someone creates a record in the web app, the mobile app or through the API, and the automation starts. Tape checks the filters first. A run appears only if the record matches the filters of the automation.

Start a run yourself in the automation editor: Open the menu in the automation editor and select Manual run. Under Run on, choose the records: selected records, a view, a number of the most recent records, or all records of the database app. With the trigger Webhook received, choose Last payload or Custom payload instead. Select Start run. Filters apply. Only records that match the filters create a run.

Use a simulation to test an automation without changing data: Open the menu in the automation editor and select Simulated run. Choose the records under Simulate on. Select Start simulation. Filters don't apply in a simulation. Actions that change data in Tape only pretend to run: record updates, record creation, comments and other changes return test data. Requests to other services run for real: Send HTTP request, Send API request and http calls in scripts. Your scripts can check current_workflow_is_simulation. Use it to skip calls to other services, so a simulation can't change data outside Tape. if (!current_workflow_is_simulation) { await http.post('https://hooks.acme.com/deals', { data: { automation_id: current_workflow_id }, headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }, }); } Tape sends data as JSON, but doesn't set the Content-Type header for you. Add it yourself when the receiving service expects application/json. The tape client in Execute a script works the same way. In a simulation, calls that change data, like creating or updating a record, return test data.

Automations: execution variables and where scripts run. Filter values: check that a filter matches only the records you expect. Errors: read failed runs and throw your own errors. Limits and throttling: limits for each run. In the Help Center: Test automations In the Help Center: Run an automation on existing records

All scripts in automations are JavaScript, as in the calculation field. Where you write the script decides what it can do: Where Code Typical use Script filter Synchronous only Decide if the automation continues Perform a calculation action Synchronous only Store a value in a variable Execute a script action Synchronous and asynchronous Call the Tape API or other services

Use synchronous code in script filters and in the Perform a calculation action. The last expression is the result. Each field of the record is a variable, named after the record name of the app, field and the field name, for example task_field_amount. In the examples, some_number_field_value stands for such a variable. The code editor lists the exact names. In a script filter, the result must be true or false: some_number_field_value >= 1000 (some_number_field_value % 2 === 0) && (some_number_field_value < 50) In Perform a calculation, Tape stores the result in a variable: some_number_field_value * 1000 some_number_field_value < 100 ? some_number_field_value : 100; Promises and async/await don't work here. Need them? Use an Execute a script action instead. Need functions or more than one statement? Wrap your code in an immediately invoked function expression (IIFE) and return the result. (function yourFunctionName() { let variable1 = 1337; function yourSubFunctionName1() { return false; } function yourSubFunctionName2() { return true; } // ... more code return yourSubFunctionName1() || yourSubFunctionName2(); })();

Use the Execute a script action to run asynchronous code. Add it in the automation editor with Add action. We recommend async/await over plain promises. Execute a script gives you more APIs, modules and functions. The code editor shows autocompletion and types for all of them. Tape API client​ Use the tape client to call the Tape API. It covers everything the action blocks don't, and gives you more control. const { data, headers } = await tape.Record.get(1234); console.log({ record: data }); data is the record itself, with record_id, title and fields. You don't need to handle authentication. Each run gets its own token, valid for that run. Setting your own key with tape.setApiKey()? Your user API key or personal access token then applies to all following actions too, including action blocks, because they use the same client. HTTP client​ Use the http client to call other services, like the Send a HTTP request action does. const { data, headers } = await http.get('https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts'); console.log({ data }); console.log({ headers }); http also has post, put, patch and delete. Pass request headers in the headers option and a body in data. A JSON response arrives parsed in data, any other response as text. An error status doesn't make the call fail. Check statusCode and throw an error to stop the run: const { data, statusCode } = await http.get('https://api.acme.com/v1/rates?base=EUR', { headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer YOUR_RATES_SERVICE_KEY' }, }); if (statusCode !== 200) { throw new Error(`Rate service returned ${statusCode}`); } var_usd_rate = data.rates.USD; Does the other service only accept known IP addresses? Allow the IP addresses of automations in its firewall.

These actions create variables you can use in all following actions: Perform a calculation Execute a script Send a HTTP request A variable exists only after the action that creates it. There is no block scope. A later action with the same variable name overwrites the value. In Execute a script, assign the value to the variable of the action. Its name is var_ plus its label in lower case, with other characters as _: the label USD rate becomes var_usd_rate. To save the value in a field, use the variable in a later Update the current record action.
Turn on Silent for an action that changes data, and Tape sends no notifications for that change. Use it for large data migrations, so people's inboxes don't fill up.

Every action that changes data has two options: Trigger automations: the change can start other automations. Trigger webhooks: the change sends webhook events. Set both for each action. Example: an action updates a record and Trigger automations is off. Automations with the trigger Record updated don't run for that change. In Execute a script, the tape client has the same options. The code editor shows them in the types.

Tape sets these variables for every run: Variable Description current_workflow_is_simulation true in a simulated run. Use it to skip changes to Tape or other systems. current_workflow_id ID of the automation. Send it to other systems for debugging. current_workflow_name Name of the automation. Send it to other systems for debugging. current_workflow_timezone Timezone of the automation. Set it in the automation editor. current_date_local, current_date_utc Date of the run, in the timezone of the automation or in UTC. current_date_formatted holds it as display text. current_datetime_local, current_datetime_utc Date and time of the run. current_datetime_formatted holds it as display text. current_time_local, current_time_utc Time of the run. current_time_formatted holds it as display text. webhook_payload_parsed, webhook_payload_raw With the trigger Webhook received: the request body as an object, or as raw text. There are more. Some depend on the execution type of the run.

Use console.log to log any variable. The output appears in the logs of the run, under Runs in the automation editor. console.log('initial field value was: ' + task_field_estimation_days_decimal_value) console.log('result of calculation was: ' + var_calculation_result)

Code editor autocompletion and types for your scripts. Libraries date-fns, Lodash and more, ready to use in every script. Date, time & timezones set dates in the right timezone. Connect Google Forms to Tape start an automation from a form webhook. Convert a PDF file to text build a complete automation with a script.

Date, time & timezones use date-fns and date-fns-tz with Tape dates. Code editor autocompletion and types for every library. Automations where scripts run and what they can do. Calculation field libraries the same libraries in calculation fields.

Limit Value What happens Run time 3 minutes The run fails with an error message Actions in one run 1000 The run fails with an error message Memory and CPU Limited The run fails with an error message Parallel async operations Limited Run HTTP calls one after another instead of in parallel Records in one collection action 1000 The collection stops at 1000 records, without an error Emails Shared 24-hour quota of your organization Further emails are refused until the quota renews

Actions that collect records, like collect_app_records and collect_app_view_records, return at most 1000 records. Tape saves a higher limit, limit_enabled: false or a value of 0 or below unchanged. The cap applies only when the run executes. Neither saving nor validating the automation warns you. This cap is separate from the limit of 1000 actions per run.
The actions send_email and collected_records_send_email use the 24-hour email quota of your organization. Once the quota is used up, Tape refuses further emails until the 24-hour window moves on.
Split large jobs into several automations. Avoid heavy computations, for example on large numbers of records. Run HTTP calls one after another.

Tape can throttle an organization that uses a very large number of actions in a short time. Throttling affects the whole organization and delays runs for a while. Tape checks the load regularly and lifts throttling as soon as the load drops below the limit. Until then, waiting runs show the orange status Throttled under Runs in the automation editor and under Automations → Runs.

Execution types: simulate a run before it changes data. Errors: read failed runs and their error messages. Request limits: limits for the Tape API. Automations: where scripts run and what they can do. In the Help Center: Automation limits and throttling

Actions that call the Tape API can fail with these errors. The error message says what went wrong. HTTP status code Code Description Example 400 validation or input_validation Validation error. A required value is missing, like a required field when a record is created or updated, or the text of a comment. 400 record_no_permission or app_no_permission Permission error. The automation has no permission for the step. Also happens when the Author of an action lacks the permission. The code is the error_code of the API response. See Error codes in the API reference for all codes. Calls to other services with the http client don't fail on an error status. Check statusCode in your script, as the HTTP client example shows.

Throw an error in Perform a calculation or Execute a script to stop the run with a failed status. Tape logs your error message. if (some_condition) { throw new Error('Oops, some_condition was true'); } The run stops at this point, and the remaining actions don't run. Use it when an important step fails and continuing makes no sense.

Filter values: why a filter can match more records than you expect. Limits and throttling: limits that make a run fail. Execution types: test with a simulation before a real run. Automations: the tape and http clients and logging. In the Help Center: Common automation errors In the Help Center: Handle errors in automations

Using a field, a variable or an earlier output as the value? If it is empty for one record when the automation runs, the condition is true for every record. Under the default and group, the automation then runs its actions on every record in scope, without an error. Before a bulk action like "update all" or "delete all", this can change your whole dataset and use credits for every record. Getting 400 when you save a filter? Create and update in the Automation API reject a comparison that is empty or of the wrong type, and name the condition: a value whose type doesn't match the field, for example text on a number field an empty comparison value, for example { "type": "text", "text": [] } the wrong number of values The error explains the risk. To check for an empty field on purpose, use is_empty or is_not_empty.
documents.s: An empty filter value matches every record

documents.t: A referenced value is empty. The field, variable or earlier output is empty for this record. It passes the save check, because the reference exists. The value channel doesn't match the field. Tape catches this on save and returns 400. Tape picks the channel from the field type: number and unique ID use number, date fields use date, category, status, relation and user use ids, text uses text. See Match the value type to the field for the channel rules. The automation is older than the check. Automations saved before this check, or in the automation editor, can hold an empty comparison. Create and update don't check existing automations again.
documents.s: How a value ends up empty

documents.t: Check the source first. If the value comes from a reference that can be empty, put the filter or action inside a conditional that checks the source, or set a fallback value. Simulate before you activate. A simulation runs the actions on real records without changing data in Tape, so a search condition inside an action that matches too much shows up early. Requests to other services still go out. A simulation skips the filter of the automation itself. To match every record on purpose, remove the condition, or send filter: null. A filter without conditions runs for every record. An empty top-level group returns 400.

GET /v1/automation/{id}/validate returns valid: true for a condition with an empty comparison value, because the definition is valid. validate checks meaning only: it doesn't run the save checks of create and update, and can't know that a reference becomes empty for some record. validate catches missing references, which is a different problem: filter_variable_missing: the subject of a condition points to a field that no longer exists. filter_value_variable_missing: the value points to a deleted field or variable. Neither code flags an empty comparison. The code filter_value_missing is reserved and no longer raised.
documents.s: Why validate does not flag an empty value

Open the page you want to improve. Select Edit this page at the bottom of the page. Make your change on GitHub and open a pull request. A team member reviews your pull request. Once it's approved and merged, your change goes live with the next publish of the docs.

You need a Tape organization with your apps in it. Moving a whole Podio organization? Use the free Zooli Migration Tool first, as described in Migrate to Tape, then point your code at Tape. The migration gives your apps, fields, and records new IDs. Replace the old IDs and external_id values in your scripts. The Developer view of each app lists the new IDs and slugs. Tape builds each field slug from the field name, with underscores instead of hyphens. A Podio external_id like due-date usually becomes due_date. Send every request to https://api.tapeapp.com. The API sends and receives JSON.

Replace the Podio header Authorization: OAuth2 <token> with a bearer token: curl https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/user \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" Choose the credential that matches your Podio flow: Podio flow Use in Tape Server-side flow, for your own scripts Personal access token. It can also act on a user's behalf when that user creates it Server-side flow, for a product other Tape users connect OAuth with PKCE and a client registered by Tape Client-side flow OAuth with PKCE and a public client registered by Tape, no client secret needed Username and password flow Personal access token App authentication Personal access token with its content access limited to that app and only the capabilities your script needs. Tape has no token per app. Records, comments and revisions show the token's user as the author, so create the token from a dedicated user for the integration. See Attribution

Webhooks verify the same way. Tape sends type hook.verify with a code, and your endpoint calls Validate hook verification. What changes: Tape sends hook.verify right after you create a webhook. Call Request hook verification only if your endpoint missed it. Tape sends a JSON body, not form parameters. Events start with record. instead of item., for example record.create. Tape adds record.restore. The payload carries record_id and revision_id instead of item_id and item_revision_id. Webhooks apply to a whole app. To react to one field, use an automation with a filter. A minimal handler in Node.js: app.post('/tape-webhook', async (req, res) => { const { type, hook_id, code, record_id } = req.body; res.sendStatus(200); if (type === 'hook.verify') { await fetch(`https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/hook/${hook_id}/verify/validate`, { method: 'POST', headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.TAPE_TOKEN}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }, body: JSON.stringify({ code }), }); } if (type === 'record.create') { // For example, create a follow-up task for a new lead. } }); How do you avoid endless loops? Update a record from a webhook with hook=false, as in the Podio API, plus workflow=false, because hook=false doesn't stop automations. Add silent=true to skip notifications. See Avoid endless loops.

A Podio flow or a Globiflow flow becomes an automation in one app. Field references use the field_id, not the external_id. Find the action for each flow step in Coming from Podio. In Podio, the flow starts when … Tape trigger An item is created, updated or deleted record_created, record_updated, record_deleted A comment is added record_comment_or_reply_created A date in a field arrives date_field_arrived A schedule is due periodic A hook or webhook comes in webhook_received Another flow calls it automation_called Someone starts it by hand or with a button Any trigger with manual-run, or a weblink with weblink_clicked

Tape counts credits per minute instead of calls per hour. All credentials of a user share one budget, so more tokens don't add throughput. Each response carries rate limit headers. After a 429, wait the seconds in Retry-After before you retry. See Request limits.

Tape has no client libraries for PHP or Ruby. Call the API over HTTPS from any language. Tasks, status updates, and the activity stream have no Tape endpoints. Use a checklist field and record revisions instead. Tape adds endpoints the Podio API doesn't have: batch create and update, restore a record, the Automation API, and the Tape MCP server.

Automations rebuild your flows in Tape. Automation API manage automations by API. Migrate to Tape move your data first.

You need a Tape account and one record you can view. No account yet? Sign up for Tape. The API sends and receives JSON over HTTPS. Send every request to https://api.tapeapp.com. Tape keeps data as records in database apps. Each record has fields, such as a name or a status. Apps live in workspaces, and workspaces in your organization. New to APIs? Follow the Tape API guide, first steps in the Tape Community. It walks you through three requests in Postman, without writing code.

Select your profile picture, then select Preferences. In the settings window, select Developer (under Features). Under Personal access tokens (PATs), select New token. Name the token, for example "Quickstart". Under Content access, clear All, then select the workspace that holds your record. Under Capabilities, clear All, then select Read records. A capability is one thing the token may do. Select Create token and copy the token. Copy the token now Tape shows the token only once. Store it like a password. Save the token as an environment variable: export TAPE_TOKEN="tape_pat_..." Lost your token? Revoke it under Developer and create a new one.
documents.s: Step 1: Create a personal access token

documents.t: Make a GET request to /v1/record/{record_id}. Send the token as a bearer token in the Authorization header. Use the ID of a record you can view: open the record in Tape, select •••, then select Developer and copy the Record ID. In the examples, replace 123456 with your record ID. cURL JavaScript Python PHP Retrieve a record curl https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/123456 \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" Retrieve a record const response = await fetch("https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/123456", { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.TAPE_TOKEN}` }, }); console.log(JSON.stringify(await response.json(), null, 2)); Retrieve a record import json import os import requests response = requests.get( "https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/123456", headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['TAPE_TOKEN']}"}, ) print(json.dumps(response.json(), indent=2)) Retrieve a record <?php $context = stream_context_create([ 'http' => [ 'method' => 'GET', 'header' => 'Authorization: Bearer ' . getenv('TAPE_TOKEN'), ], ]); $data = file_get_contents('https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/123456', false, $context); echo json_encode(json_decode($data, true), JSON_PRETTY_PRINT); The API returns the record as JSON. Your response has the ID, title and fields of your record. This example shows a contact record: Response { "record_id": 1, "app_id": 1, "title": "Clara Weber", "created_on": "2022-03-01 12:00:00", "fields": [ { "field_id": 1, "external_id": "full_name", "label": "Full Name", "type": "text", "field_type": "single_text", "values": [ { "value": "Clara Weber" } ] } ] } Key fields record_id: the ID of the record. app_id: the ID of the record's database app. You need it to create records there. title: the record title, as shown in Tape. fields: the fields of the record, one entry per field. field_id and external_id: the field's ID and its slug, a readable ID such as full_name. Use either to write values. values: the field values. Their shape depends on the field type. Getting an error? 400 or 401 error Check that TAPE_TOKEN holds the whole token, prefix included. See Authentication errors. 403 error Your token is missing the capability Read records. Create a new token that has it. 404 error Check the record ID, then check that your token's content access includes the record's workspace.

Pick your next task. Each page has a complete request and response. You sign in with your Tape account You can't add capabilities to an existing token. Create a new token for the task. Webhooks and automation runs also need the Admin role in the app's workspace.

Record create, update, delete and filter records. Pagination pages through long lists. Coming from the Podio API map items, spaces and hooks to Tape. Field value the value format of every field type. Personal access tokens limit a token to the apps it needs. Capabilities pick the capabilities for your integration. Authentication compare personal access tokens, user API keys and OAuth.
